Your role 


As Analyst, Revenue Optimization, you are responsible for ensuring that sales targets are met by applying ad inventory management and pricing strategies to optimize TV schedule revenue potential. 


You will be responsible for proactively monitoring inventory utilization and adjusting rates based on market demand. You will also work on media research projects-such as analyzing Numeris data—and provide audience forecasts and rate justifications for seasonal programming schedules. Finally, you will prepare audience tracking tools and performance analyses (both individual and overall) for programs, interpreting the results to adjust revenue generation strategies and forecasts as needed. 


You will design, develop, and optimize dynamic reports and dashboards using IBM Cognos Analytics and Power BI Desktop. Using the Cognos Analytics environment, you will handle the maintenance and evolution of existing reports. 


You contribute to the renewal of direct client agreements by proposing negotiation strategies and commercial offer parameters to the sales teams. 


We are looking for a candidate with the following: 

Qualifications: 


  • University degree in marketing or equivalent 
  • Three (3) or more years of relevant industry experience 

Skills: 


  • Ability to analyze and present data reports in an innovative and accessible way;
  • Ability to extract, analyze, and model data to generate accurate reports and actionable recommendations; 
  • Technical proficiency: Windows (Excel, PowerPoint, Power BI), Google Suite, IBM Cognos Analytics, databases and information systems (Numeris, Infosys, Instar TV/VAM, TAM), and ability to quickly learn internal tools (MRO, Rates & Rating Tool, Onair); 
  • Priority management: Meeting various deadlines, managing multiple projects simultaneously, and demonstrating rigor and attention to detail; 
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills; 
  • Bilingualism is an asset; 
  • Knowledge of the media industry, media buying agencies, and/or experience in the television and digital media is an asset.

CBC North is looking for an Announcer/Operator. Reporting to the Managing Editor, the Announcer/Operator for Nipivut is responsible for finding, researching, preparing and presenting interviews, packaged items, hosting and operating CBC Nunavut/Nunavik’s noon show in Inuktitut and English. Nipivut is a daily radio show focusing on Iqaluit and stories important to Nunavut’s capital city.


Function

Performs a variety of tasks associated with the preparation, production and presentation of programs and program material – for example, announcing, hosting, versioning between English and Inuktitut, writing and operating production equipment. Work is governed by CBC program and journalistic policies and practices but is performed in the unique broadcasting environment of the community station where limited resources dictate the need for versatility, cooperation and teamwork. Activities generally conform to predetermined formats but there is latitude for initiative and independent judgment. Work can involve coordination of the work of others.


Key Tasks:

  • Plans and organizes, or participates in the planning and organizing of programs or program segments, ensures the preparation of material for broadcast and, where a Producer is not assigned, assumes production responsibility.
  • Proposes program ideas, suggests and lines up guests or interviewees, prepares background notes and questions, and conducts interviews on or off air.
  • Writes material for broadcast.
  • Develops and maintains contacts with a variety of sources.
  • Gathers and reports information from various sources.
  • Evaluates information gathered, organizes it and presents it on air in a coherent and understandable form.
  • Edits program material.
  • Interacts with program participants such as guests, interviewees, panelists and/or members of the audience. Uses interviewing skills to elicit pertinent facts and information.
  • Provides narration and linking continuity between program segments.
  • Describes actualities such as music programs, parades and sporting or other special events.
  • Reads newscasts, news bulletins, weather forecasts and other survival information.
  • Ensures the proper operating condition of equipment by making the necessary checks.
  • Ensures that program audio mixes achieve optimum results.
  • In case of technical failure, makes emergency substitutions or repairs to maintain clear and continuous service; ensures appropriate follow-up.

As required, performs the following tasks:

  • Participate in community relations activities to promote the CBC.
  • Direct a program or program segment in studio or at a remote location.
  • Maintain an appropriate level of communication with members of the audience.
  • Archive programs and program scripts and lineups.
  • Perform incidental technical functions necessary to ensure the smooth and continuous functioning of the station.


The successful candidate will have:

  • A minimum of a high school education or an acceptable combination of education and work experience.  Previous on-air experience in radio or television would be an asset.
  • Excellent on-air presentation skills.  
  • Excellent Inuktitut skills.
  • Good writing, and interviewing skills.
  • A critical thinker with strong editorial judgment.
  • A strong understanding of Inuit and northern issues.
  • Good computer skills and willingness to maintain Social Media networks using external platforms like Facebook, Twitter etc.
  • Mature, positive attitude and an excellent ability to contribute to a team environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to perform at a high level in a high pressure, tight deadline environment.

Your Role


Radio-Canada Saskatchewan is looking for an energetic and forward-thinking Associate Producer to take on a vital support role. You will be assigned primarily to on-air presentation for the radio morning show Point du jour, produced at the Regina Broadcast Centre. The shift is Monday to Friday, 5:00 a.m. to 1:45 p.m.


You will also be assigned to gather, write and present program material for all our media platforms. You will participate in the production, direction and/or post-production of a program and/or program segment. Guidance and direction are regularly available from one or more producers, but there is latitude for initiative and independent judgment.


Work must comply with CBC/Radio-Canada journalistic and program policies, standards and practices. Work can involve co-ordination of the activities of others, and close co-operation with the program unit is essential.


Key Tasks:

  • Operate the studio board during live programming and pre-taped segments, direct/time the program, and provide control room support for on-air staff.
  • Contribute ideas for program content; help determine program objectives.
  • Secure studios, lines, uplinks, remotes and other technical and production resources required for the program.
  • Assist in developing program content (includes writing, researching and/or editing). Prepare scripts, ensuring adherence to the style and format of the program.
  • Organize appearances of interviewees, creative contributors and other guests on the program; develop background, intros and lines of questioning; conduct or arrange for any necessary research; and ensure briefing of hosts. Maintain contact files.
  • Participate in the evaluation of all aspects of the production.
  • Perform the following tasks as required:
  • Select music, sound effects and/or actuality.
  • Produce program elements.
  • Direct a program, either live or pre-packaged, in studio or at a remote location.
  • Assign, direct and co-ordinate the work of other personnel working on a project for which the Producer is responsible.
  • Edit and mix, or direct the editing and mixing of, audio and/or visual elements.
  • Write continuity, edit text, and edit and prepare voicemail for broadcast or publication.
  • Log programs and music in appropriate information systems.
  • Assemble, code, digitize, and index sound and digital images for a website and social platforms using appropriate technologies.
  • Assist in maintaining manageable, appropriate audience engagement and communication aligned with the style and nature of the program.
  • Perform other production or administrative tasks associated with the smooth functioning of the newsroom, program unit or station.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.


What You Bring:

  • University degree or equivalent.
  • Combination of education and experience equivalent to a university degree plus three (3) years’ practical, relevant experience, or a college diploma and five (5) years’ practical, relevant experience.
  • Bilingual mandatory (English/French).
  • Ability to thrive in a high-pressure, tight-deadline environment.
  • Ability to collaborate and work as part of a team.
  • Resourceful, proactive mindset.
  • Proficiency with digital and broadcast IT tools.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a strong team-player orientation. 
  • Comfort with the demands and needs of television, radio and digital news production.
  • Strong organizational skills, with the ability to handle a variety of functions quickly and efficiently.
  • Ability to solve problems independently and in team settings (with an openness to new ideas and approaches).
  • Ability to work flexible hours and overtime.
  • Understanding of the structure and workflow at Radio-Canada, and the ability to build and maintain strong relationships with internal counterparts.
  • Strong knowledge of Saskatchewan and the issues facing the Fransaskois community.

Familiarity with in-house production tools (Dalet, iNews, Avid).

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we all have a story to tell. What’s yours?

 

If you share our passion for Canadian storytelling, and you wish to help us engage with individuals and communities across our various digital platforms, this is where you’ll want to be!

 

Every day, you will have an opportunity to shape the way in which Canadians see themselves reflected in our digital services. Your work will have a direct impact on how millions of Canadians from various communities connect with our products, with one another, and with the diverse voices that make our country so unique.

 

You will have the opportunity to play a part in enlightening and entertaining Canadians through our innovative work in building the mediums that deliver our content. We are an innovative hub, where the talented professionals we work with are respected and valued for their contributions. Our product teams are vibrant and our work culture strives to achieve the highest standards of diversity and inclusion. We believe that hiring people with different career paths and backgrounds is fundamental in our shared success and in building healthy and highly performant teams.

 

When you join our mission, you are not only shaping the vision of CBC/Radio-Canada, but the future of our country.

 

We know that commitment to equity, inclusion and diversity is essential to creating content that mirrors and resonates with the rich and evolving makeup of our country.  We’re also committed to reaching out and connecting with our audience on multiple platforms this includes creating virtual places where communities can come together.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why is this role important?

 

You will be an important element of our over-the-top platform team. As such, working closely with the product owners, architects and technical managers, your role is to ensure the smooth execution of product front-end development and coordinate the technical work required to deliver requested features, while adhering to the standards and practices agreed to by the development management team.

 

The team you will be part of is in charge of an harmonized product, powering CBC Gem and ICI TOU.TV.

 

Perks you can look forward to:

  • Flexible work schedules, allowing you to prioritize yourself, your family and your work
  • Work from home opportunities
  • Competitive total rewards package
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups
  • Pair programming and mentorship opportunities, where you can learn from the best in the industry and help coach new talent
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity
  • An environment which favours experimentation and an iterative approach in order to achieve the highest form of technical innovation.

 

Your responsibilities:

  • Design and/or modify reusable components for Radio-Canada's digital platforms; such as the audio/video player.
  • Ensure compliance with standards and control the quality of the product throughout the project's execution.
  • Stay informed of new trends in the various fields of digital development.
  • By being proactive, propose solutions to the challenges encountered.
  • Participate in Agile Scrum activities designed to review ongoing production projects in order to make necessary corrections and adjustments, or completed projects to measure their results.
  • Participate in the development of user stories for our various products.
  • Ensure the good performance of developed applications to handle high loads.
  • Participate in sprint planning, retrospectives, and application deployments.
  • Participate in code reviews and solution deployments.

We are looking for a candidate matching the following profile:

  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • At least 3 years of experience in software development.
  • Proficiency in C#, ASP.NET Core and WebAPI.
  • Excellent grasp of REST API principles.
  • Knowledge of Git.
  • Knowledge of SQL Server, Entity Framework.
  • Knowledge of Redis is an asset.
  • Knowledge of JavaScript/TypeScript is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Azure Data Lake is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Docker, Kubernetes, and Azure cloud is an asset.
  • Knowledge of audio-video broadcasting on the web (streaming) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of other programming languages is an asset.
  • Knowledge of design patterns is an asset.
  • Good general knowledge and strong intellectual curiosity (to acquire and develop new knowledge and skills).
  • Critical thinking (to question and propose new ideas).
  • A keen interest in the major trends and challenges of the digital world.
  • Meticulousness, independence, and resourcefulness.
  • Excellent stress management and priority setting.
  • Analytical and conceptual thinking skills.
  • Flexibility, initiative, and dynamism.
  • Ability to work in a team, excellent communicator.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) spoken and written is mandatory.

 

Please note that due to the nature of the mandates and responsibilities of this role, all candidates will be required to work in a multilingual environment, where business will be conducted in both official languages (English and French). Therefore, employees working in this role will be expected to make the required efforts and adjustments to navigate this multilingual environment in a respectful manner for all.

CBC News is proud to offer its winter internship to aspiring journalists from across the country, a six-week, in-person program that provides valuable hands-on experience in multiplatform news environments. 


Please note that we can only consider your application if you have been recommended by the journalism coordinator at your university or college. Please do not apply unless you have been recommended by your school and have received an invitation from CBC to apply to our program.


We are currently accepting applications for our winter 2027 session:


Winter Session: Monday January 11 to Friday February 19, 2027


The deadline for submitting your application is Friday October 23, 2026, at 11:59 pm ET.


About the program:

  • Our six-week full-time program offers students hands-on experience in multiplatform news environments. 
  • Our placements are located at the CBC Toronto Broadcast Centre but include the possibility of working at other local newsroom locations in Ontario. 
  • Interns parallel the programs they're assigned to. Most work is in person, Monday to Friday. However, some placements are hybrid home-office arrangements. Some roles require weekend shifts and/or early morning or late afternoon/evening work. 
  • Internships are unpaid. Interns are responsible for accommodation and travel. 
  • If successful, a student’s placement area will depend on the interests they express to us, our assessment of their strengths and the ability of our programs/departments to host interns.

Note: Here is a list of typical placement areas however they're subject to availability and vary throughout the year. 

 

Program criteria:

  • You must be enrolled in a journalism program recognized by CBC.
  • Internship must be a requirement of your program. 
  • We will not consider any student application unless recommended by your school’s coordinator.
  • Students must not have already interned in an editorial role at the CBC.
  • Students must be in—or about to enter—their final year of study at the time of the internship.
  • Students must be available full-time. We are unable to accommodate class/work schedules. 
  • Applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada at the time of application and throughout the internship period. Proof of work authorization may be required.
  • You and your college or university must ensure you are covered for all eligible insurance costs through the Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities.

Note: Standard recruitment at CBC includes a mandatory background check for selected students prior to receiving an official internship offer. There is no charge.  

 

Please note that CBC values equal opportunity and nurtures an inclusive workplace where individual differences are not only recognized and valued, but also extend to and pervade all the services we provide as Canada's public broadcaster. For more information, visit the Diversity and Inclusion section of our website.


Should you have workplace accessibility or accommodation needs, please inform us as soon as possible. 


What are the application requirements?


To be eligible for consideration, candidates must ensure they provide a single PDF that consists of the follow items:

  • A one-page cover letter that explains what you bring to the program
  • A one-page resume 
  • Portfolio:  Please provide three examples of your journalism work. If you've worked in more than one medium, make sure your examples reflect that range (ie. text, audio, video, interactive, etc). For each link, please write one sentence about why you chose to submit this piece. Please provide links to your work, not the actual files. Group projects are acceptable; however, you MUST clearly describe your own contribution.

Employment during internship:


While we do not want interns to overextend themselves during their internship, we are sensitive to the importance of income derived from part-time jobs. If the work is journalistic in nature, we will ask interns for details to ensure that there is no conflict of interest while at the CBC. 


Note:


Although proficiency in technical skills is essential to the work of journalists, this is not a technical internship. This is an editorial internship which is not designed for people who are interested in careers in directing, switching, lighting, editing and camera work.


If your school has nominated you but you decide NOT to submit an application, please notify us.


Thank you for your interest, time and effort. We look forward to reviewing your application package!

job.description:

Status of Employment:

Position Language Requirement:

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance. 
 
Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

2026-12-18 11:59 PM

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

 

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This role requires full-time on-site presence.

 

Your Role


Coordinate and execute various tasks for On- Air programs, as well as ensure the continuity of acquisition, feed and communication resources for CBC/Radio-Canada networks and external clients, including various regions. Distribute the signals of programs and program segments, ensuring quality control.

 

Key Tasks

  • Insert station IDs, spots, promos and sponsored graphics into programs and breaks, ensuring seamless co-ordination with all other scheduled continuity elements.
  • Verify the availability of all broadcast assets; proactively manage workflows to ensure that all elements (including schedules, programs, spots, promos, keys, voice-overs and closed-captioning files) are present and compliant prior to air.
  • Screen and approve spots and promos prior to ingesting them into the server; reject non-compliant assets and initiate corrective action.
  • During live broadcasts, verify all commercial content (such as names, billboards and foreground voices) and co-ordinate the integration of commercial pods and other elements jointly with the program production team.
  • Check and ensure the accuracy of program elements slated for broadcast against cue sheets and the schedule; view the program and make necessary corrections.
  • Check audio/video, captioning and communications signals for programs or program elements across the entire Radio-Canada distribution system, including those from outside distribution companies (e.g., cable operators, satellite signal providers), along with all technical elements (e.g., VTRs, servers, external links); make corrections if they are not compliant with standards.
  • Integrate cue sheets and schedule, resolve and correct rejected elements, then complete and finalize the schedule, coding the program elements using management software. Organize the sequencing and allocation of equipment according to the constraints specific to each element making up the program.
  • Set up, load, test, position, install and operate the VTRs, servers (e.g., audio-video, captioning) and other technical equipment (e.g., broadcast graphics, digital delay), ensuring everything is clean, secure and in good working order.
  • Ensure the accuracy of the broadcast schedule and, if necessary, correct it by shortening or lengthening programs; depending on the circumstances or in the event of a fault, rework it, replacing certain items or programs.
  • In emergency situations, evaluate and manage the broadcast of news flashes, short-form special programing, PSAs and news crawls in accordance with established protocols and programming tone, and be responsible for rescheduling or pre-empting commercials and promos and notifying all affected network affiliates.
  • Notify management, French network regional and affiliate stations, as well as Production, Sales and Communications, of any changes or relevant information regarding broadcasts.

  • Carry out, as needed, all or part of the duties of another job classification within an equivalent or lower salary group, as well as other related duties.

Copy Editor CBC BC Interior (Kelowna, Kamloops or Prince George locations)



This is a full-time permanent position scheduled for 11:00 am Sunday - Thursday.  


That schedule is subject to change based on operational needs.


We are looking to hire an experienced copy editor to join our team and support journalism across British Columbia and our Local Service Expansion reporters in parts of western Canada.  


Reporting to the executive producer and coordinating producer, you will be responsible for the timely editing and delivery of a range of news stories — from breaking news to long-form features — to CBC’s digital and social platforms, while ensuring accuracy and balance. 


The successful candidate will demonstrate an understanding and awareness of issues and events particular to British Columbia, and will have strong ties to, and a deep understanding of, under-represented communities and equity-deserving groups across the province. 


The job involves handling text copy, video, images and interactive features for a digital audience, as well as contributing to CBC’s live story pages. You must be familiar with and understand visual storytelling tools and techniques, and able to adapt to evolving technologies.


You must be a self-starter, detail-oriented and comfortable taking on responsibilities and making independent editorial decisions.


You care about the people you work with and have a deep appreciation for different perspectives, opinions, and experiences. You live and promote the values of diversity, inclusion and respectful work culture. 


Duties:

  • Editing daily news copy, features, long-form stories, social media copy, and text for video and graphics.
  • Editing newsletters for the Local Service Expansion bureaus. 
  • Working urgently to cover breaking news.
  • Ensuring inclusive language and framing in stories that accurately represent the diverse experiences of British Columbians.
  • Ensuring stories are balanced and conform to CBC’s in-house style and Journalistic Standards and Practices.
  • Curating story packaging — including photos, video, graphics and embeds.
  • Ensuring the digital news lineup reflects the top stories and news priorities of the day, through an audience-first lens.
  • Talking through story ideas and assignments with writers and producers while ensuring that perspectives from diverse and under-represented communities are considered.
  • Identifying what a story lacks and clearly articulating to writers how to improve storytelling and packaging. 

Your profile: 

  • Strong news judgement and critical thinking.
  • Knowledge of legal and ethical issues related to journalism.
  • Experience and proven ability to package online news stories in compelling and innovative ways.
  • Ability to manage large volumes of fast-moving information.
  • Strong headline writer. 
  • Good communication skills.
  • Flexibility with work hours on weekdays and weekends.
  • University degree or equivalent.
  • Minimum of three years’ experience editing at a print or digital publication preferred.

 

Assets:

  • Use of content management systems
  • Canadian Press style
  • Active user of social media platforms and creator of social content.




Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

CBC Prince Edward Island is looking for a host for its Island Morning radio program.  

In this role, you will be the voice that sets the news agenda for listeners across P.E.I., helping them make sense of their world as they get up each morning.

You are an insatiably curious early-morning storyteller with a passion for drawing emotion and stories out of interview guests. You are equally comfortable holding a politician accountable as you are chatting with children, and you know when to put people at ease and when to challenge them. 

You understand that audiences want to be both entertained and informed as they start their day, and you realize the importance of making audiences feel welcome and part of a community. You know that using a full range of tone, including humour, is key to strong radio current affairs programming.

You have a sense of adventure, an eclectic range of interests and a keen desire to meet new people, explore our communities, and learn other perspectives. You are passionate about championing stories from P.E.I.’s under-represented communities, and you love meeting listeners where they live through in-person public appearances and at remotes.

An experienced journalist and a keen observer, you must be able to quickly analyze a broad range of issues and thrive in the fast-paced, high-pressure world of live, local radio. You have a strong grasp of our province’s political landscape and its resource-driven economy, and you understand how these issues affect the day-to-day lives of the people who live here.

As a member of the Morning team, it’s clear you care about your colleagues. You act as a team unifier and collaborator, and are always looking for creative solutions to challenges.

This role requires full time on site presence. 

Your responsibilities:

  • Pitch and produce original stories that deepen Island Morning’s community connections, elevate a range of voices and reflect the day’s top local news.

  • Conduct research and interviews, gather audio, write radio scripts, and package and present content for all platforms including audio, video and digital. 

  • Host Island Morning live on air between 6:00-8:30 a.m. weekdays, conducting interviews on a wide variety of current events.

  • Interact extemporaneously with program participants such as guests, reporters, experts and members of the audience.

  • Participate in public relations or community outreach activities to promote Island Morning and CBC, with a focus on growing new audiences and building community connections.

Your profile:

  • An engaging, curious, and spontaneous on-air personality, with a wide range of genuine interests, knowledge and insight, reflecting curiosity in many current affairs topics, and an ability to make them relevant to existing and new audiences.

  • Strong journalistic skills, demonstrated through original story ideas, live interviewing, innovative storytelling, and writing and vetting abilities.

  • Excellent critical thinking skills, including knowledge of and familiarity with CBC Journalistic Standards as well as the legal and ethical issues related to journalism.

  • Ability to react quickly to changing circumstances and breaking news; comfortable going off-script when needed.

  • Familiarity with digital and social storytelling, including podcasting, and a willingness to learn and tackle new tasks across all CBC platforms (TV, radio, digital).

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across teams and locations.

  • A proven work ethic and a positive team-first attitude. 

  • A strong desire to live and promote the values of diversity and an inclusive and respectful work culture.

  • A passion for public outreach and an enthusiastic ambassador of public broadcasting and the program.

  • Ability to work a variety of shifts including early starts, late finishes and weekends.

  • University degree or equivalent in a related field, with a minimum of five years of relevant or comparable experience.

We want to hear what you sound like! Please include a link to samples of your on-air work in your cover letter.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media.

 

The Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) team is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation's technologies and infrastructure, enabling the creation and continued delivery of quality content across all platforms. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people, and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology—not just in Canada, but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force and we are the team making it happen.

 

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines and operational needs.

 

Your Role

 

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Strategic Alignment and Engagement, the Junior Specialist plays a pivotal role in nurturing corporate culture and enhancing the employee experience within CBC/Radio-Canada’s Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) division.

 

As a key member of the People & Engagement team, you will act as a champion for internal engagement initiatives. You will collaborate with clients and partners to deliver ad hoc communications support while co-ordinating and rolling out events and initiatives that drive active participation, team cohesion and a sense of community. In this role, you will leverage your interpersonal strengths, writing flair and graphic design talent to build meaningful relationships and produce compelling copy and visual content.

 

We are seeking a versatile communicator with a keen interest in technology and employee engagement. You bring exceptional bilingual writing abilities (French and English), sharp analytical thinking and the skill to quickly distil complex technical concepts into clear, captivating messaging and eye-catching visual designs.

 

Outstanding interpersonal skills will enable you to thrive as an advocate for team culture and create the type of engaging content required for the role.

 

The position can be based in Toronto or Montreal.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Gather content for, design and share internal communications materials with the goal of building a unified, engaging culture within T&I.
  • Create and maintain communication channels and platforms targeting T&I, including the newsletter, staff portal and iO pages.
  • Provide logistical support for internal events designed to strengthen the workplace culture at T&I.
  • Connect with T&I team members to boost engagement and uncover inspiring stories that build pride and belonging.
  • Actively support the development and rollout of engagement programs and campaigns that inspire employee participation.
  • Apply graphic design expertise to create dynamic, high-impact visuals tailored to various communication channels.
  • Stay aligned with CBC/Radio-Canada and T&I strategic priorities — specifically regarding official languages, equity, diversity and inclusion — to ensure consistent, relevant and effective messaging.
  • Help define T&I’s voice, culture and brand to ensure clear recognition and strong resonance among staff.
  • Actively contribute to co-ordinating and promoting corporate and T&I initiatives.
  • Adhere to and promote organizational content accessibility standards.

 

What You Bring

 

Skills and Qualifications

  • University degree in communications, marketing, public relations or journalism an asset.
  • Experience in event co-ordination and content writing.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in both official languages (English and French).
  • Ability to work well in a team environment and collaborate effectively with others.
  • High degree of autonomy and self-motivation.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with a proven ability to respond to multiple urgent requests and meet deadlines.
  • Ability to clearly demonstrate flexibility and agility when faced with changing priorities.
  • Strong graphic design skills and proficiency with visual design software (such as the Adobe Creative Cloud suite) an asset.
  • Familiarity with content management systems (CMSs), Mailchimp and RGE Studio an asset.

Program Manager


This is a permanent full-time role, based in Regina.

CBC Saskatchewan is looking for a program manager to help lead CBC Saskatchewan at a pivotal time in the province’s history. You will report to the Director, Journalism and work alongside CBC Saskatchewan’s leadership team to execute the station’s editorial vision on our programs.


As the program manager, you will lead all programming on video, audio and digital platforms. You will be a key point person, along with the Managing Editor, in JSP guidance and programming direction. You will work closely with our communications team to ensure program and community outreach align.


You will be a champion of audience growth. You will bring audience metrics and data to our program teams. And you will work relentlessly to help connect our storytelling with the community. 


You will work with a great team, and will be a key supporter of its ongoing development.


You will be a great leader, and an even better teammate.


Main responsibilities:


  • Oversee CBC Saskatchewan programming
  • Work within the leadership team to execute an editorial vision across CBC digital, radio, and visuals that balances immediate breaking news with enterprise storytelling.
  • Ensure our storytelling adheres to CBC’s journalistic standards and practices, ensuring all content is fair, balanced, and accurate. 
  • Ensure our coverage reflects the true diversity of Saskatchewan, building trust with new audiences through inclusive storytelling.
  • Oversees the station’s community outreach strategy
  • Ensure program content is strategically leveraged, adapted, and shared across CBC Saskatchewan’s digital and television platforms to maximize impact.
  • Drive the CBC Saskatchewan hiring strategy.
  • Oversee the onboarding of new editorial staff, ensuring deep familiarity with CBC’s Journalistic Policy, technical tools, and local newsroom culture.
  • Oversee performance management of all programs, including mentorship and training and development.
  • Act as the primary local authority on CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices (JSP), when Managing Editor is unavailable, ensuring all stories meet the core tenets of accuracy, fairness, balance, and integrity.
  • Provide real-time counsel on complex journalistic questions, including legal risks (defamation, publication bans), ethical dilemmas, and sensitive interviews.
  • Serve as the final escalation point in the newsroom for breaking, highly sensitive, or controversial local stories, coordinating with CBC Legal and network leadership when necessary.
  • Help navigate audience complaints or corrections transparently, upholding CBC’s accountability to the public


Experience Required

  • Minimum of 10 years' related experience, including experience leading in a newsroom 
  • A track record of guiding complex journalistic decision making
  • Experience managing staff and resources within budgetary constraints
  • Experience leading the application of journalistic standards and practices in a daily newsroom setting
  • An ongoing interest in and understanding of media trends as they apply to a multiplatform newsroom
  • Experience in setting clear objectives and goals, and then to deliver on them 
  • Proven ability to make decisions rapidly and frequently within tight deadlines

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.


Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.


A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.


This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.


Your role


Reporting to the Value Management Delivery Office (VMDO), the Project/Program Portfolio Manager (Real Estate Projects) plays a pivotal matrix leadership role. Operating without direct hierarchical authority, you will act as the strategic and tactical orchestrator of the Corporation's real estate transformation. Your mission is to oversee the entire investment portfolio (Capex/Opex), ensuring rigorous alignment with corporate objectives, resource optimization, and standardized risk management.


As the key facilitator for the instances of the new real estate governance model, you will bridge the gap between technical teams, operations, service provider, and senior executive leadership.


You are seen as someone who:

  • Fosters and maintains alignment among diverse stakeholders.
  • Balances strategic thinking with execution and delivery.
  • Demonstrates and encourages continuous improvement and value creation.
  • Effectively reports out to and works with other areas including Finance and Executive Governance.

The opportunity


CBC/Radio-Canada is implementing a rigorous portfolio approach to its real estate assets to achieve critical strategic objectives.  This role offers the opportunity to be a driving force in ensuring that financed real estate projects align with the corporation's strategic goals, while maximizing the efficiency of financial resources. You will champion transparency, resource optimization, and risk management while supporting critical executive reporting.


Primary Duties and Responsibilities


Governance, Facilitation, and Strategic Alignment

  • Committee Leadership: Act as the primary leader and facilitator for the Steering Committee (SteerCo) and the operational Portfolio Sync instance. Actively support the executive Governance Committee.
  • Strategic Alignment (100% Target): Deploy and maintain an evaluation framework to ensure that 100% of funded real estate projects directly align with corporate priorities.
  • Arbitrage and Continuity: Structure prioritization and trade-off files throughout the year to ensure dynamic allocation of financial and human resources during monthly and quarterly reviews.

Capacity Management and Resource Optimization

  • Integrated Roadmap Planning: Maintain global and centralized visibility of the short-, medium-, and long-term real estate roadmap (annual and 5-year plans).
  • Demand/Capacity Balancing: Continuously assess internal and external team workloads against capacity envelopes to proactively anticipate bottlenecks and plan future requirements effectively.
  • Interdependency Management: Cross-analyze critical dependencies across different groups (Facilities Planning, Asset Management, Engineering, Leasing, Major Construction Projects) to eliminate operational conflicts.

Delivery and Synchronization

  • Dashboards and Visibility: Develop and maintain Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and visual tracking tools to provide stakeholders with real-time visibility into costs, timelines, and expected benefits.
  • Data Integrity: Ensure the collection, centralization, and modeling of operational and financial portfolio data to support informed, value-driven decision-making.
  • Escalation process: Identify and resolve escalated tactical issues impeding project delivery, preparing files for the Governance Committee when required. Identify risk or issues that require escalation to the SteerCo for resolution.

Standardized Risk Management and Partner Tracking

  • Risk Management Process: Based on a risk-wise approach, drive informed risk management strategies, tracking action plans to reduce overall portfolio exposure.
  • Partner Performance Monitoring: Monitor the tactical and operational performance of PDS service provider, ensuring adherence to CBC/Radio-Canada’s quality control and compliance standards.

We are looking for a candidate with the following:

  • Seven (7) or more years of experience in project/program management, with at least three (3) years acting in a portfolio management or senior leadership role on complex initiatives.
  • Experience delivering large Real Estate projects and a strong understanding of what is involved in the maintenance of assets, modernization of workspaces, and transformation of owned/leased portfolios.
  • Strong financial acumen and understanding of both capital and operating expenditures within a real estate portfolio.
  • Expert ability to adapt communications and maintain alignment among diverse audiences, bridging the gap between highly technical teams, operational groups, and executive governance.
  • Strong proficiency in utilizing data tools to track portfolio performance metrics, turning complex, multi-location information into tailored summaries and comprehensive dashboards.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and negotiation skills (internal and external) to navigate seemingly-conflicting requirements and manage expectations.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Engineering, Business Administration, or equivalent experience and training.
  • Functional bilingualism (English/French).
  • Experience with Jira, Power BI, MS Project or similar tools is an asset.
  • Some travel may be required.

Are you a vibrant community connector? Creative brand storyteller? Strategic social media marketer?


Your role

CBC Yukon is looking for a Senior Communications and Marketing Specialist to join the CBC Marketing, Communications and Brand team in Whitehorse, YT.


The successful candidate will report to the Manager of Communications, Marketing and Brand for the North, including Yukon, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, and Nunavik. They will collaborate with team members to implement a variety of marketing/communications strategies, projects and initiatives to support CBC’s digital, radio and television programming across the North. 


This position requires someone with a passion for storytelling and relationship building, a deep understanding of the diverse and changing demographics of the region, and who thrives in fast-paced environments and relishes that no two days are the same


This is a permanent position based in Whitehorse, YT. This position is hybrid. An in-office presence in the CBC Whitehorse’s station is required, as is the ability to travel and work at community events and locations across the region as required. 


Duties for this position may include: 

  • Advancing strategic objectives to grow CBC’s connections with younger, diverse audiences, creating strategies to identify new audiences and reach people where they are, both in-person and online.
  • Leading and developing community engagement activities for CBC in the North including working closely with community partners and editorial colleagues on station initiatives, outreach opportunities, community events and stakeholder engagement.
  • Developing, implementing and monitoring strategic integrated marketing plans to promote the CBC brand, programming and initiatives across all platforms (social, digital, radio, TV). 
  • Collaborating with cross-functional teams and departments to develop and generate strategic campaigns that attract target audiences and foster meaningful engagement.
  • Create and implement innovative social media strategies to deepen our community connection and promote awareness and attendance for campaigns and events with new audiences. 
  • Creating strategies to identify new audiences, create tailored on-line experiences, foster brand engagement and enable community connection. 
  • Develop reports demonstrating campaign successes as well as identifying key learnings.
  • Collaborate with marketing communications teams across CBC to elevate national priorities and campaigns while supporting editorial objectives and journalism standards and practices.
  • Cultivate and manage relationships with internal and external partners including community members, partner organizations and vendors.

We are looking for a candidate with the following: 

  • Post-secondary certificate, diploma or a university degree in Communications/Public Relations or Marketing, or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience. 
  • Five or more years of experience in communications, public relations and/or marketing.
  • A strong proven connection to the communities we serve across the North, and experience developing strategies to connect with new, younger and more diverse audiences.
  • Superior writing, editing and proofreading skills, working knowledge of a wide range of communications and marketing materials and tactics and ability to adapt writing for different audiences and platforms.
  • Strong organization and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects on tight deadlines and with attention to detail.
  • Demonstrated ability to plan and coordinate events, both in-person and virtual, including development of critical path, run of show and briefing documents, and understanding of budget management.
  • Demonstrated public speaking and networking skills.
  • Superior social media marketing skills, with a keen understanding of digital/social trends and demonstrable success in creating social media content (filming, editing, posting according to brand guidelines), executing strategies/campaigns and managing business channels.
  • Ability to leverage research data to drive marketing decisions.
  • Experience with Google Suite tools (Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Meet).
  • Experience with Dash Social or other social media tools, and video editing tools with an understanding of creation, editing, captions for social media content purposes.
  • Flexibility in work hours as workflow demands, including the ability to work shift work, including evenings, weekends and holidays, as required.
  • Availability to travel across the team’s region for short periods if required. A valid driver’s licence as well as a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada's insurance company is considered an asset.
  • Knowledge of languages other than English is considered an asset, particularly an Indigenous language.
  • Demonstrated connection to and knowledge of Indigenous cultures and communities, and of the North.

Role Purpose:

Reporting to the Senior Director, Total Compensation, the Senior Manager, Total Compensation leads a team of two Senior Specialists in the governance, strategic design, implementation, and continuous improvement of CBC/Radio-Canada's core total compensation and associated programs. Serving as an operational leader, this role ensures robust compensation governance, provides expert advisory services across Human Resources and Industrial Relations, and leads the functional oversight of the People and Culture Access to Information and Privacy (ATIP) portfolio.

Key Responsibilities:

Compensation Governance, Strategy & Program Management

  • Establish, review, and evolve corporate standards, policies, and methodologies for all compensation-related programs across the Corporation (including market benchmarking, pay structures, job evaluations, and salary reviews).

  • Lead the annual salary planning (merit review) cycle, external market benchmarking studies, and comprehensive pay scale reviews.

  • Develop, implement, and monitor job evaluation plans to ensure regulatory compliance, process efficiency, and alignment with corporate benchmarks.

  • Conduct regular and specialized research into internal and external market practices; develop revised pay structures, models, and policy recommendations for senior leadership.

  • Recommend and implement updates to compensation and related policies to maintain the Corporation’s target competitive market position while ensuring full regulatory compliance and alignment with the corporate strategy.

Pay Equity & Union Collaboration

  • Participate in the implementation of the Corporation’s Pay Equity Plan in close collaboration with unions, leadership, and external consultants.

  • Oversee and conduct mandatory 5-year Pay Equity Audits in accordance with federal regulations, coordinating directly with union representatives and joint committees.

  • Provide strategic compensation input and recommendations for collective bargaining negotiations; provide support  to the Total Compensation expert representative at the bargaining table when required.

Strategic Partnerships & System Optimization

  • Partner with HRIS and HR Services teams in the continuous enhancement and optimization of HR Information Systems (Workday), identifying opportunities to streamline workflows and improve data efficiency.

  • Collaborate with the Benefits and Pension teams to foster a unified Total Rewards model and deliver clear, compelling Total Rewards employee communications.

  • Maintain an integrated HR approach, partnering closely with Talent Management & OD, Industrial Relations, HR Services, and HR Business Partners to ensure cohesive client service delivery.

ATIP & Regulatory Portfolio Oversight

  • Lead the Access to Information and Privacy (ATIP) portfolio for People & Culture, serving as the primary liaison with the corporate ATIP office and external governing bodies.

  • Manage and coordinate all People & Culture responses to ATIP, Privy Council Office, Statistics Canada, and other government/regulatory requests, ensuring accurate and timely delivery.

  • Provide functional guidance, coaching, and subject-matter expertise to HR Business Partners and Talent Acquisition leads on compensation frameworks and ATIP compliance principles.

Team Leadership & Operational Oversight

  • Direct, coach, and mentor a team of two Senior Specialists, establishing clear performance goals, providing developmental feedback, and fostering high team engagement.

  • Oversee the team’s daily workload to ensure high-quality, compliant execution of specialized compensation projects, advisory services, and continuous process improvements.

  • Influence and collaborate across People & Culture to promote process efficiency and operational productivity linked to Total Rewards and ATIP programs.

  • Go to resource when the Senior Director, Total Compensation is unavailable.

Qualifications, Experience & Skills:

Education & Experience

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Industrial Relations, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred).

  • Professional Experience: 8 to 10 years of progressive HR experience, with at least 5 years dedicated to compensation design, governance, and administration.

  • Leadership Experience: Minimum 2 to 3 years of experience directly managing, supervising, or mentoring direct reports or project teams.

  • Environment: Proven experience working within a complex, unionized public, Crown or private sector environment is strongly preferred.

  • Certifications: CCP (Certified Compensation Professional) or CHRL (Certified Human Resources Leader) designation is an asset.

Knowledge & Skills

  • Bilingualism: Fully bilingual in French and English (written and spoken) is mandatory.

  • Compensation Expertise: Advanced expertise in base pay design, job evaluation methodologies, market salary surveys, and federal pay equity legislation.

  • ATIP & Privacy Knowledge: Strong working knowledge of Access to Information and Privacy regulations and governance principles within the public sector context is an asset.

  • Critical Thinking & Decision-Making: Superior analytical capability and sound judgment to resolve complex, precedent-setting issues while balancing business needs with policy compliance.

  • Interpersonal & Strategic Communication: Excellent negotiation, diplomacy, and communication skills with a demonstrated ability to build strong cross-functional partnerships and influence senior executive stakeholders.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

The opportunity

CBC/Radio-Canada operates one of the world’s leading technology infrastructures and one of the largest private networks, which distributes its content and services across the country. CBC/Radio-Canada is looking for a technical senior manager, project oriented, to join our Engineering team. This position requires an interesting mix of leadership and expertise. This is a full-time permanent position, and the successful incumbent would be based in Montreal, with eventual and occasional travel to various other sites nationally.

What’s in it for you?

Challenges. We spend our days solving problems of all kinds. Media systems workflows are highly specialized and complicated; updating, installing and supporting technologies that are organization-wide and that impact broadcasting content is a time-sensitive, complex technical feat. And that’s just the beginning; we have challenges on all fronts. Reporting to the Director, you will help to manage the IT / Telecom Engineering team, support the implementation of important initiatives, help to improve our standards and best practices, as well as build bridges with other departments. Additionally, you will be afforded to work with cutting-edge technology and their experts.  

Perks you can look forward to:

  • Four weeks of vacation per year.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development - including access to e-learning services, customized courses and certification opportunities.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.

As our new Senior Manager, you will:

  • Work on strategic planning of technical resources.
  • Provide support and technical guidance to departmental employees.
  • Meet with stakeholders and business partners to determine requirements and solutions.
  • Take ownership of complex and strategic initiatives.
  • Track the schedules, budgets and progress on initiatives.
  • Contribute to the execution of complex procurement processes.
  • Manage a multidisciplinary team of technical professionals along with associated administrative processes.
  • Define, communicate, and monitor clear priorities, objectives, and performance metrics.
  • Actively participate to create an efficient and agile work environment.
  • Identify opportunities of operational, technical improvements and build innovative processes.

What you bring:

  • Experience in a leadership position and the management of various technical resources.
  • Experience in project management, specifically with the Agile approach.
  • Experience in delivery of high impact and complex technological projects.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Applied Science or Engineering, or a Diploma In Applied Science and Technology.
  • Membership, or eligibility to become a member, of the provincial Engineering Association (PEO, OIQ, … etc) is mandatory.
  • Strong, influential and clear communication skills, in English and French, considered a strong asset.
  • Strong commitment to ethical conduct and adherence to high business standards.
  • Acts as a role model by promoting a culture of trust, fairness, and compliance with organizational policies, and industry best practices.
  • Expertise on various technologies : Networking, Data centers, cabling infrastructure, IT systems (Compute, Storage, Virtualization & Cloud).
  • Knowledge on ST-2110 standards, multicasting, Telecom rooms, cybersecurity, and data management or relevant certifications is considered an asset.
  • Ability to build and maintain strong relationships with employees, peers, partners, management and external vendors.
  • Demonstrates sound decision-making abilities and effective delegation skills.
  • Proven ability to mobilize teams and quickly adapt to shifting priorities.
  • Ability to travel to different CBC locations to oversee different phases of projects.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

Senior Producer, Audience Growth(English Services) (On-Site)

CBC British Columbia is looking for an experienced newsroom leader who understands how to create content that will grow younger audiences where they look for it - on their phones.

This is a full-time, temporary 10-month position.

As CBC News prioritizes the needs of mobile and streaming audiences and delivers content that aligns with our strategic objectives, the new senior producer of audience growth ensures CBC's content directly connects with people who live and work in the province, including new and younger Canadians. You understand what people want to consume — and where, when, and how they want to consume it. You are obsessed with optimizing display content - the headlines, images and framing that audiences first see when they encounter our stories across platforms.

You bring a deep understanding of platform behaviours, effective publishing practices, video formats, SEO, comments, moderation and audience expectations. You understand and keep up to date on industry trends and technologies. You know how to package compelling text and video for CBC’s mobile and streaming news apps, as well as third‑party platforms like YouTube and TikTok. 

As a strong editorial leader reporting to the executive producers of CBC British Columbia, you work closely with reporters and producers to ensure daily digital storytelling is innovative, timely and consistent with CBC's Journalistic Standards and Practices. You work in conjunction with the wider Audience Growth team to support best practices that set us up to win on mobile and streaming platforms. You are constantly communicating learnings and data back to the teams.

The position requires full-time, on-site presence at the Vancouver CBC Office. 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Provide and interpret audience data to newsroom leaders to help inform their programming decisions.

  • Provide clear, actionable feedback to teams on audience needs and publishing and packaging fundamentals.

  • Work in partnership with CBC News’ Audience Growth team to:

  • Communicate audience insights and context across all platforms to daily news teams.

  • Establish best practices across platforms to deliver on measurable audience growth goals for CBC News.

  • Optimize high-performing local stories (including photos, graphics headlines, story-framing, sidebars, etc.).

  • Evolve tactics for growing local audiences, including new platform experiments (e.g., WhatsApp).

  • Identify training needs across the newsroom.

  • Partner with EPs and MEs to set regional audience targets aligned with engagement objectives.

  • Make quick editorial decisions under pressure in complex, time‑sensitive environments.

  • Work closely with teams to get breaking news to the audience quickly and cohesively.

  • Monitor trends across digital media and adapt workflows and publishing strategies as needed.

  • Partner with executive producers and CBC British Columbia’s Managing Editors to set regional audience targets aligned with engagement objectives.

  • Use key production tools (9CMS, DTV, Media Central, Dalet, Adobe).

Skills & Experience:

  • Minimum seven years of journalism experience, five years of which must include video experience in a breaking news environment.

  • Experience interpreting audience analytics and applying them to editorial and strategic decisions.

  • Demonstrated ability to assign, motivate, and develop staff.

  • Excellent editorial judgment and a strong understanding of CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices.

  • Proven passion for strong journalism, innovative video storytelling, and sharp, effective writing.

  • Experience in copy editing, fact‑checking, packaging, and production across platforms.

  • Intimate knowledge and experience producing different video formats, such as vertical and mobile‑optimized storytelling.

  • Nuanced understanding of audience behaviours on social and video‑sharing platforms.

  • Comfortable with constant change; able to adapt, communicate clearly, and maintain composure.

  • Strong coaching skills and ability to train staff quickly.

  • Cultural awareness, openness, and collaborative communication skills.

  • Ability to work flexible hours, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays.

  • Ability to meet tight deadlines and navigate unexpected overtime.

  • University degree or equivalent experience

Your role


Radio-Canada Toronto is looking for an enthusiastic senior writer to join its Economic Bureau. This is a temporary position until mid-September 2027.


The successful candidate will identify and produce original stories related to the economy, innovation, and consumer trends. They will present their content across all Radio-Canada platforms, with priority given to digital formats.


They will possess strong journalistic skills, tact, and solid experience writing digital news. The selected candidate must know how to create and organize digital news content and enrich texts with multimedia elements to increase their value to the audience.


The chosen candidate will also report and explain news stories concerning, for instance, commercial trade or the impact of changes to the Bank of Canada key interest rate, sometimes under tight deadlines.


The work is performed under the direction of a senior producer or assignment editor, but you are expected to show initiative and judgment. You will also be asked to edit the work of others.


Main tasks:

  • Find stories of interest to a broad audience.
  • Gather information from various sources and report it in text, video, or audio format across all our platforms, prioritizing digital.
  • Write, edit, assemble, and publish content related to economics, business, innovation and consumer trends in a clear and concise manner for regional and national audiences, prioritizing digital formats.
  • Rewrite texts as needed to better align with the platform format.
  • Ensure that all texts adhere to standard grammar rules and Radio-Canada site style, including proper spelling and capitalization.
  • Prepare and draft digital alerts.
  • Select photos and audio/video clips to accompany published reports.
  • Critically review content and items produced by others and suggest changes while showing tact and respect.
  • Prepare and write articles and headlines from information provided by reporters, news wires, CBC, or original sources.
  • Edit audio and video content to produce reports within deadlines.


This role requires full-time on-site presence.


Your profile:

  • University degree or equivalent.
  • Three (3) to five (5) years of experience directly related to the position, including proven knowledge of online and digital news media.
  • Extensive and evident knowledge of Ontario current affairs, major economic issues, and the business world, as well as a strong interest in consumer trends and innovation topics.
  • Sound editorial judgment to evaluate information and ability to work effectively under pressure in a newsroom with tight deadlines.
  • Ability to write a wide range of material related to news and current events.
  • Experience and proven ability to write/edit following best practices and style for digital platforms.
  • Ability to select and prepare photos and videos to enrich reports.
  • Experience identifying potential legal issues and journalistic policy violations in digital content.
  • Ability to determine news value for online audiences.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills; excellent team player.
  • Strong commitment to embodying and promoting diversity, inclusion, and respect in the workplace.
  • Ability to develop original, initiative-driven journalism.
  • Skills in mathematics and data analysis are an asset.
  • A valid driver's license and driving record meeting CBC/Radio-Canada's insurer minimum requirements is an important asset.
  • Ability to work various shifts, including early mornings, late evenings, and weekends.
  • Knowledge of audio and video editing software is an asset.

CBC News is looking for an innovative and versatile video producer with a strong interest in world news and excellent field video producing skills to join our new bureau in Jerusalem, covering the Middle East. If you’re a creator at heart and enjoy storytelling and producing content across visual formats, this job could be for you. 

At a time when the world, and Canada’s place within it, is rapidly changing, being present on the ground to bring stories Canadians want and need to know about is critical. As part of our expanding world coverage team, you’ll work closely with a correspondent in Jerusalem, your colleagues in other world bureaus and journalists with Radio-Canada, who will also be working in the Jerusalem bureau. 

You bring a deep knowledge of the historical complexities of the Middle East and the confidence to help shape the CBC News editorial coverage. 

You’re a technical whiz who will be shooting, editing, packaging and publishing content using a variety of gear and apps. This includes social video content, live hits, live streams and on demand content. 

You are also strong editorially. You have story ideas and are thinking about creative treatments to attract new and younger audiences through social-first formats. You excel at guiding stories from concept to post-production, and are quick to pivot when plans change. 

You are deeply committed to the values of a public service broadcaster. You uphold the CBC Journalistic Standards and Practices, especially our core principles of accuracy, fairness, balance, impartiality and integrity. 

You understand that stories can break at any time of the day and you have a genuine desire to be on-top of that coverage. The position requires long-hours, flexible schedules and a willingness to deploy on a moment’s notice, including to conflict zones. The minimum assignment length for this position is two years and, if agreed to by both parties, may be extended for up to an additional two years. 

What you’ll be doing: 

  • Pitches, shoots, produces and edits short and long-form digital-first video content tailored for platforms like TikTok and YouTube as well as CBC.ca.

  • Manage on-the-ground gear — including cameras, portable lighting, and wireless mics — to capture visually impactful footage and clean audio for news content. 

  • Ingest, organize, assemble, and edit raw footage into compelling narrative formats using industry-standard software (such as Premiere Pro); attention to good sound design and mixing; knowledge of basic motion graphics/titles to elevate production value. 

  • Generate and execute compelling journalism, including researching, writing, generating and editing video, audio and text. 

  • Performing location surveys and identifying special requirements such as audio, lighting, camera angles and equipment, including production limitations. 

  • Providing technical guidance and expertise focused on content production techniques, workflows and creative content gathering techniques for complex situations. 

  • Collaborate effectively across CBC News to ensure comprehensive coverage across multiple platforms, programs and locations. 

What is required: 

  • You are a seasoned video-journalist with at least five (5) years of directly related field experience at a network/national level and, preferably in a foreign environment, who thrives in a deadline driven, high pressure environment. 

  • A superior level of technical knowledge and understanding of live coverage, social treatments, visual gathering, visual production and post-production methods and remote filing tools.

  • A strong sense of creativity, initiative and a high degree of responsibility for the accuracy and quality of work throughout the complete production cycle.

  • Demonstrated editorial skills, showing proficiency in story preparation and production of highly creative, innovative visual storytelling, from story generation through to the final edits. 

  • Strong communication, interpersonal and relationship-building skills are required, including active listening, problem-solving and an ability to work across teams.  

  • Ability to work independently in a deadline-driven environment while maintaining a professional attitude.

  • Must possess a valid passport and have the ability and willingness to travel internationally on short notice. 

  • Graduate degree/diploma from a University or Community college in a relevant course of study or equivalent industry experience. 

  • Ability and willingness to work overtime and various shift patterns including overnights and weekends. 

Your application will be evaluated on your experience, as well as your portfolio of work. 

Please include at least two examples of: 

  • Digital / social stories you produced and shot

  • Packaged daily news video content you shot and edited 

  • A cover letter that tells us why you want this role, and how you will use your experience to support the bureau

job.title: Chief Engineer
job.description:
Connoisseur Media is looking for a Full-Time Engineer for our North Dallas (Sherman-McKinney, TX) market. The ideal candidate has basic knowledge of, or is willing to learn about, radio broadcast technical systems and equipment to ensure reliable, high-quality audio transmission for our three radio stations - 97.5 KLAK, 93.1 KMKT, and 102.5 KMAD-FM. The ideal candidate works well under pressure, creates solutions, and is a resourceful, diligent, engaged, and creative problem-solver, with not just a “can-do” but a “will-do” attitude. While we seek someone well-versed in, or willingness to learn, broadcast engineering, a candidate’s interpersonal and communication skills, as well as business and personal integrity, are just as important as technical ability.

Responsibilities

for this position include: Compliance with FCC regulations and station policies regarding broadcast standards. Maintenance of safety protocols in all engineering practices. Chief Operator (EAS, Maintenance, and Transmitter Readings log management & review). Regular inspection and maintenance of broadcast equipment, including a mix of solid-state and high-power tube transmitters, audio consoles, studio gear, audio automation systems, remote broadcast systems, and other related equipment. Perform hands-on routine preventive maintenance and repairs on all technical systems. Monitor audio quality and signal strength during radio broadcasts and be able to quickly troubleshoot issues, as needed. Under the direction of Corporate IT, complete all necessary procedures and paperwork relating to the market’s computer system and be the local eyes and hands for remote IT Help Desk support. Oversee the installation of new equipment and technologies, including the planning and implementation of upgrades to existing systems. Work with the Director of Engineering and market Operations Manager to manage capital projects and implement corporate initiatives. Maintain minimal downtime of broadcast, audio and computer systems, including emergency repairs, but also planning and advocating for any necessary improvements to all systems. Provide technical support and expertise, as needed, to other departments in planning and executing initiatives. Clear, professional, and productive communication with employees who do not have technical or programming backgrounds, as well as subcontractors and vendors. Develop clear instructions relating to simple tasks for non-technical employees to understand and perform. Maintain an accurate equipment inventory, maintenance logs, and technical schematics. This includes the preparation of reports relating to asset additions/disposals and technical issues and solutions. Requirements of this position include the following: A minimum of 1-3 years audio engineering, Radio/TV broadcast engineering and/or IT experience. Knowledge of FCC Regulations. Availability to travel to multiple market locations and transmitter sites. Familiarity with, or willingness to learn about, broadcast automation and centralized audio routing systems. Basic knowledge of, or willingness to learn about, computer networks, STL systems, RF & landline, including analog, digital, and IP. A flexible self-manager with the ability to prioritize tasks and shift priorities as needed. This position requires a fully insured personal vehicle and a valid driver’s license. The candidate is required to provide a safe driving record covering the past three years. Must be able to develop collaborative and productive relationships with market employees, so market staff can help troubleshoot effectively when the engineer is off-site. On call availability for transmitter, studio, and remote broadcast technical issues, remote alarm calls, emergencies, and be proactive about coverage when unavailable. ​

Military or Post-Secondary electronics training. SBE Certification.

Experience

with Axia LiveWire routing. Demonstrated Project Management skills.​

job.description:
