job.title: Bilingual Sales Consultant
job.description:
Bilingual Sales Consultant, Austin, Texas← View all Norsan Media careersNorsan Media

Bilingual Sales Consultant

Austin, Texas•Full-time
$30,000+ annuallyApply
About the Job
Are you a results-driven, bilingual sales professional with proven sales experience, preferably in advertising, media, or marketing but not necessary looking for an opportunity in media sales?

Do you have a passion for helping businesses grow through innovative advertising solutions? If so, we want you on our team!

Why Join Us?
At Norsan Media, we are more than just a media company, we are a trusted voice in the Latino community, delivering engaging radio, print, digital, and event experiences across multiple markets. As a Bilingual Sales Consultant, you’ll play a key role in helping businesses connect with their audience through impactful radio advertising campaigns.

What You’ll Do:
  • Identify and develop new business opportunities by prospecting potential clients.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, understanding their unique advertising needs.
  • Create customized advertising solutions that align with clients’ marketing goals.
  • Negotiate and close advertising contracts that deliver mutual success.
  • Work closely with internal teams to ensure seamless campaign execution.
  • Monitor ad performance, provide insights, and recommend optimizations.
  • Stay ahead of market trends and competitor activities to provide strategic advice.

What We’re Looking For:
  • Bilingual (English & Spanish) with excellent communication skills.
  • Proven sales experience, preferably in advertising, media, or marketing.
  • A go-getter attitude with strong prospecting and networking skills.
  • Ability to understand client objectives and develop tailored marketing solutions.
  • Skilled in negotiation and closing deals.
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple projects.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and CRM software.

What We Offer:
  • $30,000 annual base salary + uncapped commission (your earnings are in your hands!).
  • Ongoing training and professional growth opportunities.
  • A dynamic, collaborative, and supportive work environment.
  • Flexible schedule and remote work options. Mileage reimbursement for client visits.

Ready to Make an Impact?
If you’re passionate about sales, media, and making a difference in the Hispanic market, we’d love to hear from you!

Apply today and start your journey with Norsan Media!
About Us:
The company currently owns and operates Regional Mexican, Latin Urban, Latin Pop/Tropical, Spanish Adult Contemporary stations in the Southeast and Austin, TX. The company has a combined reach of over 3 million Hispanics with their coverage in the US. In 2004, NORSAN launched Norsan Media in the Southeast and is based in Charlotte, NC and currently owns over 50 radio stations, 4 TV stations, a weekly regional digital and printed publication, and digital marketing and social media platforms in North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida and Texas.

Norsan Media’s holding company, NORSAN, was founded in 1987 by Norberto Sanchez. He continues to serve as Chairman of the company. NORSAN currently owns and operates 18 restaurants including Frontera Mexican Kitchen, Luciano’s Ristorante Italiano, Pampas Steakhouse, Frankie’s the Steakhouse, La Capital MX, H&W Steakhouse, Pinto’s Mexican Made Easy concept and operates the 1818 Club. Prime Meats, a USDA and SQF certified company providing high-quality meats to various distributors across half of the US, was recently acquired by Shoreline Equity Partners where Norberto Sanchez continues as Chairman of the Board.Apply

job.title: ACPR Federal Manager
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Deadline and Instructions:

  • Please submit your resume and cover letter by 5:00 pm EST October 16th, 2026
  • Please answer the following prompt in your cover letter:
    • Tell us about a policy or program that you played a role in changing, developing or creating from the original idea to the execution. Please include what you learned from that experience.

 

Under NPR’s Employee Code of Conduct, this employee will be considered an “Outward-Facing Employee”, and as such should (i) avoid public participation in political and partisan activities in order to protect NPR’s reputation and its ability to pursue its mission; and (ii) refrain from public statements or actions that might call into question NPR’s commitment to accuracy and fairness.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain a sophisticated political network across Capitol Hill and federal agencies, serving as a registered lobbyist; manage LDA compliance activities pertaining to ACPR.
  • Proactively manage a dynamic advocacy strategy for ACPR federal initiatives in support of public radio stations. 
  • Track, analyze, and brief internal leadership on legislative, regulatory, and policy developments impacting ACPR’s federal strategy.
  • Design and execute proactive engagement plans, including policy briefings, staff delegations, and advocacy days that support public radio station relationships with Capitol Hill.
  • Regularly meet with Hill staff, including all Committees relevant to public radio, to educate them, utilizing all available communications means to keep them informed on relevant public radio updates.
  • Conduct in-depth research on Members of Congress and executive branch officials to develop effective political and advocacy strategies.
  • Research and track upcoming congressional hearings, monitor administrative policy announcements, and distribute notes to internal teams and coalition partners.
  • Partner with the ACPR Sr. Manager for Communications & Engagement to develop and transmit ACPR advocacy materials, including hill blasts, factsheets, testimony, and blog posts.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • 5-7 years experience in a government affairs or advocacy role
  • Time spent working in Congress with an emphasis on the House of Representatives, or working on agriculture or Farm Bill issues
  • Existing professional networks on the Hill, with an emphasis on the House of Representatives
  • Experience navigating the federal appropriations process 
  • Experience with nonpartisan advocacy initiatives 
  • Proficient in the use of MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Google suite products

Preferred Qualifications

  • Demonstrable experience creating new programs, championing appropriations on behalf of a member organization and/or trade association, and/or establishing or adapting appropriations
  • Awareness of local media ecosystems, emergency communications networks, rural development, and/or local cultural institutions

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Ability to communicate clearly to a variety of audiences including public radio leaders, public officials, stakeholders and the general public
  • Experience working with bipartisan lawmakers and a commitment to working in a nonpartisan environment
  • Willingness to work collaboratively with an evolving team
  • Enthusiasm for the mission of public radio

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Communications or a related field, or equivalent work experience

Work Location & Requirements

  • Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. Some aspects of this role require duties better performed at an NPR facility. The employee will be required to be in the office at the Washington, D.C. location at least 3 days a week- Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday. The employee must also reside in an NPR-supported location based on the number of on-site days they choose.

Job Type

  • This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S.-based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $132,000 - $139,000 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees. 

Does this sound like you? If so, we want to hear from you.

#LI-HYBRID

NPR is an Equal Opportunity Employer. NPR is committed to being an inclusive workplace that welcomes diverse and unique perspectives, all working toward the same goal – to create a more informed public. Qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnicity, national origin, ancestry, age, religion, religious belief, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions, lactation, and reproductive health decisions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, transgender status, gender non-conforming status, intersex status, sexual stereotypes, nationality, citizenship status, personal appearance, marital status, family status, family responsibilities, military status, veteran status, mental and physical disability, medical condition, genetic information, genetic characteristics of yourself or a family member, political views and affiliation, unemployment status, protective order status, status as a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking, or any other basis prohibited under applicable law.

If you are a person with a disability needing assistance with the application process, please reach out to employeerelations@npr.org.

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

NPR is seeking a Systems Engineer for its Distribution IT Infrastructure team to manage, test, and maintain our enterprise virtualized infrastructure, including servers, storage, and networking systems. In this role, you will deploy, configure, monitor, and troubleshoot modern virtualization platforms (such as VMware vSphere, HPE Morpheus VM Essentials, or Proxmox) to guarantee high availability, scalability, and security across NPR's core distribution technologies.

This role sits at the intersection of physical and virtual infrastructure: you will help stand up new data center hardware and build NPR's private cloud environment on top of it, from rack and cable to hypervisor and host networking.

Working collaboratively with Infrastructure and Security colleagues, you will analyze business workflows, implement structured change management processes, and support capacity planning initiatives to deliver resilient, mission-critical operations for NPR and our nationwide Member station network.

Responsibilities

  • Physical Infrastructure Build-Out: Partner with Infrastructure colleagues to install, rack, cable, and configure new server, storage, and network hardware, including firmware updates, out-of-band management (e.g., HPE iLO, Dell iDRAC), and RAID/BIOS configuration, to establish the foundation for virtualized workloads.
  • Virtual Infrastructure Deployment & Maintenance: Deploy, configure, and maintain virtualized systems using enterprise tools (e.g., HPE Morpheus VM Essentials, Proxmox, Nutanix, Incus, or VMware) to support operational reliability.
  • Architecture Evaluation & Testing: Evaluate virtual system architecture, compare existing applications, and create metrics to measure response times and availability for test environments.
  • Change Management Implementation: Recommend and execute system enhancements following established organizational change management policies and procedures.
  • Operational & Capacity Support: Assist the Distribution Infrastructure team in executing cloud/virtualization workflows and capacity planning tools focused on return on investment and business value.
  • Security Alignment & Compliance: Partner with Security Engineers to ensure virtual hosts, operating systems, and network configurations comply with organizational security policies.
  • Workflow & Process Analysis: Analyze and document Distribution IT process workflows, identifying areas for continuous improvement and operational efficiency.
  • Technical Documentation & Knowledge Sharing: Create comprehensive documentation, procedures, instructions, and training materials for internal colleagues and system users.
  • Incident Escalation & Operational Support: Proactively communicate operational status to management, participate in an on-call rotation, and respond to critical system issues on a 24x7 basis as needed.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 3+ years of professional experience supporting, maintaining, troubleshooting, and administering servers and networking within a data center environment.
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience in the planning, design, deployment, and management of enterprise virtualized cloud infrastructure (e.g., VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V, or open-source hypervisors).
  • Hands-on experience with physical data center hardware, including racking and cabling servers, configuring out-of-band 
  • Competence in DNS administration (BIND preferred).
  • Experience with IP address management (IPAM) and DHCP services.
  • Experience with configuration management (Puppet preferred).
  • Experience creating agentless automation workflows (Ansible preferred).
  • Experience with Mail Transfer Agent administration (Exim).
  • Working knowledge of Windows Server administration (2022+) alongside core directory and networking protocols (Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, IIS).
  • Practical experience supporting enterprise storage (NetApp or TrueNAS).
  • Comfortable with networking configuration of hosts, switches, and routers, including VLANs, trunking, and NIC bonding/link aggregation as applied to hypervisor hosts.
  • Proven track record as a key contributor or project leader on complex technical initiatives, including the creation of detailed technical documentation and workflow diagrams.
  • Demonstrated ability to participate effectively in a team environment, handle multiple concurrent projects, and contribute to an on-call rotation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Unix/Linux networking configuration and Cisco switches and routers (Catalyst or Nexus/NX-OS).
  • Familiarity with scripting languages (Python, PowerShell, or JavaScript).
  • Experience with enterprise backup/recovery solutions (e.g., Veeam).
  • Experience with HPE ProLiant or Dell PowerEdge server hardware.
  • Knowledge of Linux operating systems and relevant industry certifications (VMware VCP, Microsoft, or AWS).

Required Skills/Competencies

  • System Troubleshooting & Diagnostics: Ability to systematically isolate, diagnose, and resolve complex issues across hardware, server, storage, network, and virtualized layers.
  • Structured Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills to present technical concepts and write actionable system documentation.
  • Prioritization Under Pressure: Capacity to prioritize tasks effectively during high-urgency system maintenance or operational incidents.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Strong interpersonal skills to partner seamlessly with Security, Network, and Distribution engineering teams.
  • Continuous Learning Mindset: Commitment to staying current with emerging virtualization tools, cloud platforms, and data center technologies.

Education Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, OR equivalent practical work experience.

job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Instructions

  • Application Deadline: Monday, October 19th, at 5:00 pm ET.
  • Submission Instructions: Please submit a cover letter in addition to your resume including a direct link to a story (audio or digital) that you edited and were particularly proud of. Please describe any challenges you encountered, and call out the contributions you made.

Intro to Position

The Network Desk represents NPR’s strategic commitment to deepening, broadening, and transforming how we partner with Member stations and Regional Hubs. As the Northeast Regional Editor, you will serve as the essential bridge between local station newsrooms across the Northeast and national NPR news programs and digital platforms. In this role, you will help identify, curate, and elevate distinctive local reporting to national audiences while helping stations plan and execute ambitious enterprise and breaking news coverage.

The ideal candidate brings a collaborative editorial mindset, sharp line-editing skills across audio and text, and a commitment to expanding the diversity of sources and stories emerging from the region.

NPR defines its Northeast Region as ME, NH, VT, MA, RI, CT, NY, NJ, PA, DE, MD, and DC.

This is a union represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with SAG-AFTRA. 

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff are defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.   

Responsibilities

  • Network Editorial Coordination: Communicate and collaborate daily with journalists, news directors, and editors across Northeast regional hubs and Member stations to identify, develop, and coordinate coverage with national resonance.
  • Content Editing & Quality Assurance: Edit, fact-check, and supervise the preparation of multiplatform material (audio, digital, broadcast) from station reporters and freelancers, ensuring all work meets NPR’s journalistic standards of fairness, accuracy, and technical quality.
  • Breaking News Leadership: Coordinate rapid-response breaking news coverage from the region, directing station updates and dispatches for national shows, digital platforms, and hourly newscasts.
  • Show & Platform Integration: Maintain ongoing communication with NPR daily news magazines (Morning Edition, All Things Considered, Here & Now), podcasts, and the digital news desk regarding story length, angles, framing, and scheduling.
  • Coverage Planning & Horizon Scanning: Track evolving regional news cycles, maintain forward-looking editorial calendars, and spot emerging cultural, political, and systemic trends across the Northeast.
  • Editorial Mentorship & Training: Partner with Regional Hubs to conduct workshops, coaching sessions, and feedback discussions that strengthen station reporting capabilities and familiarize partners with NPR production workflows.
  • Inclusive Sourcing & Story Development: Champion story ideas that reflect the full demographic and geographical diversity of the Northeast, actively expanding regional source networks.
  • Desk Administration & Contributor Management: Coordinate administrative desk workflows, including processing freelancer agreements, story commissions, and reporter filing payments in accordance with established agreements.
  • Network Collaboration: Partner with fellow regional editors and Network Desk leadership to refine communication pipelines, eliminate operational silos, and improve newsroom workflows.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time. 

Required Skills

  • 5+ years of professional journalism experience at with a reputable news organization.
  • 3+ years of experience editing regional or national daily news coverage across audio and digital platforms.
  • Demonstrated track record editing breaking news under tight deadlines with precision and journalistic integrity.
  • Proven experience editing enterprise, investigative, or feature journalism, guiding stories from pitch to final audio/digital production.
  • Sound journalistic judgment rooted in rigorous fact-checking, balance, fairness, and adherence to editorial ethics.
  • Track record of building collaborative partnerships with decentralized reporters, freelancers, or station partners.
  • Experience editing for both the ear (audio broadcast/podcasting) and the eye (digital news writing).
  • Willingness to travel up to 10% of the time for visits to member stations and other stakeholders.

Preferred Skills

  • Prior reporting or editing experience within the public media system (Member stations, regional news hubs, or public media collaborations).
  • Deep familiarity with the socio-political, economic, and cultural landscape of the Northeast region.
  • Bilingual or multilingual fluency relevant to regional coverage areas.

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Editorial & Audio Craft: Exceptional news-writing, line-editing, and sound-rich audio structuring skills.
  • Collaborative Leadership: Ability to offer constructive, empathetic, and clear feedback to journalists of varied experience levels.
  • Adaptability & Calm Under Pressure: Ability to prioritize multiple assignments and navigate breaking news calmly and decisively.
  • Cross-Platform Agility: Comfort navigating modern digital content management systems, audio editing tools, and communication platforms (Slack, AirTable, etc.).

Education Requirement

  • Bachelor's degree in journalism, communications, or a related field, or equivalent relevant work experience.

Work Location

  • Remote Required: This is a remote required role. This role includes duties that are better performed or are required to be performed in a designated location OUTSIDE of an NPR facility. The employee is required to work at a designated remote work location within the designated coverage area: ME, NH, VT, MA, RI, CT, NY, NJ, PA, DE, MD or DC.

Job Type

  • This is a full time, exempt position.

Compensation

Benefits: NPR offers access to comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Deadline:

Please submit your application by 5:00 pm EST on October 23rd, 2026

Intro to Position

You will be critical to building a new, leaner, audience-centric, data-driven app that serves NPR and partnering stations in multi-modal formats. As the Insights Analyst, you will support data-informed decision-making for NPR’s digital ecosystem. Central to this role is hands-on SQL expertise—writing complex queries against massive, unaggregated datasets, translating raw digital behavior into actionable product insights.

In this role, you will be the main point of contact to create measurement plans, implement and QC analytics tags, build automated dashboards, and perform deep-dive analyses across app, web, and video platforms. Working closely with digital product teams, the newsroom, and member station leaders, you will apply a blend of data curiosity and technical pragmatism to expand weekly audiences, increase listening hours, and deepen daily habits.

This role reports to the Audience Insights Director, Digital Insights.

This is a union-represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with NABET-CWA DMU.

Responsibilities

  • Advanced SQL Analysis & Querying: Independently write, optimize, and streamline complex SQL queries across app, video, and web datasets; regularly handle raw event data, including unnesting nested arrays and struct fields (e.g., BigQuery GA4 export).
  • Tagging Implementation & QC: Develop and manage measurement plans for NPR's owned and operated platforms using Google Tag Manager; conduct quality control (QC) and validation of tracking tags across releases.
  • Data Infrastructure & Automation: Maintain and optimize scheduled queries, data summaries, and automated reporting pipelines to support sustainable backend data hygiene.
  • Stakeholder Consultation & Dashboards: Partner closely with Product and Data Products teams to design, build, and maintain interactive dashboards (e.g., Looker) and establish self-service analytics frameworks for internal stakeholders.
  • Product Optimization Insights: Support product analytics needs for the NPR App, website, and video platforms, extracting actionable user habit and audience retention insights.
  • Data Quality & Troubleshooting: Diagnose, investigate, and resolve data discrepancies, tracking errors, or underlying schema issues across reporting tools.
  • Documentation & Best Practices: Write clear technical guides, tagging specifications, and documentation for app, video, and website analytics standards.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with product managers, editorial teams, and technical groups to translate business questions into technical measurement plans and data infrastructure updates.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 2+ years of hands-on SQL experience: Demonstrated proficiency writing complex queries from scratch, working with relational databases and enterprise data warehouses (e.g., BigQuery, Dataform).
  • Raw Data & Array Manipulation: Proven experience querying large-scale, raw digital event datasets (such as GA4 raw exports), including demonstrated skill in unnesting arrays and handling complex record structures.
  • 2+ years of App & Digital Analytics: Direct experience with app and web event tracking (Firebase, GA4, or similar platforms) and understanding the full tracking lifecycle from tag firing to analysis.
  • Tag Management Expertise: 2+ years of experience creating measurement plans and testing/QCing tracking implementations via Google Tag Manager (GTM).
  • Data Visualization & Tools: Experience building reports and dashboards in Looker (or similar BI tools) alongside advanced spreadsheet modeling capabilities (Google Sheets/Excel).
  • Cross-Functional Communication: Proven ability to collaborate with technical and non-technical teams, translating stakeholder needs into structured data infrastructure plans.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience within news media, public broadcasting, or digital content platforms.
  • Experience modeling or analyzing data using statistical scripting languages (R or Python).
  • Familiarity with building sustainable data governance or self-service analytics systems.

Required Skills/Competencies

  1. Advanced SQL & Raw Data Querying: Fluent in writing efficient SQL queries against high-volume, event-level and unaggregated data
  2. Tagging & Analytics Implementation: Technical competence in digital analytics architecture, Google Tag Manager deployment, Firebase event tracking, and data QA protocols.
  3. Data Visualization & Storytelling: Proficiency in transforming raw SQL query outputs into intuitive Looker dashboards and clear spreadsheets for stakeholder decision-making.
  4. Cross-Functional Alignment: Strong partner capable of bridging the gap between digital product managers, software engineers, and editorial teams.
  5. Analytical Problem-Solving: A self-starter mindset dedicated to identifying root causes of data anomalies, writing clear documentation, and iteratively improving data systems.

Work Location & Requirements

  • NPR Remote-Permitted: This is a remote-permitted role. This role is based out of our Washington, D.C. office, but the employee may choose to work on a remote basis from a location that NPR approves. You will have the option of working (a) remotely from a location of your choosing within the United States that is supported by NPR; (b) on-site at an NPR facility, based on the availability of desks and approval from NPR; or (c) a combination of both. Regardless of where you choose to work from, you may be expected to travel to other locations from time to time to perform the duties of your position.

Job Type

Compensation

job.description:

We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

Application Instructions

  • Application Deadline: Friday, October 16th, at 5:00 pm ET

Intro to Position

As the Music Rights & Clearances Manager, you will serve as the essential bridge between NPR Music’s creative programming and the complex landscape of intellectual property rights in an evolving media environment. You will lead the end-to-end clearance process for flagship productions—including the globally recognized Tiny Desk series—acting as a critical partner between production units, legal counsel, and external music industry rights holders.

This is a high-impact operational role for a detail-oriented licensing professional ready to modernize rights-tracking infrastructure, execute publishing and master agreements, and protect the artistic integrity and legal compliance of one of the most influential entities in music and public media.

Responsibilities

Flagship Clearances & Production Licensing

  • Clear Publishing & Composition Rights: Manage the research, negotiation, and clearance of musical compositions and publishing rights for NPR’s Tiny Desk concerts, special music events, and other programming.
  • Secure Master & Synchronization Licenses: Lead the acquisition of master recording, sync, performance rights, and other clearances for music-focused podcasts, documentary video series, and digital editorial packages.
  • Administer Releases & Performance Documentation: Maintain robust systems to verify that all featured artists, touring musicians, and record labels have signed required appearance releases, liability agreements, and rights documentation prior to broadcast or publication.

Platform Rights Management & Financial Coordination

  • Oversee Multi-Platform Digital Rights: Collaborate with Permissions Department and external distribution partners to monitor, claim, and clear music rights across third-party digital platforms (e.g., YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, and streaming channels).
  • Coordinate Royalties & Distribution Accounting: Partner with internal finance teams, accounting colleagues, and external rights holders to support payment schedules and reconcile royalty obligations related to content distribution models.
  • Manage Inbound & Outbound Rights Agreements: Review, execute, and archive inbound licenses and outbound syndication agreements, maintaining compliance across all content-sharing partnerships.

Operational Infrastructure & Legal Governance

  • Design & Implement Clearance Workflows: Design, document, and operationalize repeatable cross-functional clearance workflows and intake protocols that eliminate bottlenecks between production teams, legal counsel, and external partners.
  • Partner with Office of General Counsel: Collaborate closely with NPR’s legal team to interpret contractual provisions, assess intellectual property risk, and enforce organizational compliance standards across all active agreements.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • 5+ years of professional experience in music licensing, clearances, or copyright administration within a media company, record label, music publisher, streaming service, or entertainment law environment.
  • Deep operational mastery of music licensing processes, including synchronization rights, master recording rights, publishing agreements, public performance rights (ASCAP, BMI, SESAC, GMR), and mechanical licensing frameworks.
  • Proven experience clearing rights and managing copyright claims across third-party digital and social media video platforms (e.g., YouTube Content ID, TikTok, Meta).
  • Demonstrated track record interpreting, administering, and managing inbound and outbound appearance releases and licensing agreements.
  • Proven experience designing, documenting, and implementing operational workflows or clearance tracking systems that improve turnaround times and team adoption across creative and administrative units.
  • Proven ability to build consensus and collaborate effectively across creative production teams, legal counsel, and external artist representatives under strict production deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on proficiency utilizing enterprise database and workflow management systems (such as Airtable, Salesforce, Asana, or dedicated rights-tracking software).
  • Prior experience in requesting, negotiating, and securing gratis licenses, promotional waivers, or favorable rate structures from music publishers and record labels for cultural, editorial, or non-profit productions.

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Analytical Legal Acumen: Ability to analyze contract language meticulously, identify intellectual property liabilities, and propose practical, risk-mitigating solutions.
  • Diplomatic Negotiation: Exceptional interpersonal and negotiation skills to advocate for NPR's creative interests while cultivating positive, long-term relationships with artists, managers, and labels.
  • High-Urgency Prioritization: Strong organizational ability to manage high-volume clearance pipelines and adapt swiftly to changing production schedules without sacrificing accuracy.
  • Structured Cross-Functional Communication: Clear, professional written and verbal communication skills to present legal requirements and licensing status updates to non-legal production staff.
  • Mission-Driven Artistic Advocacy: Passion for supporting independent and diverse musical artistry, public service media, and accessible cultural storytelling.

Education Requirements

  •  Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience

Work Location & Requirements

  • Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. The employee will be required to be in the office at either our Washington, D.C., New York, NY or Culver City, CA location at least 3 days a week. The employee must also reside in Washington, D.C., New York or Los Angeles Metro Area(s).

Job Type

Please submit your resume and cover letter. In your cover letter please share your philosophy for leading a newsroom overnight in order to deliver the most up-to-date morning broadcast possible.

Intro to Position

Morning Edition and Up First are looking for a resilient journalist with strong news judgment, excellent writing skills and a willingness to work overnights as the Overnight/Live Broadcast Supervising Editor, managing  a production team that executes what is needed to get the live radio show to air and the Up First podcast to publication.

Millions of listeners depend on Morning Edition and Up First to set the news agenda to start their day. We deliver the latest national and international news stories paired with analysis to put headlines into context. Morning Edition is a platform for accountability through interviews with government officials and decision makers who make or influence policy that affect people's lives. The show also features culture stories about music, movies and books that bring joy and provoke thoughtful conversations about who we are in this world.

The right candidate for this position is committed to daily news, and is eager to deliver the freshest, most important stories to listeners. They put the needs and wants of audiences first. They believe in the mission of public media.

As the Overnight/Live Broadcast Supervising Editor, you will join a team of managers who collaboratively lead news and editorial coverage of events in the U.S. and around the world for Morning Edition and Up First. You ensure that the show is at the leading edge of the conversation across a range of issues. Most importantly, you work directly with our hosts to edit and make final changes to the show before and while it is live on air to ensure we are broadcasting our best journalism and editorial work.

Duties for this position include assigning stories and segments to hosts, producers and editors; editing show scripts, crafting live coverage and breaking news plans; leading the control room during the live broadcast; finding guests and reporters to feature on the show when needed; monitoring news and responding with show coverage plans as needed; mentoring and editing producers’ and editors’ writing for stories and show segments; managing staff work schedules as emergencies arise; coordinate and collaborate with other newsroom editors, leaders and journalists on show coverage plans, projects; upload editorial standards and ethics as the lead show manager during your shift. As a manager, you will be assigned direct reports and are expected to evaluate and develop staff.

This is an overnight position with a shift scheduled from approximately 11:30pm - 8:30am Eastern Time Sunday-Thursday.

Morning Edition is a 24/6 news operation. Successful candidates can work holidays and may be asked to temporarily change their work schedule to cover other show shifts and special assignments as needed.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff are defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.    

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead the show production team in bringing the live radio show and podcast to air, including the most listened to segment that airs during the 7a ET hour
  • Manage the editorial operation of the control room during the live broadcast
  • Coordinate with teams for live updates for later news feeds
  • Work directly with show hosts, guests and reporters to prep, record and edit live and taped interviews for the show and podcast on a tight deadline
  • Line edit various scripts for the live show while maintaining NPR’s editorial standards for all parts of the final product
  • Make editorial, programming and news judgment decisions about edits and show coverage plans, especially during breaking news situations
  • Provide written and verbal editorial feedback to staff on work
  • Evaluate, develop, and manage staff performance
  • Collaborate with multiplatform news teams to maximize reach of show content
  • Participate in the hiring of individual staff
  • Cultivate, promote and advance diversity, equity, and inclusion in one’s work and in the workplace.
  • Demonstrated awareness of intersectional identities and ability to collaborate with people from diverse backgrounds
  • Other duties as assigned

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • At least 3  years of experience managing direct reports in a newsroom or operation
  • At least 5  years of experience writing and editing broadcast journalism content
  • At least 5 years of experience producing daily news journalism content for a national or international news organization

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with audio production and mixing techniques
  • Experience working in a live control room
  • Experience being the lead producer or editor for a radio or podcast show 
  • Experience editing news content for various platforms
  • Familiarity in another written language other than English, such as Spanish or Mandarin

Bachelor's degree or equivalent in work experience.

On-site: This is an on-site role based in Washington, DC .

  • Proficiency in people management skills such as delivering constructive feedback, clear communication and conflict resolution.

job.title: Senior Data Insights Analyst, Mobile App
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Deadline:

Please submit your application by 5:00 pm EST on October 23rd, 2026

Intro to Position

You will be critical to building a new, leaner, audience-centric, data-driven app that serves NPR and partnering stations in multi-modal formats. As the Senior Insights Analyst, Mobile Analytics, you will drive data-informed decision-making for the NPR App, serving as the core owner of platform experimentation and advanced mobile product analytics.

Central to this role is high-level SQL mastery. You will extract actionable insights from complex, unaggregated datasets—frequently writing advanced queries (e.g., raw GA4 and Firebase exports in BigQuery) for deep cohort, behavioral, and retention analyses. Additionally, you will establish quality control standards for SQL execution across the team, train colleagues on query optimization, and design end-to-end A/B tests that expand weekly audiences, deepen listening habits, and maximize revenue yield.

This role reports to the Audience Insights Senior Manager, Product.

This is a union-represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with NABET-CWA DMU.

Responsibilities

  • Advanced SQL & Raw Data Engineering: Write, optimize, and QC complex SQL queries using BigQuery; transform raw event logs, access nested arrays, and perform advanced cohort, pattern, and behavioral analysis across app and web platforms.
  • Experimentation Ownership: Lead the experimentation lifecycle on NPR’s owned and operated platforms using Optimizely (or comparable tools); partner across teams to formulate hypotheses, design rigorous A/B testing frameworks, run experiments, and translate results into product recommendations.
  • Product Insights & Strategy: Deliver foundational trend reporting and deep-dive mobile app analytics to product managers, newsroom leaders, and station stakeholders to advocate for audience needs and guide strategy.
  • Technical Mentorship & Enablement: Share advanced SQL and analytical expertise with teammates; build sustainable self-service insight tools and train cross-functional partners to utilize data effectively in daily decision-making.
  • Data Infrastructure & QC: Streamline scheduled queries, data summaries, and automated pipelines; partner with Data Products to diagnose and resolve tracking anomalies and optimize tool design based on user needs.
  • Workload & Stakeholder Prioritization: Manage incoming analytical requests by evaluating business impact, aligning deliverables directly with departmental strategy and media landscape trends.
  • Culture & Best Practices: Proactively share research tools and insights to cultivate a transparent, data-driven learning culture across NPR and partner stations nationwide.
  • Documentation & Standards: Establish guidelines, data dictionaries, and technical documentation for app, video, and web metrics to ensure organizational reporting consistency.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years of advanced SQL experience: Demonstrated expertise writing complex SQL queries from scratch, querying raw, unaggregated event logs, and utilizing data warehousing environments (e.g., BigQuery, Dataform).
  • Raw Data & Array Manipulation Expertise: Proven ability to fetch, transform, and manipulate complex data structures, taking raw data to create audience cohorts and behavioral pattern modeling.
  • 5+ years of Mobile & Web Analytics: Hands-on experience with app and digital behavioral analytics datasets (e.g., Google Firebase, GA4) across mobile product environments.
  • 2+ years of Experimentation Design: Demonstrated experience formulating, executing, and evaluating A/B and multivariate tests using enterprise platforms (e.g., Optimizely).
  • Data Visualization & Reporting: Expert proficiency in converting complex SQL outputs into clear visual stories (Looker, Tableau) and advanced spreadsheet models (Excel/Google Sheets) for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Stakeholder Enablement & Training: Proven track record of training partners on data tools, establishing self-service frameworks, and mentoring peers on SQL and data hygiene best practices.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience within digital news media, public broadcasting, or media streaming platforms.
  • Statistical modeling proficiency using scripting languages such as R or Python.
  • Demonstrated success in building cross-functional partnerships to solve complex, multi-departmental analytical problems.

Required Skills/Competencies

  1. Advanced SQL & Raw Data Extraction: Exceptional ability to write efficient SQL to unnest arrays, parse JSON/struct fields, and build scalable datasets from raw event-level digital behavior.
  2. Experimental Methodology: Deep competency in A/B testing design, statistical significance testing, hypothesis formulation, and post-test behavioral analysis.
  3. Data Translation & Communication: Mastery in presenting quantitative findings to executive, technical, and non-technical audiences with clarity and actionable strategic connections.
  4. Technical Mentorship: Demonstrated dedication to elevating team-wide technical capabilities through SQL code reviews, documentation, and training.
  5. Prioritization & Autonomy: Strong ability to independently navigate shifting priorities, evaluate business impact, and lead complex projects from inception to completion.

Work Location & Requirements

This role is based out of our Washington, D.C. office, but the employee may choose to work on a remote basis from a location that NPR approves. You will have the option of working (a) remotely from a location of your choosing within the United States that is supported by NPR; (b) on-site at an NPR facility, based on the availability of desks and approval from NPR; or (c) a combination of both. Regardless of where you choose to work from, you may be expected to travel to other locations from time to time to perform the duties of your position.

Job Type

Application Instructions

  • Submission Instructions: Please submit a cover letter in addition to your resume answering the following question: How would you describe yourself as an editor?

Intro to Position

The Senior Editor, Editorial Review is part of a critically important team at NPR committed to providing additional editing support to our journalism and our journalists; to ensure that NPR maintains and solidifies its status as a trusted source of news and information for the American public. 

As part of a team, the Senior Editor will review journalistic work from across the Content Division as a final look before air or publication. The focus is on ensuring excellence, fairness, accuracy and consistency of individual work and work across platforms, recognizing that formats, story selection and story-telling techniques for different platforms will and should vary, in service of specific audiences. 

The ideal candidate is an  experienced journalist and editor with wide-ranging editorial experience, including expertise across different platforms and subject matter. They must be deeply curious, open-minded and flexible; be skilled at editing in a large, complex media organization where the topics and journalists vary greatly and where the deadlines and volume of content can be intense. 

This editor will work a Sunday through Thursday shift, for the general hours of 10 a.m. to 7 p.m., although some flexibility is required for breaking news. 

This role is an on-site role based in Washington, DC. The editor will be required to work onsite at a frequency set by their manager. There will be some flexibility to work remotely on occasion with manager approval. 

This is a union-represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with SAG-AFTRA. 

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff are defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events. 

Responsibilities

  • Edit journalistic content for accuracy, fairness and consistency, as a final editorial review before air or publication. The level/kind of review will vary depending on the type of work it is, for what platform and the circumstances surrounding it; for example, is this a breaking news situation or a long-term enterprise story?
  • Copy edit digital news stories, breaking news, long-form features and multiplatform pieces, digital videos for grammar, general factual accuracy, as well as AP and NPR style.
  • Determine what kind of additional editing may be needed for specific stories, depending on their complexity or subject matter, and depending on what kind of review has already been done by legal, standards and practices editors or others. 
  • Collaborate closely with the main editors for all content you’re reviewing, as well as with the show/platform leads for which this content will appear. 
  • With guidance from the Managing Editor or Deputy Managing Editors for Editorial Review, understand the expected content coming through for review on a day-to-day basis so as to effectively manage your workflow.
  • Work closely with the Managing Editors for News and Planning and the newsroom Deputy Managing Editors who are managing both coverage planning and breaking news coverage so that your work is integrated with theirs, and you can effectively work as partners. 
  • Work closely with the Managing Editor for Standards and Practices and other leaders to develop guidance on editorial matters and best practices for the division. 
  • Review and understand data provided by content analysts about the division’s collective body of work and the review team’s impact on it; act on the findings as appropriate.  

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

  • At least 8 years of distinctive, original news reporting or editing experience on a national level.
  • Demonstrated experience editing on multiple platforms and a familiarity with the different audience needs of individual platforms.
  • Demonstrated excellence in editing breaking news, explanatory journalism and feature stories. 
  • Excellent communication skills and a track record of working on collaborative projects.
  • Proven experience in editorial decision-making.
  • Ability to handle multiple and complex projects simultaneously under stringent timeframes, with changing priorities/conditions.
  • Ability to work quickly and efficiently under deadline pressure.
  • Demonstrated commitment to data analysis and its use in understanding the division’s work and in service of audiences. 
  • Deep understanding of NPR’s core values and public service mission.
  • Passion for connecting with diverse audiences on a range of platforms.
  • Proven ability to consistently work well with others.
  • Positive approach to embracing change.
  • Well-developed interpersonal skills, ability to get along with diverse personalities.
  • Ability to respect input but ultimately be confident enough to take decisive action and take responsibility for said action.

Education Requirements

Intro to Position

A Software Architect exemplifies technical expertise and excellence at NPR. Working alongside engineering leadership and cross-functional discipline teams, you will guide strategic technology decisions, design scalable solutions, and build robust pipelines, services, and tools that support NPR and our Member Station Network.

In this role, you will lead technology strategy across our most complex engineering initiatives—those impacting multiple product lines, distributed systems, and mobile platforms simultaneously. Responsible for end-to-end architecture from platform services to client applications and downstream data pipelines, you will balance system performance, developer velocity, data privacy, and cost-efficiency to deliver exceptional public media experiences at scale.

Architectural Strategy & System Design

  3. Drive Technology Standards & Evaluation: Conduct technical evaluations for custom builds versus vendor solutions; introduce modern technologies and establish architectural standards across divisions.

Cross-Team Collaboration & Governance

  1. Lead Multi-Team Engineering Initiatives: Provide technical oversight and direction across cross-divisional product roadmaps, project proposals, and OKR planning cycles for multi-team initiatives.
  2. Establish Quality & Code Governance: Conduct architectural proposals and code reviews, providing substantive feedback on system designs, security protocols, workflows, and peer-written software.
  3. Integrate Compliance & Cost Controls: Architect solutions with explicit focus on privacy compliance (GDPR/CPRA), security standards, CDN caching strategies, and cloud cost optimization frameworks.

Operational Excellence & Mentorship

  1. Support Deployment & Operational Resilience: Participate in automated deployments across QA, UAT, and production environments; join the developer on-call rotation to diagnose and resolve critical incidents.
  2. Contribute High-Quality Code: Author documented, resilient code and reusable core libraries aligned with department standards and sprint commitments.
  3. Foster Technical Mentorship & Team Growth: Assist in onboarding, training, and interviewing software engineering staff, advocating for efficient agile processes and inclusive team practices.

  • Proven track record designing high-traffic, resilient distributed systems, RESTful/GraphQL APIs, and client-server integration patterns.
  • Practical experience architecting media playback, streaming protocols, CDN configurations, and cloud infrastructure ecosystems (e.g., AWS or GCP).
  • Hands-on experience integrating data privacy and compliance standards (GDPR, CPRA) alongside cloud cost optimization frameworks in high-availability environments.
  • Demonstrated experience with modern version control systems (Git), continuous integration pipelines, and automated testing frameworks.

Intro to Position

NPR is scaling and maturing our audience engagement practice into a unified, data-driven, cross-platform growth and engagement engine, and lifecycle management is at the center of that transformation. This role owns the lifecycle activation tools, with a mandate to replace manual, campaign-by-campaign execution with scalable, AI-enabled (where appropriate) processes, and their work focuses on key touchpoints of engagement such as email acquisition, repeat engagement and donation conversion/retention. This role works in daily partnership with Data, Editorial, Marketing, Design, Engineering and Product teams with a mission to make every relationship touchpoint personalized, measurable, user-friendly and tied to business outcomes.

This is a union-represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with NABET-CWA DMU. 

Responsibilities

  • Product Strategy & Roadmap Ownership: Lead the product roadmap for NPR's audience lifecycle and martech ecosystem (including Piano.io and Salesforce Marketing Cloud), translating stakeholder requirements into prioritized engineering backlogs.
  • Martech Operationalization & Tooling: Build, configure, and operationalize internal-facing audience activation tools, establishing intuitive self-serve processes, user permissions, and governance guardrails for content and marketing leads.
  • Audience Journey Optimization: Partner with cross-divisional teams to design scalable automation rules and capabilities that enhance the full listener journey—from email discovery and content re-engagement to recurring donation conversion and win-back.
  • Data Integration & Measurement Alignment: Collaborate with Data and Analytics teams to enhance customer data platform (CDP) segmentation, tracking taxonomy, and attribution modeling to measure the direct impact of activation campaigns.
  • Newsletter Product Infrastructure: Drive technical development and platform enhancements for the NPR editorial newsletter suite in close coordination with newsroom and product leadership.
  • AI & Workflow Efficiency Integration: Evaluate and deploy practical, responsible AI and automation capabilities within lifecycle workflows to minimize repetitive manual execution.
  • Diverse Audience Engagement: Support audience diversification goals by designing personalization and segmentation workflows that welcome and sustain cross-generational and diverse audiences across digital touchpoints.
  • Standard Operating Procedures & Enablement: Author product documentation, establish lifecycle governance best practices, and conduct internal training sessions to ensure cross-departmental adoption of activation tools.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • 3+ years of digital product management experience managing complex platforms, with a track record of driving measurable business or audience outcomes.
  • Substantive experience managing enterprise marketing automation platforms, customer data platforms (CDPs), or audience lifecycle suites (e.g., Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Piano.io, Braze, Segment).
  • Demonstrated experience translating complex cross-departmental requirements into structured user stories, technical specifications, and prioritized roadmaps.
  • Proven track record leading technical software migrations, vendor integrations, or enterprise tooling rollouts.
  • Strong background in data-informed product development, including experience with digital analytics, cohort tracking, and structured A/B testing.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience within a media organization, digital publishing company, non-profit, or subscription/membership-driven enterprise.
  • Practical experience implementing AI-enabled automation or algorithmic segmentation within marketing workflows.
  • Familiarity with user privacy regulations, consent frameworks, and modern consumer data compliance standards.

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Systems Thinking: Ability to synthesize inputs from across a federated matrix of stakeholders into a coherent product architecture and execution plan.
  • Internal Tool & Platform Enablement: Deep empathy for internal users, balancing self-service flexibility with structured organizational guardrails.
  • Data Literacy & Attribution: Fluency in customer segmentation logic, data pipelines, retention funnels, and performance reporting.
  • Cross-Functional Influence: Superior written and oral presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical partners.
  • Iterative Problem Solving: Ability to prioritize high-leverage product enhancements and maintain roadmaps through periods of organizational or technical evolution.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Marketing, or related field, OR equivalent practical work experience demonstrating equivalent technical and product management capability.

Work Location & Requirements

  • NPR Remote-Permitted: This is a remote-permitted role. This role is based out of our Washington, D.C. office, but the employee may choose to work on a remote basis from a location that NPR approves. You will have the option of working (a) remotely from a location of your choosing within the United States that is supported by NPR; (b) on-site at an NPR facility, based on the availability of desks and approval from NPR; or (c) a combination of both. Regardless of where you choose to work from, you may be expected to travel to other locations from time to time to perform the duties of your position.

Job Type

job.title: Temporary Senior Brand Lead, Design
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Instructions or Deadline: 

All applicants must submit a portfolio, which will be the primary source of evaluation for this role. Please link to your online portfolio in your application and your résumé.

Please submit your application by 5:00 pm EST October 11th, 2026.

Intro to Position

We are looking for a creative, bold, big-ideas designer to join our fast-paced team of copywriters, designers, strategists, and campaign managers. This individual will apply creative savvy, top-notch design expertise, and brand-building chops to strengthen NPR’s brand and attract new users to its ever-growing portfolio of shows. 

This individual will create brands and marketing campaigns that are seen by millions every day. They will center their work on NPR’s top ambition: To engage younger, more diverse audiences with our compelling editorial programming and first-rate investigative journalism. 

Responsibilities

This individual will: 

Build Brands

  • Conceptualize and create brand systems for new NPR podcasts, programs, products and properties. Elements will include (but are not limited to): Logos, podcast tiles, key art, typography, color palettes, brand patterns, brand guidelines, social media templates, and brand kit packages.
  • Reimagine the brands of existing NPR editorial properties (particularly podcasts) to resonate with younger, more diverse audiences.
  • Create brands that are: 
    • Compelling, by visually expressing the unique ethos and editorial mission of the podcast, program, or editorial property. 
    • Distinctive, by exploring the visual styles of competitors, identifying what sets this product/property apart, and expressing that unique value through design.
  • Carefully consider the NPR parent brand, collaborating with others to create a brand family/hierarchy that makes inherent sense to users.

Build Campaigns

  • Along with the copywriter, conceptualize a unique vision for each campaign, creating and bringing together different elements, including original graphics, copy, content websites, social media, and other marketing materials.

Help develop the overall campaign approach: its art direction and creative concepts

  • Build all campaign assets required for each campaign: digital and social ads, Apple/Spotify art, illustrations, animations, video beginning/end slates, outdoor art, photography, and graphic systems.
  • Pay attention to audience research and user testing, adapting to new insights and applying learnings to your work. 

Brainstorm Big Ideas

  • Actively contribute to team brainstorms, whether in the room or via collaboration tools.
  • Invest in the larger mission of a brand and/or campaign. Share big ideas that shape the product beyond the visual design — brand/campaign concepts, copywriting ideas, campaign tactics/executions, social media extensions, new platform activations, and other out-of-the-box ideas.

Work collaboratively and present your own work

  • Partner closely with copywriters to imagine brand directions and/or campaign visions.
  • Create distinct visual styles based on target audience data, project ambitions, requirements, and limitations — articulated by strategists in creative briefs.
  • Prioritize workload and produce top-notch work within tight budgets and deadlines.
  • Confidently present ideas, creative concepts, and designs to project stakeholders across NPR and the public radio network.
  • Ensure final graphics and layouts are high-quality, align with brand standards, and maintain consistency across brands and campaigns.

Education

  • Bachelor's degree, Design degree, or equivalent in work experience

Required Skills

  • 8-10 years of experience in graphic design and digital advertising. Expertise in branding, typography, key art, illustration, digital, campaign creation, and social media design.
  • Experience creating motion graphics and animation (or a willingness to learn). 
  • Passionate about brands, marketing, and creative campaigns, with a strong grasp of advertising best practices.
  • Adept at working in a fast-paced, constantly evolving, news-driven environment.
  • Opinionated and confident, yet also open and amenable to feedback from stakeholders and team members. Ability to interpret the deeper intent behind feedback and find the common ground between differing opinions. 
  • Highly motivated, independent-minded, self-driven, and enthusiastic. Willing to work without the direct supervision of a design/creative director.
  • Experience working closely with copywriters preferred.
  • Able to juggle multiple projects at once. Meets deadlines while paying close attention to details and visual aesthetics.
  • Strong presentation skills, with an ability to read a room and tailor presentations accordingly.
  • Knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite required (Photoshop, InDesign, Illustrator etc.).
  • Keynote and PowerPoint experience required. 
  • Working knowledge of Premiere and/or After Effects is a plus.

Work Location & Requirements
