Overview:

Owns compensation strategy and execution for the company's AI/ML, product, and technology organizations — the highest-stakes, most competitive talent pools in the business. Partners with engineering and product leadership, recruiting, and Total Rewards leadership to design pay structures that win and retain talent in an AI labor market where comp packages move fast and get very large, very publicly.  

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Compensation strategy for tech/AI orgs: Design base, bonus, and equity structures for ML research, applied AI, and core engineering/product roles, including specialized retention and sign-on packages for high-demand AI talent
  • Market intelligence: Track fast-moving AI comp benchmarks (base salary inflation, mega equity grants, competitor offer data) and translate that into internal guidance before the market moves again
  • Leveling & career frameworks: Refine and maintain job architecture and leveling guides for technical ladders (IC and management tracks) that hold up as roles evolve quickly
  • Executive & critical-talent comp: Structure offers and retention packages for senior technical leaders and other business-critical hires, including complex negotiations
  • Equity strategy: Partner with Legal/Finance on equity plan design, refresh grant strategy, and dilution management specific to tech talent pools
  • Cross-functional partnership: Act as the trusted comp advisor to engineering/product VPs and recruiting leaders — fast turnaround on offer construction, counter-offer strategy, and internal equity checks
  • Program governance: Ensure pay equity, compliance, and consistency across the technical org as it scales, while staying flexible enough to move at hiring speed

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • 12+ years in compensation, with meaningful time designing comp for AI/ML or high-growth technical orgs at a large or high-growth tech company
  • Direct experience with the current AI talent market — comfort with unconventional, large, or fast-negotiated packages
  • Strong quantitative/analytical background; fluent in comp modeling, market data tools (Radford, Aon, etc.), and equity mechanics

 

Additional Qualifications:

  • Track record advising senior technical and product leaders directly, not just running programs from a distance
  • Executive presence — able to say no to a VP or push back on a comp ask with data, not just process

Overview:

CBS News is seeking a WGA Planning Producer to help direct and manage our streaming network’s daily coverage line-up. From scheduling correspondents and camera positions to coordinating live interviews and future-event logistics, and jumping in during breaking news, this role is a key part of our live programming team and reports to the Editorial Director. This is a New York-based position that is covered under the Collective Bargaining Agreement with the WGA-E.   The ideal candidate has a demonstrated ability to coordinate with editorial leaders and live-show producers, as well as newsgathering stakeholders, field producers and correspondents, to ideate, plan and bring to air same-day and future coverage. The planning producer will collaborate with production and publishing units across streaming, network news and digital, and will also be a point of contact working with partners as well as Paramount Global properties.   As a hardworking journalist, the producer is equally interested in domestic and international news, and thrives on organization and attention to detail. You enjoy working in a fast-paced news environment, pitching original ideas daily, researching segments and pre-producing special coverage, and rising to the occasion during breaking news events.  

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Coordinate with assignment desk, booking team, show producers, domestic and international bureau editors on the planning of day-to-day programming and major news events
  • Identify and pitch stories with high potential for compelling and comprehensive live video storytelling, including day-of-air, special and feature segments
  • Identify key events for future coverage planning
  • Collaborate with digital reporters to develop original segments based on their reporting
  • Gather and flag elements during breaking news as needed
  • Contribute to the streaming network’s news event and coverage calendar
  • Communicate coverage plans to streaming-network and broadcast stakeholders
  • Work closely with the Editorial Director and Senior leadership team to plan coverage for live events & specials

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years work experience in either a broadcast or streaming television newsroom, ideally at the national level with some segment producing experience
  • Hands on newsroom experience scheduling correspondents, booking studios, and gathering elements during breaking news
  • Fluent and knowledge of current events, politics and pop culture
  • Availability to work all shifts, including early morning, nights, weekends and holidays, on short notice and as coverage needs require, as this is a 24-hour news operation

 

Additional Qualifications:

  • Basic understanding of control room operations
  • Ability to communicate with anchors, correspondents and producers in the field
  • Familiarity and working knowledge of digital video production-related techniques and online content management
  • Knowledge about social media and the competitive digital news environment
  • Familiarity with ENPS & iNews

job.title: Yield Manager, Yield Analytics
job.description:
#WeAreParamount on a mission to unleash the power of content… you in?
We’ve got the brands, we’ve got the stars, we’ve got the power to achieve our mission to entertain the planet – now all we’re missing is… YOU! Becoming a part of Paramount means joining a team of passionate people who not only recognize the power of content but also enjoy a touch of fun and uniqueness. Together, we co-create moments that matter – both for our audiences and our employees – and aim to leave a positive mark on culture.

 

Overview:

Does the task of optimizing the revenue potential of one of the largest media organizations in the world excite you? Do you possess the self-belief to make hard decisions? If so, please consider applying for the Yield Manager position in Paramount’s Yield Management group. The goal of the Yield group is simple: grow revenue not simply by selling more, but rather by selling more productively. The Yield Team reports into the Head of Programmatic and Yield.   Yield brings analyses and insights to people at all levels of the Paramount organization, but its core responsibilities revolve around how inventory is measured, packaged, and priced. The Yield team helps the sales team shape individual proposals and keeps track of how those proposals collectively consume inventory. Every month this translates into an inventory puzzle with billions of individual pieces, and by guiding how these pieces are assembled, the Yield team contributes to the overall revenue growth of Paramount.   To the applicant, the role offers the following: The Yield Manager works with a diverse group within the company and has the opportunity to work on projects that cross departments and functions. Yield Managers are relied on as subject matter experts, and contribute to projects with significant visibility.  

Responsibilities include but not limited to:

  • Help shape sales proposals by providing input on product mix, inventory availability, and pricing.
  • Monitor and optimize active campaigns.
  • Provide ad hoc reporting to senior management. This involves writing SQL queries for large data sets to identify business critical KPIs and building reports and dashboards directly from the data warehouse.
  • Work with client services, integrated marketing, and ad operations to inform product strategy.
  • Streamline business processes to mitigate problems that lead to revenue losses.
  • Develop go-to-market pricing and inventory strategy for tentpoles such as March Madness, VMAs, Grammy’s, Paramount+ Originals and many others.
  • Stay informed of marketplace trends (streaming, DTC, measurement, CCPA) and apply learnings to strategy for emerging lines of business
  • Involvement in Paramount vast array of products - Paramount+, Pluto, CBS News Digital, Sports HQ, and ETLive
  • Develop new and effective ways to monitor and report on highly complex digital media inventory.
  • Test and implement creative strategies to optimize the performance of client-specific campaigns.
  • Dive deep into our data to discover potential revenue opportunities, diagnose revenue-impacting issues and provide recommendations to senior leaders.
  • Partner with teams across the company to provide analysis that will impact the way our key brands look, function, and generate revenue.
  • Build, maintain and enhance our ad sales financial models as our business evolves.

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • 2+ years related work experience. Extraordinary candidates with less experience will be considered.
  • BS/BA degree in a quantitative/problem solving field, or equivalent training and experience

 

Additional Qualifications:

  • Solid Excel/Google Sheets & PowerPoint/Google Slides skills
  • SQL experience
  • Experience with DoubleClick/GAM, YieldEx, Operative, Omniture, Google Analytics, Freewheel, Data Studio, Tableau, Nielsen, or Comscore
  • Solid interpersonal skills
  • The ability to collaborate successfully within the Yield Team as well as engage seamlessly with stakeholders across all of Paramount is essential to success
  • Candidates should display both a natural curiosity and a talent for finding the signal through the noise

 

Paramount Skydance Corporation (NASDAQ: PSKY) is a leading global media and entertainment company that creates premium content and experiences for audiences worldwide. Driven by iconic studios, networks and streaming services, Paramount's portfolio of consumer brands includes CBS, Showtime Networks, Paramount Pictures, Nickelodeon, MTV, Comedy Central, BET, Paramount+, and Pluto TV, among others. Paramount delivers the largest share of the U.S. television audience and boasts one of the industry's most important and extensive libraries of TV and film titles. In addition to offering innovative streaming services and digital video products, the company provides powerful capabilities in production, distribution and advertising solutions.

 

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

 

Hiring Salary Range: $80,000.00 - 90,000.00. 

 

The hiring salary range for this position applies to New York City, California, Colorado, Washington state, and most other geographies. Starting pay for the successful applicant depends on a variety of job-related factors, including but not limited to geographic location, market demands, experience, training, and education.  The benefits available for this position include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) plan, life insurance coverage, disability benefits, tuition assistance program and PTO or, if applicable,  as otherwise dictated by the appropriate Collective Bargaining Agreement.  This position is eligible to earn sales incentive compensation. 

 

What We Offer:
  • Attractive compensation and comprehensive benefits packages. Check out our full list of benefits here: https://www.paramount.com/careers/benefits
  • Generous paid time off.
  • An exciting and fulfilling opportunity to be part of one of Paramount’s most dynamic teams.

  • Unique opportunities to make meaningful connections and build a vibrant community, both inside and outside the workplace.

From the programming and movies we create to employee benefits/programs and social impact outreach initiatives, we believe that opportunity, access, resources and rewards should be available to and for the benefit of all. job.title: Senior Accountant
job.description:
Join a team of proud, passionate, and caring people that together share their diverse talents and backgrounds to serve our members and grow the game of golf. Being at the PGA of America means you are supported, respected, and appreciated for your contributions.

The Senior Accountant provides comprehensive accounting and financial support to PGA of America Section offices by maintaining accurate and complete general ledger records, managing month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close activities, preparing financial statements and management reports, and supporting budget planning and variance analysis. Serving as a trusted financial partner to Section Executive Directors and staff, this role provides guidance on accounting policies, financial procedures, reporting, and internal controls; leads the onboarding of new Sections into the Section Financial Program; trains Section Accountants; supports process improvement initiatives; and serves as the primary backup for assigned Sections.


RESPONSIBILITIES (Specific areas of responsibility include but are not limited to):

  • Responsible for the monthly financial close by preparing account reconciliations, submitting journal entries and working with Sections to obtain relevant information.
  • Manage monthly, quarterly, and annual close activities for assigned PGA of America Section offices.
  • Track fixed assets and review depreciation schedules.
  • Serve as a financial resource and business partner to Section Executive Directors and staff.
  • Prepare timely and accurate financial statements, management reports, and other financial analyses.
  • Review financial statements with Section Executive Directors and explain trends, variances, and opportunities for corrective action.
  • Work with accounts payable and accounts receivable to ensure processing is timely and accurate.
  • Train and coach Section staff on accounting processes, policies, procedures, and financial reporting tools.
  • Assist Sections with the preparation, review, and monitoring of annual operating budgets.
  • Support the onboarding and implementation of new Sections entering the Section Financial Program.
  • Lead or contribute to special projects, departmental initiatives, and cross-functional process improvements.
  • Serve as the primary backup for assigned Sections and provide coverage during staff absences or periods of increased activity.
  • Bring forward ideas that enhance efficiency, consistency, service delivery, and the overall Section experience.
  • Develop and implement methodologies to improve the tracking, analysis, and reporting of financial and performance metrics.
  • Proactively identify issues, recommend solutions, and add value to the department, colleagues, and Section offices.

INCLUSION:

Contribute to a respectful and inclusive team environment by welcoming and respecting others’ beliefs, backgrounds, identities, abilities, and individuality to help ensure a supportive and engaging experience for Association Members, partners, customers, and guests. PGA of America respects the uniqueness of each employee and offers everyone the means to find their place and thrive.


SHARED VALUES:

SUPERVISION:

No supervisory responsibilities.  


FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY:

No financial responsibility.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Bachelor’s Degree (B.A.) in Accounting or Finance.
  • Five (5) years of progressive accounting experience, including general ledger experience.
  • Strong knowledge of month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close processes.
  • Workday Financials experience is strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting multiple entities, departments, or business units is preferred.
  • Google Suite experience is preferred.

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE AND ABILITIES: 

Must have knowledge of accounting principles, practices, financial reporting, and financial information systems. Must have the ability to apply strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills when interpreting accounting policies, regulations, and related guidance. Must have the ability to maintain the confidentiality and security of sensitive financial and organizational information. Must have the ability to provide effective financial support to three to four PGA of America Sections while managing competing priorities and deadlines. Must have strong written and verbal communication skills, along with the ability to explain financial information clearly to both financial and non-financial stakeholders. Working knowledge of Gmail, Google Drive, Google Sheets, and Google Docs. Basic fluency in artificial intelligence (AI) tools and concepts. This includes using AI to enhance business operations and drive innovation, enabling us to better serve our Members and stakeholders.

job.description:

You will report to the Senior Manager of Marketing Analytics.


Where You'll Work

  • This role is remote; job seekers must reside in one of the following states to be considered: Ohio and Kentucky
  • This role may require you to be on site at our West Chester, Ohio Corporate Office as needed.

What You'll Do

This is a multi‑faceted individual contributor role with responsibility for the following key areas:

  • Day‑to‑day measurement support for Paid Media and Email Labs, partnering with brand and channel leads to design tests, validate methodologies, measure incremental impact, and translate results into clear business implications.
  • LiftLab Media Mix Modeling measurement support, including data integrity validation, modeling support, and reporting to inform optimization of marketing spend across four brands representing over $100MM in annual media investment.
  • Measurement and analysis of Customer, Channel, and overall Marketing Mix programs, with a focus on understanding impact on customer file health and other key performance indicators.

The Marketing Analyst collaborates closely with Paid Media, CRM, Transformation Lab Members, and external agency partners.


What You'll Bring

  • Three years of digital advertising experience preferred
  • Strong understanding of Google and Meta platforms
  • Strong understanding of CRM programs like Email and SMS
  • Ability to gather and analyze data and create reports
  • Prior experience with marketing platform variant testing design and analysis
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to articulate ideas clearly and effectively.
  • Highly organized with strong project management and time management
  • Strong analytical, planning, modeling, forecasting and research skills, with the ability to interpret data, draw insights and make data-driven decisions.
  • Demonstrated understanding of core Digital Marketing and CRM KPIs, including how they connect business and financial outcomes.
  • Strong analytical foundation with familiarity in testing, incrementality measurement, and marketing effectiveness best practices.
  • Ability to translate complex analyses into clear, concise, and compelling narratives for non‑technical and executive audiences.
  • Strong communication skills with the confidence to present insights, influence stakeholders, and challenge assumptions using data.

  • Comfort working with ambiguous problem statements, evolving data, and imperfect information while exercising sound analytical judgment.
  • Advanced skills in Excel, SQL, Power BI, or other data analysis and visualization tools, with demonstrated competence in data analysis and modeling.

job.title: Assistant Professor of Creative Production (Tenure-Track)
job.description:
Assistant Professor of Creative Production (Tenure-Track)


Job No: 541508
Work Type: Full Time
Location: Main Campus (Gainesville, FL)
Categories: Communications/Public Relations/Marketing, Education/Training/Instructional Design, Information Technology
Department: 23030000 - CJC-MEDIA PROD, MGMT, TECH

Job Description

Classification Title:

AST PROF

Classification Minimum Requirements:

- A terminal degree (MFA, PhD, or equivalent) in film, media production, or a related field by August 2027
- A strong record of creative achievement, such as award-winning films, documentaries aired on network or streaming services, VR experiences showcased at SIGGRAPH, or new media installations.
- Evidence of teaching/mentoring effectiveness
- The candidate should demonstrate their potential in establishing a national and/or international reputation.

Job Description:

The Department of Media Production, Management, and Technology (MPMT) in the University of Florida's College of Journalism and Communications seeks to hire a tenure-track Assistant Professor with a demonstrated record of creative production to begin Fall 2027.

We seek a dynamic scholar/practitioner whose creative output advances storytelling through innovative media formats. We value candidates who push boundaries in media innovation and foster content that addresses contemporary social issues, cultural narratives, or technological disruptions.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate excellence in creative production while maintaining industry connections. Areas of expertise may include feature-length and short films, television series and specials, documentary filmmaking, emerging technologies such as augmented reality (AR) or virtual reality (VR), streaming series development and production, or hybrid formats that blend narrative with interactive elements. This role emphasizes a robust portfolio of creative work—such as films, documentaries, series, or interactive projects—alongside teaching and service contributions.

The MPMT department recognizes the critical importance of creative tenure tracks where artistic output is valued as highly as traditional scholarly research. Tenure evaluation will prioritize impactful creative scholarship, evidenced by honors and awards at nationally recognized film festivals, publications in creative outlets, peer-reviewed exhibitions, grants from bodies like the National Endowment for the Arts, or collaborations with industry leaders.

Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate courses in media production (for example, filmmaking techniques; camera and lens systems; documentary storytelling; VR/AR production; streaming content creation; mentoring students in hands-on projects; supervising capstone productions) and integrating emerging technologies into the curriculum. Candidates are expected to maintain an active agenda of original creative work, secure external funding, and disseminate outputs through festivals, broadcasts, online platforms, or academic conferences. Service duties include department and college committees, advising student media organizations, and contributing to college initiatives and other duties as assigned.

About the Department of Media Production, Management, & Technology

The Department of Media Production, Management, and Technology is one of the premier programs in offering courses related to mass media and emerging media. Our curriculum prepares students for the media industry through two specializations: Digital Film and Video Production, and Media Management and Technology. The department has about 500 student majors and 16 full-time faculty. Students from the department pursue careers in film production, TV program production, social media management, brand management, consumer analysis, UI/UX design, and digital marketing, among others. https://www.jou.ufl.edu/mpmt/

About the College of Journalism and Communications

We are recognized as a national leader in communication scholarship and professional skills development. Be part of an ambitious, progressive, and collaborative program at one of the top public research universities in the United States.

Accredited by ACEJMC, the college has earned its reputation for excellence over the last half-century on the strength of its programs, faculty, students, and alumni; the stories they tell; and the difference they make around the world. With over 70 full-time faculty members and 175 part- time instructors serving in four academic departments— Advertising; Journalism; Media Production, Management, and Technology; and Public Relations —we enroll about 2,500 undergraduates both in-person and online. Additionally, more than 700 graduate students are earning master's and doctoral degrees.

The College of Journalism and Communications offers multiple research and teaching environments, including the Atlas Lab for social media listening; the Consortium on Trust in Media and Technology; the STEM Translational Communication Center; the Center for Public Interest Communications; the Media, Effects, and Technology Lab; the Institute for Public Relations; The Agency, a full- service student-run advertising and public relations agency; the Innovation News Center; Division of Media Properties; and more. The College is highly involved in UF's AI Initiative. https://www.jou.ufl.edu/

About the University of Florida

Our university ranked in the top 6 among public universities, in the top 28 overall, and as the number 1 in online undergraduate programs by the 2024 U.S. News and World Report. UF continues to expand its faculty ranks and the impact of its research and curriculum. UF faculty members annually generate more than $1 billion in research expenditures, with a comprehensive long-term AI initiative (https://ai.ufl.edu/about/) and access to state-of-the-art infrastructure, including one of the most powerful supercomputers in the U.S.

The University of Florida is a member of the Association of American Universities and is categorized in the Carnegie Commission's top tier of research universities. UF has a student body of more than 60,000 who come from all 50 states in the United States and more than 100 countries. The university and greater Gainesville communities enjoy a number of different cultural events, restaurants, year- round outdoor recreational activities, and social opportunities.

he University of Florida is situated in north-central Florida, a region renowned for its abundant natural beauty. Gainesville is within a two-hour drive of Tampa, Orlando, Jacksonville, the Atlantic Ocean, and the Gulf of Mexico.

About Gainesville

As home to Florida's largest and oldest university, Gainesville (http://cityofgainesville.org (http://cityofgainesville.org/)) is one of the state's centers of education, medicine, cultural events, and athletics. Gainesville and the surrounding area is home to about 250,000 people, a robust arts community, several museums, a world-class health care system anchored at UF, a downtown core known for its restaurants and brew pubs, excellent public and private schools, and abundant nature exemplified by clear, natural springs. Additionally, within 2 hours are attractions such as Disney World, Universal Studios, Busch Gardens, and historic St. Augustine. Explore Gainesville in 60 Seconds. (https://www.youtube.com/watch? v=e_7nUKAFanM)

UF Benefits

At the University of Florida, you will not only find competitive salaries, but you'll enjoy elevated benefits and leave options, tuition assistance programs, and stability and support with opportunities for advancement and career growth that only UF can offer. To view the university's Total Reward benefit package, please click here, https://benefits.hr.ufl.edu.

Expected Salary:

Commensurate with experience and education

Required Qualifications:

- A terminal degree (MFA, PhD, or equivalent) in film, media production, or a related field by August 2027
- A strong record of creative achievement, such as award-winning films, documentaries aired on network or streaming services, VR experiences showcased at SIGGRAPH, or new media installations.
- Evidence of teaching/mentoring effectiveness
- The candidate should demonstrate their potential in establishing a national and/or international reputation.

Preferred:

Expertise in software such as Adobe Premiere, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, Unity for VR, or data-driven tools for audience engagement; experience in streaming series productions; screenings or selections at mid-major or major film festivals; familiarity with ethical considerations in AI-assisted production or sustainable filmmaking practices. Experience teaching at the university-level.

Special Instructions to Applicants:

Submit: cover letter (be creative in explaining how your unique talents, creative vision, and professional experiences will advance MPMT's mission of valuing creative output as scholarship, enhance our curriculum, and benefit our students)

curriculum vitae; portfolio links or samples of creative work (e.g., reels, scripts, VR demos); teaching statement; evidence of teaching effectiveness; and contact information for three professional references.

job.title: Career-track Teaching Professor or Clinical Professor (Content Creation)
job.description:
Career-track Teaching Professor or Clinical Professor (Content Creation)

Description
The Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication at Arizona State University-one of the nation's premier professional mass communications programs-seeks a professor to teach and lead within the school's L.A. Content Studio and instruct courses related to media production and content creation.

Hosted in the ASU California Center in Downtown Los Angeles, the Content Studio is an immersive strategic content learning experience in which students activate their multimedia content creation skills to build their own content brands, and work with existing brands to expand their content footprints.

The L.A. Content Studio is one of the Cronkite School's signature professional immersive learning experiences, exemplifying its "teaching hospital" model of education through hands-on learning and faculty mentorship. In the Content Studio, students cultivate their media and audience development skills as independent content entrepreneurs, producing video, digital, social and immersive media content; measuring content performance; and optimizing content strategy. Students work to build (and often monetize) their own independent content brands through YouTube channels, TikTok accounts, Substack newsletters, brand partnerships and more. The program's faculty leader will nurture students' content creation skills, and develop their strategic approach, content measurement skills and audience development acumen.

The successful candidate is an experienced multimedia content creator of the highest caliber with an entrepreneurial spirit and a firm understanding of how to thrive in the creative economy. The candidate must be a creative problem solver who is comfortable in an energetic, dynamic, startup environment while demonstrating a commitment to innovation and collaboration.

As a member of the faculty, the professor will have teaching and service responsibilities within the Cronkite School. In this role, there are no research or creative activity responsibilities.

This is a full-time, benefits-eligible, 12-month appointment based in the ASU California Center in Downtown Los Angeles. It is not a tenure-track appointment. The salary range for this position is $110,000 to $120,000. The professor will hold the rank of assistant, associate or full teaching professor, or assistant, associate or full clinical professor. This is not a tenure-track position.

Essential Responsibilities



- • Teach lower-, upper- and graduate-division courses (four classes in the fall semester, and four in the spring semester)
- • Foster a culture of innovation by harnessing fresh ideas and experimenting with new tools, technologies and techniques that enhance strategic communication and client impact
- • Lead the L.A. Content Studio, an immersive incubator for video, digital and social content creators, and support undergraduate and graduate students in meeting the Content Studio course learning outcomes
- • Teach related courses for graduate and undergraduate learners (the equivalent of four courses each semester, including the Content Studio)
- • Guide students in goal-setting, content strategy and launch/growth for their own content brands, and ideate compelling content guided by those strategies
- • Supervise student content production from conception to completion, for content produced both in the field and in the ASU California Center's production studios, editing rooms and control room facilities.
- • Develop students' content measurement and analytics reporting capabilities, and lead optimization and monetization.
- • Develop and engage clients for the Content Studio across a variety of industries, and lead brand activation and strategy within the course.
- • Foster a learning culture that inspires students with relevant content, tools and techniques that enhance digital storytelling and audience connection.
- • Serve as a disciplinary thought leader, proactively staying abreast of new content creation and strategic communication techniques and technology updates; curating exemplars of superior research and professional work; and highlighting superb student work.
- • Collaborate with leadership, faculty and staff to assess, optimize and develop curriculum
- • Perform service both internally (e.g., committee assignments, student recruitment, thesis direction) and externally (e.g. professional workshops, contest judging, academic/industry leadership)
- • Perform other duties as assigned



About the ASU California Center

At ASU's flagship Los Angeles campus, students can access internships and learning

opportunities only available in a global city, and world-class faculty and innovative media projects only available at the Cronkite School. The California Center hosts the L.A. Content Studio, where students build their own content brands and produce content for existing brands; Cronkite News' L.A. Bureau, where journalism students create award-winning news and sports content; the MA in Narrative and Emerging Media, which develops storytellers specializing in AR, VR and emerging media techniques; and a growing portfolio of learning experiences.

The heart of ASU's California Center campus is the flagship Herald Examiner Building, located at 11th Street and Broadway. Commissioned by William Randolph Hearst and designed by architect Julia Morgan, the building has stood in downtown L.A. since 1914. For decades, the building housed the Hearst Corporation's Herald Examiner newspaper; now, it's home to the L.A. Content Studio, Cronkite News' L.A. Bureau, as well as video/audio editing bays, a broadcast studio, a 3D studio, classrooms, a two-story event space and more.

About the Cronkite School

The Cronkite School is widely recognized as the nation's premier mass communication school. Rooted in the time-honored values that characterize its namesake-accuracy, responsibility, integrity-the school fosters excellence and ethics among students as they master the professional skills required to succeed in the media world of today and tomorrow.

Based on ASU's Downtown Phoenix campus in the heart of the nation's fifth-largest city, the School is known for its hands-on "teaching hospital" approach to learning led by a faculty composed of Pulitzer Prize-winning professional journalists, strategic communication leaders and world-class media scholars. More than 2,500 undergraduate, master's and doctoral students regularly lead the country in national competitions as they prepare for careers in journalism, PR, marketing, strategic media and related communication fields.

About Arizona State University

Arizona State University, ranked the No. 1 "Most Innovative School" in the nation by U.S. News & World Report for 10 years in succession, has forged the model for a New American University. Repeatedly ranked No. 1, ASU has topped more than 20 lists in the last three years: No. 1 in the U.S. for global impact (Times Higher Education) and No. 1 in the U.S. for sustainable practices (Association for the Advancement of Sustainability in Higher Education). ASU is a comprehensive public research institution, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural and overall health of the communities it serves. ASU operates on the principles that learning is a personal and original journey for each student; that they thrive on experience and that the process of discovery cannot be bound by traditional academic disciplines. Through innovation and a commitment to accessibility, ASU has drawn pioneering researchers to its faculty even as it expands opportunities for qualified students, attracting some of the highest-quality students from all 50 states and more than 130 nations.



Qualifications
Required Qualifications



- Candidates pursuing a clinical professor rank must have a master's degree at the time of appointment, and at least 7 years professional experience in strategic communication, or equivalent specialized experience.
- Candidates pursuing a teaching professor rank must have a terminal degree at the time of appointment, and at least 7 years professional/teaching experience in strategic communication, content creation or equivalent specialized experience.



Desired Qualifications

• Demonstrated experience creating strategic content and campaigns for a brand, organization or media outlet with measurable success

• Expertise in content strategy, including goal-setting, audience targeting, funnel strategy, audience measurement, engagement and current approaches

• Exceptional video, digital and social content creation skills in mobile and studio formats

• Experience using native analytics tools and reporting content performance

• Demonstrable video editing ability, including knowledge of Adobe Premiere or equivalent nonlinear software

• Demonstrated leadership and supervisory experience in a content-creating team or role

• Experience cultivating and managing client, brand and/or partner relationships

• Experience working with students in a university, agency or production setting and/or mentoring emerging content creators

• A network of content creators, strategic communication practitioners and related experts who can advise on the field



Application Instructions
Applicants will be asked to create or use an existing Interfolio Dossier to submit the following:

• A cover letter stating qualifications

• Curriculum vitae or resume

• Contact information (name, address, email, telephone number) for three professional references

Successful candidates will demonstrate throughout their materials how their teaching, research, and service will contribute to the fulfillment of the ASU Charter.

The applicant's name should appear in each uploaded file name. Cover letters may be addressed to the Search Committee Chair, senior associate dean Jessica Pucci. Questions about the position should be directed to the search committee chair at: mailto:jepucci@asu.edu

Application deadline is October 29, 2026. Applications will continue to be accepted on a rolling basis for a reserve pool. Applications in the reserve pool may then be reviewed in the order in which they were received until the position is filled



For more information and to apply, visit https://apply.interfolio.com/193795

job.title: DC Based Live Event Producer
job.description:
Producer


Decibel Events | Washington, DC | Full-Time


ABOUT DECIBEL EVENTS

Decibel Events (dB) is a full-service event production and management company based in Washington, DC. We create stunning live events for federal agencies, associations, and corporations throughout the US and abroad, from broadcast-quality general sessions and multi-day conferences to trade shows and city-wide festivals.


Our clients include the Library of Congress, the U.S. Small Business Administration, the Department of War, Trane Technologies, and T. Rowe Price, and some have been with us for more than 15 years. We are experts at what we do. We work side by side with our clients to make every event seamless, and the work we put into preproduction is what our clients see onsite. We are a team of six, so everyone here has a hand in the work and a direct relationship with the client.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a full-time Producer to join our events team, reporting to Eric Bibbs, Senior Producer. You will own each event from the first planning call to the final cue. You'll lead discovery calls with the client, write the proposals, build the paperwork, hire the crew, and lead the team onsite. When the show needs a caller, you'll call it. When we're chasing new work, you'll help us win it. You’ll also support productions in our new Washington, DC studio, helping dB expand its podcast, video and content production capabilities


WHAT YOU'LL DO


Plan

·      Meet with clients to understand their goals, audience, budget, and what success looks like

·      Develop event concepts and production approaches with the client and the dB team

·      Build and manage production schedules and lead regular client calls from kickoff through load-out


Budget and Document

·      Build and manage event budgets, and write proposals, scopes of work, and pricing

·      Create show paperwork: run of show, cue sheets, crew schedules, and labor calls

·      Create or revise ground plans, stage plots, and room layouts in Vectorworks or CAD


Produce

·      Source and manage vendors, venues, and freelance crew, including federal facilities

·      Lead the production team through load-in, rehearsals, show, and strike

·      Call the show when needed, and back up our show callers on large general sessions

·      Support the operation of dB Studios, including podcast, video, virtual and hybrid productions; assist with studio setup, recording, switching, audio, lighting and client sessions as needed.


Grow

·      Mentor our production assistants

·      Lead the after-action review on your events

·      Support new business through proposals, site visits, pitches, and RFP responses


WHAT YOU BRING


Requirements

·      5+ years planning and producing live events, with deep experience in corporate, government, and association events in and around DC

·      Strong knowledge of DC venues, federal facilities, vendors, and labor

·      Experience managing budgets, proposals, vendors, and freelance crew

·      A solid understanding of audio, video, lighting, staging, and content

·      Excellent communication with clients, senior executives, government stakeholders, staff and crew

·      A flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays

·      A valid passport


The X factor

Ever wonder what could set you apart as a candidate? That X factor. These fit the bill, and there could be others. Let your experience shine here and tell us more.

·      Showcalling: you've called shows and can jump in and take the headset

·      Vectorworks or CAD experience

·      A book of business or clients that want to move with you

·      Experience with federal clients or events in secure facilities

·      Experience operating a podcast, broadcast, livestream or video production studio, including familiarity with multi-camera production, audio mixing, lighting, video switching and virtual meeting platforms.


CMP certification

Decibel Events is dedicated to the Certified Meeting Professional (CMP) program. A current CMP is preferred. If you don't have one, Decibel Events pays for the program, and you must earn your CMP within one calendar year of your start date. The experience required for this role should qualify you for the CMP program immediately.


LOCATION AND TRAVEL

Our office and planning work happens in Washington, DC, and we're lucky to have a few local shows. The rest are national and international, so a passport is a must. You must live in the DC metro area or be willing to relocate. This role requires long periods on your feet, climbing stairs and ladders, and lifting up to 50 lbs. This is a full-time position. Freelancers need not apply.


SALARY AND BENEFITS


$100,000 to $135,000, depending on experience.

·      CMP program paid by Decibel Events

·      Medical, dental, and vision stipend

·      Matching 401(k)

·      Flexible time off and paid holidays

·      Up to 2 remote days per week

·      Daily breakfast and craft coffee


HOW TO APPLY


Send the following to careers@decibelevents.com with "Producer" in the subject line:

1.     A 60-second to 2-minute video cover letter (required). Tell us who you are, a show you're proud of, and why you want to work at dB. Send a link, not an attachment.

2.    Resume

3.    Example show paperwork (run of show, cue sheet, budget, or ground plan), with confidential details removed

4.    Sizzle reel or portfolio, with a note on your role in each event

5.    Three professional references

6.    Salary requirements


Applications without a video cover letter will not be considered.

Decibel Events is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

job.title: Executive Producer – The Kim Komando Show
job.description:
Look, most media companies will tell you they’re “a powerhouse.” We actually are one.

The Kim Komando Show reaches millions of people every week across 500+ radio stations, SiriusXM, popular newsletters like The Current, a growing YouTube channel, and a podcast network that keeps expanding. Our audience? Everyday Americans who want to live smarter and safer in a world that changes faster every day. We give them exactly that.

Now we’re looking for an Executive Producer who can help keep that engine running.

What You’ll Actually Do

This isn’t a “manage the calendar and nod in meetings” job. You’re steering editorial. You’re making calls. You’re the reason the show sounds sharp every single week.

Here’s what that looks like day to day:

  • Develop show topics and story ideas that connect tech to what people actually care about: their money, their safety, their family, their time
  • Oversee scripts for broadcast and podcast production from first draft to final cut
  • Write Daily Listener Hacks (DLHs), segment teases, and show notes people actually want to read
  • Manage and support producers so everything runs on time and on point
  • Review callers and place them in the right segments for maximum impact
  • Book and prep guests who have something real to say (not just a PR pitch)
  • Conduct outreach via email, phone, and social media to land the right voices
  • Write podcast titles and descriptions that actually get clicks
  • Update show notes and content on Komando.com
  • Collaborate with the video team on social clips that stop the scroll
What You Bring to the Table
  • Real experience in radio, podcast, TV or digital media production
  • Strong editorial instincts. You know a good story when you see one.
  • Organization skills sharp enough to juggle multiple deadlines without breaking a sweat
  • Experience booking and prepping interview guests (and handling the ones who cancel 20 minutes before air)
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment where things change quickly and that’s just Tuesday
🌟 Why This Job Is Different

You won’t be producing content that disappears into the void. Your work reaches millions of real people every single week. People who take action because of what they heard on the show. That’s not nothing. That’s everything.

You’ll wear multiple hats, pitch ideas that actually get made, and work alongside a team that genuinely loves what they do. No corporate bloat. No investor nonsense. Just a passionate crew building something that matters.

If you’re organized, creative, and ready to help shape how America understands technology, we want to hear from you.

We’d say this job will keep you on your toes. But really, you’ll be so busy producing great content, you won’t have time to sit down anyway.

Come for the career. Stay for the dad jokes.

Salary: $80,000-88,000

job.title: Experiential Events Line Producer
job.description:
Company Description Mother Sauce Creative is a creative and production agency focused on helping clients reconnect with the source of their creativity. The agency is grounded in the belief that art and artists are central to our creative and strategic work.


Role Description The Experiential / Events Line Producer is a contract, remote role responsible for overseeing the planning and execution of live experiential events and press or creator trips from initial concept through post-event wrap.


Day-to-day work includes building and managing production timelines, coordinating pre-production logistics, managing additional production team members as assigned and needed, updating client-facing decks, interfacing with client teams, and supervising event production teams and vendors. This role manages budgets, tracks expenses, and ensures projects meet creative, technical, and operational requirements.


The Experiential Events Line Producer partners closely with the Executive Producer, account, and production stakeholders to maintain clear communication, mitigate risks, and deliver on-time, on-budget events that align with client goals. The role also involves documentation of processes, preparation of call sheets and run-of-show materials, and continuous improvement of production workflows.


Qualifications

  • 5+ Years of line production experience across experiential and events like branded launch events, multi-day pop-ups, and brand trips, including oversight of staffing, scheduling, and on-site execution.
  • Demonstrated budgeting skills, including cost estimating, expense tracking, and financial reconciliation for multi-phase projects of at least 12 projects over a budget of $150k.
  • Proficiency in pre-production planning, including timelines, run-of-show creation, vendor sourcing and coordination, and production logistics.
  • Production management experience, with the ability to manage multiple projects, teams, and vendors in fast-paced settings.
  • Excellent organizational, communication, and problem-solving abilities, with attention to detail and deadlines.
  • Comfort working remotely with distributed teams, using digital collaboration tools and project management platforms.
  • Background in experiential marketing, live events, or creative production; agency or production company experience is beneficial.
  • Ability to work flexible hours based on event schedules; on-site presence at event locations will be required as needed.
  • Ability to work as a local in NYC, if based outside of NYC.


Please include examples of past projects you have managed, the role you held, and the budget level of the project.


Please note: Experience with TV Production, photo & motion production, or live broadcast-style production is not applicable to the experience and background we are seeking for this role at this time.

job.title: Field Producer
job.description:
Rossen Reports is looking for an experienced freelance producer to work closely with Jeff Rossen on retail and shopping videos filmed inside major retailers. We reach more than 4 million subscribers and followers across our digital platforms, helping consumers save money and shop smarter. We’re looking for a resourceful, organized producer who loves retail, shopping, and consumer content.


As we grow, this could evolve into a full-time role for the right candidate.


What you’ll do

  • Research assigned retail stories, including products, deals, price comparisons, and what’s worth buying—or skipping.
  • Verify prices, product details, availability, and other facts before filming.
  • Prepare research notes and organize the products and information needed for each shoot.
  • Work directly with Jeff Rossen in the field, filming on an iPhone and helping bring each story to life.
  • Capture product shots, price tags, demonstrations, and other supporting footage.
  • Coordinate with our production and editing team to deliver organized footage and accurate story notes.


What we’re looking for

  • Prior experience in producing, digital content creation, television, or consumer-focused video.
  • Strong research skills and attention to detail.
  • Comfort filming on an iPhone, with an eye for framing and clean audio.
  • A real interest in retail, shopping, lifestyle, and helping people save money.
  • The ability to move quickly, meet deadlines, and work independently.
  • A collaborative approach and comfort working closely with on-camera talent.


Location and availability

This is a freelance opportunity requiring in-person shoots in South Florida, ideally based near Boca Raton. Candidates must be able to travel to local retail locations.


To apply

Please send a DM. Plus, email your résumé, and a brief note about your producing and shooting experience, location, and availability.



Company Description Rossen Media is the parent company of Rossen Reports, a nationally recognized consumer journalism franchise focused on helping audiences save money, avoid scams, and navigate complex systems. With more than 4 million subscribers across digital platforms and a national broadcast presence, Rossen Media delivers smart, practical, and investigative consumer content to a broad audience. The company is built on credibility, innovation, and strong audience loyalty, making it a trusted source for consumer information. As Rossen Media expands its digital footprint and develops new programming, it is building a next-generation media brand centered on empowering consumers everywhere. Team members join a mission-driven organization that values impactful storytelling and journalistic integrity.

job.title: Guest Booker Producer/Coordinator
job.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

This role will be responsible for identifying, securing, and coordinating guests for the Dan Le Batard Show and the Le Batard and Friends Network. This would include booking prominent figures across the sports industry, friends of the network and news makers.

You will have a deep knowledge of sports, news and culture, exceptional communication skills, outstanding organizational abilities, and, most importantly, an established network of relationships throughout the sports industry. You should already have direct access to athletes, coaches, executives, agents, media personalities, publicists, and other influential figures who can contribute to compelling podcast content.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Leverage an existing network of sports industry contacts to consistently secure high-quality guests.
  • Research and identify new guests that align with the podcast's audience and content strategy.
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with athletes, coaches, sports executives, journalists, broadcasters, agents, publicists, and influencers.
  • Conduct outreach through email, phone, social media, and professional networks.
  • Negotiate guest availability and schedule appearances.
  • Manage a guest pipeline and booking calendar to ensure shows have guest-related content


GUEST BOOKING

  • Confirm recording dates, times, and technical requirements.
  • Provide guests with pre-show information, talking points, and expectations.
  • Coordinate logistics across hosts, producers, and guests.
  • Send reminders and follow-up communications before and after recordings.
  • Ensure all required release forms and permissions are completed.


RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for guests.
  • Deliver a professional, high-quality guest experience.
  • Expand and strengthen the company's network of sports industry relationships.
  • Maintain an organized database of contacts, previous guests, and future prospects.
  • Foster long-term relationships that lead to repeat appearances and referrals.


This role may require irregular hours, weekend work and travel


QUALIFICATIONS

  • Strong research and story development skills, including the ability to identify timely, relevant guests and angles in sports and culture.
  • Experience in talent booking or coordinating guests for podcasts, digital shows, or broadcast content, preferably in a media or entertainment environment.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills for working with talent, representatives, and internal production teams.
  • Proven organizational and time-management abilities, including scheduling, coordinating logistics, and managing multiple projects and deadlines.
  • Familiarity with sports media, pop culture, and current events, and comfort working in a fast-paced, deadline-driven setting.
  • Ability to work collaboratively on-site in Miami, FL, while taking initiative and ownership of booking responsibilities.
  • Professional experience with production tools or workflows (e.g., shared calendars, project management software, call sheets) is beneficial.


Salary: $65,000-$85,000 depending on experience

job.title: Line Producer – Primetime Programming
job.description:
(Benefits include transportation allowance or paid parking option, paid leave and up to 10% matching for 403(b) retirement plan)


GENERAL FUNCTION:

Serves as the lead Control Room Producer for C-SPAN's live, nightly primetime programming and, on occasion, other high-profile live C-SPAN public affairs programming. Responsible for building and managing program rundowns and executing programs live on air in collaboration with the Senior Producer, Hosts and production team.

 

Position requires strong editorial judgment, extensive live control room experience and a deep understanding of national politics, government and public affairs.

 

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Builds, organizes and manages daily program rundowns, including segment placement, interviews, teases, graphics, video, viewer participation and other production elements.
  • Line produces live programs, maintaining timing and pacing and making real-time editorial and production decisions in coordination with the Senior Producer.
  • Works closely with the Senior Producer and Hosts to execute the editorial direction, structure, pacing and flow of each program.
  • Leads coordination of the production team during live broadcasts and communicates clearly with Directors, Hosts, Producers, Associate Producers and Production Assistants in the control room and studio.
  • Responds quickly to breaking news and changing editorial priorities, restructuring rundowns and coordinating new program elements as circumstances warrant.
  • Monitors live events and breaking developments before and during programs and determines, in coordination with the Senior Producer, how those developments should be incorporated into the broadcasts.
  • Writes and edits scripts, opens, teases, guest introductions, transitions and other broadcast copy.
  • Reviews and coordinates video, graphics and other production elements to ensure they are accurate, complete and ready for air.
  • Works with Associate Producers and Production Assistants to coordinate and execute program elements and ensures production deadlines are met.
  • Coordinates viewer participation elements, including calls, texts and other audience interaction, as appropriate.
  • Coordinates with digital and social teams to identify significant program moments and content for distribution across C-SPAN platforms.
  • Helps ensure editorial accuracy and adherence to C-SPAN's standards of fairness, accuracy and balance.
  • Line produces other high-profile live C-SPAN public affairs programming as assigned.
  • Other duties as assigned.

 

BACKGROUND/SKILLS:

  • Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Political Science, Communications or related field preferred.
  • Minimum four years of relevant experience in news or public affairs television, including significant line producing and live control room experience.
  • Demonstrated editorial decision-making experience and strong news judgment.
  • Strong knowledge of and interest in politics, government, Congress and public affairs.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and manage live program rundowns and make sound editorial and production decisions under deadline.
  • Strong writing and editing skills for live television.
  • Ability to respond quickly and effectively to breaking news and changing program circumstances.
  • Strong communication and leadership skills and demonstrated ability to coordinate a production team during live programming.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with Hosts, Producers, Directors and editorial, production and technical teams.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple program elements simultaneously.
  • Understanding of C-SPAN programming and editorial approach, including its emphasis on primary-source video, substantive interviews, viewer participation and nonpartisan presentation.
  • Ability to work effectively under pressure and consistently meet deadlines.
  • Flexibility with hours and workdays, including evenings and weekends as required.

job.title: Program Director
job.description:
Program Director


R0153633
University of Nevada, Reno - Main Campus

The University of Nevada, Reno (UNR) appreciates your interest in employment at our growing institution. We want your application process to go smoothly and quickly. Final applications must be submitted prior to the close of the recruitment.

If you need assistance or have questions regarding the application process, please contact our recruitment helpline at (775) 784-1495 or jobs@unr.edu.

Job Description

Reporting to the General Manager of KUNR/KNCJ Public Radio, the Program Director provides strategic and day-to-day leadership for the broadcast programming and on-air operations of KUNR Public Radio, KNCJ Nevada's Classical and Jazz, and KNCC Elko. This position plays a central role in shaping the station's sound, programming strategy, audience experience, and overall broadcast quality while ensuring that programming meets professional public media standards and FCC requirements. The Program Director leads, coaches, and develops KUNR's full-time and part-time on-air talent and works closely with newsroom and station leadership to strengthen local programming and storytelling across platforms. The position oversees programming systems, broadcast automation, program schedules, network content, and technical audio quality to ensure reliable and seamless service to listeners. The Program Director also serves as an on-air host and participates in fundraising, community events, and other activities that advance KUNR's mission and connection with its audience. This position is well suited for a public media professional who combines strong editorial and programming judgment with leadership, technical aptitude, journalistic integrity, creativity, and a passion for developing people and serving audiences.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to:
• Shape KUNR's sound and programming strategy while balancing local storytelling with high-quality national public media content.
• Develop and mentor on-air talent, helping broadcasters grow professionally and strengthening the overall quality of the station.
• Champion local programming and help identify opportunities for new programs, podcasts, partnerships, and content distribution.
• Work across departments with newsroom, engineering, development, and station leadership to advance KUNR's mission.
• Engage with the community through events, partnerships, interviews, and public media initiatives.
• Help guide the station's future, using audience information, emerging technologies, and evolving public media practices to improve the listener experience.
• Be part of a university environment that connects public media, journalism, education, and service to the Northern Nevada community.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree and four years of professional work experience; OR a Master's Degree and two years of professional work experience

Related experience: On-air broadcasting, news collection, reporting, radio programming, or a closely related media field.

Schedule



- Regular schedule will generally be Monday through Friday and will be determined in part by assigned on-air programming. Current anticipated schedules may include approximately 6:00 a.m.-2:00 p.m. or 10:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m.

- The position requires occasional evening and weekend work for station events, special programming, emergency news coverage, and other operational needs.



Compensation Grade

Administrative Faculty - C

To view the salary schedule for this position, please visit: https://www.unr.edu/hr/compensation-evaluation/compensation/salary-schedules and select Administrative Faculty by Grade. Salary is competitive and commensurate with related education and experience.

Remarkable Retirement

Our retirement plan is beyond compare. Your 19.25% contribution is generously matched by the University. With the faculty retirement plan, you are 100% vested your first day. Sit back and watch your retirement dollars grow! All permanent employees on an annual "A" or "B" contract who are employed at least 50% full-time are eligible to participate in the NSHE retirement program unless they are members of PERS of Nevada.

Perks of Working at UNR



- Health insurance options including dental and vision - https://www.unr.edu/bcn-nshe/benefits/insurance

- Generous annual and sick leave and life insurance - https://www.unr.edu/hr/benefits/leave-and-time-off/faculty

- E. L. Wiegand Fitness Center offers annual or semester memberships and spouse/domestic partner membership options. https://www.unr.edu/fitness/memberships

- https://www.mountaineap.com/ supports employees (and eligible dependents) through life's difficult moments. Mountain EAP is located in Reno and specializes in counseling and advising services for personal or interpersonal issues.

- Faculty Senate is the principal representing body for faculty. Its membership includes representatives from each academic and administrative major unit of the University. https://www.unr.edu/faculty-senate

- No state income tax!



Grants-in-Aid for Faculty Employees

The University is proud to provide a reduced-rate tuition benefit to faculty and qualified dependents. Faculty can take up to six credits per semester at a reduced rate. Dependents of faculty have unlimited credits, but in order to be eligible children must be unmarried and under the age of 24 and must receive at least 50% of their financial support from the employee and/or employee's spouse or domestic partner. https://www.unr.edu/hr/benefits/educational-benefits/faculty

Faculty Dual Career Assistance Program

The University of Nevada, Reno recognizes the importance of addressing dual-career couples' professional needs. We offer a dual career assistance program to newly hired faculty spouses/partners that provides resources and assists them to identify career opportunities in Northern Nevada. https://www.unr.edu/hr/jobs/dual-career-program

Department Information

Contact Information

Sheryl Gann - mailto:sgann@kunr.org

Exempt

Yes

100.0%

About Us

The University of Nevada, Reno is a leading public research university committed to the promise of a future powered by knowledge. Founded in 1874 as Nevada's original land-grant university, the University serves more than 23,000 undergraduate and graduate students from all 50 states and 63 countries.

Classified by the Carnegie® Classification of Institutions of Higher Education as an R1 ("Very High Research") university, it is also recognized in the Carnegie® Community Engagement classification. The University is also ranked by U.S. News & World Report among the "Best National Universities" and "Best National Public Universities." It also ranks in the top tier of the WSJ/Times Higher Education World University Rankings and the New York Times' "Top Colleges for Economic Diversity."

Since 2009, nearly $1 billion has been has invested in advanced labs, facilities, and residence halls on the main campus. The University is home to Nevada's first medical school - the University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine and the Wayne L. Prim Campus at Lake Tahoe, where education, research, and creative work thrive in a stunning mountain setting. The University delivers on its original land-grant mission with outreach across the state through the University of Nevada, Reno Extension, Nevada Agricultural Experiment Station, Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology, Nevada Small Business Development Center, the Nevada Seismological Laboratory, and Wolf Pack Athletics.

The main campus is in Reno, Nevada, a burgeoning global technology hub with a vibrant midtown and downtown. Found where the high desert of the Great Basin meets the High Sierra and Lake Tahoe, the beautiful, 290-acre main campus is also a Nevada State Arboretum. The University's physical infrastructure is expanding with ongoing construction of the newly named John Tullock Business Building, set to open in fall 2025. Groundbreaking is also planned for a new State Public Health Laboratory Building on campus, alongside the recent acquisition of 16 parcels near campus, known as "University Village," to provide affordable housing for graduate students and early career faculty.

Collaborating with world-renowned organizations, the University fosters innovation through initiatives such as the Digital Wolf Pack partnership with Apple, which ensures equitable access to technology for students, providing new incoming freshman or transfer students with an iPad Air and accessories. Google's TechWise initiate is an 18-month program that fully supports undergraduate students in becoming entry-level software engineers by graduation.

In 2023, the U.S. Department of Commerce's Economic Development Administration (EDA) announced that Nevada - led by the University of Nevada, Reno - was named one of the inaugural 31 Regional Technology and Innovation Hubs (TechHubs). Nevada was selected from a competitive pool of 489 applicants from across the United States and its territories. Nevada's Tech Hub will strengthen America's lithium batteries, critical elements and other electric vehicle materials industry sectors within the state.

Through its commitment to high-impact education, world-improving research and creative activity, and outreach that's transforming Nevada's communities and businesses, the University continues its 150-year tradition of benefitting our state, nation and world.

The University recognizes that diversity promotes excellence in education and research. The inclusive and engaged community on campus recognizes the added value that students, faculty, and staff from different backgrounds bring to the educational experience.

Today, the University delivers on its original land-grant mission of access to education and knowledge by investing in the academics, facilities, support, engagement and vibrant campus life that promote our diverse students' cognitive growth and academic achievement - all while remaining one of the best values in American higher education.

For more information, please visit the http://www.unr.edu/.

job.title: Administrative Assistant, KIVI - Boise, ID
job.description:
Are you an organizational powerhouse who thrives on keeping things running smoothly behind the scenes? KIVI is looking for a highly experienced, detail-driven administrative professional to provide advanced, confidential support to our general manager or department head. This is a role where your expertise, discretion, and proactive mindset will directly shape the effectiveness of station leadership — and make a real impact on how we operate every single day. If you bring broad administrative knowledge, a collaborative spirit, and the ability to juggle competing priorities without missing a beat, we want to hear from you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Prepare advanced business presentation documents and spreadsheets.
  • Assist in special projects, perform research and maintain records.
  • Compose correspondence, based on the general knowledge of the manager's view, about administrative matters and general office policies for manager's approval.
  • Prepare recurring reports independently for signature.
  • Answer the phone, provide information and receive information concerning matters related to the department.
  • Schedule and maintain calendar of appointments, meetings and travel itineraries, coordinate related arrangements, and arrange for meeting rooms.
  • Anticipate and prepare materials needed by the manager for conferences, correspondence, appointments, meetings, telephone calls, etc.
  • Prepare and distribute minutes from meetings.
  • Establish and maintain a variety of files and records.
  • May be required to take and transcribe dictation.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Associates degree in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Specialized training/certification may be required
  • Generally, 5+ years of experience in related area of responsibility

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Three to five years related experience and/or equivalent combination of experience and training in the professional discipline of the department.
  • Proficiency with various software programs including Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint for Windows.
  • Above average knowledge of general office practice and business etiquette.
  • Ability to balance multiple priorities and to work under tight deadlines while providing consistent and professional service.
  • Ability to perform secretarial and clerical duties with speed and accuracy without immediate and constant supervision.
  • Good knowledge of business correspondence composition.
  • Accurate and efficient typing skills.
  • Possess above average interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to maintain good working relationships with all co-workers.
  • Possess above average organizational skills including attention to detail and follow through.
  • Maintain complete confidentiality, possess a professional demeanor, and exercise discretion at all times.
  • Be able to work overtime as needed, often with little notice.
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: Boise is one of the West's most livable and fastest-growing cities, offering a rare combination of big-city amenities and easy access to the great outdoors. The Boise River Greenbelt winds through the heart of the city, giving residents a scenic corridor for biking, running, and walking year-round. Bogus Basin Mountain Recreation Area sits just 16 miles from downtown, delivering skiing and snowboarding in the winter and hiking and mountain biking in the summer. Whether you're into river rafting, fly fishing, or simply exploring the trails of the Boise Foothills, adventure is never far from your front door.

Downtown Boise is a thriving hub of culture, cuisine, and community. The famous Basque Block celebrates the city's unique Basque heritage with authentic restaurants, a cultural center, and lively festivals. The local food and craft beverage scene is booming, with award-winning restaurants, farm-to-table eateries, and a growing number of craft breweries and cideries. The annual Treefort Music Festival draws music fans from across the country, and the Boise Contemporary Theater, Treefort, and the Boise Philharmonic give the city a rich arts presence.

Boise is also a proud college sports town, home to Boise State University and the iconic blue turf of Albertsons Stadium. The city consistently earns recognition for its quality of life, safety, and economic opportunity, attracting professionals from across the country who want the energy of a growing metro without sacrificing affordability or a sense of community. It's a place where people put down roots — and love every minute of it.

job.title: Executive Reporter, WTKR
job.description:
WTKR, The E.W. Scripps Company CBS affiliate in Norfolk, Virginia, is seeking an Executive Reporter who will lead our mission to enhance storytelling across all platforms. This is your opportunity to combine your passion for impactful journalism with mentorship, helping shape the next generation of reporters while continuing to tell the stories that matter most to our community.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Lead, develop, and enhance the storytelling skill and abilities of all reporters and MMJs in the station

  • Collaborate with other newsroom leaders to consistently execute the content strategy through authentic, meaningful storytelling

  • Oversee the writing of stories for all platforms; provide timely feedback to foster continuous improvement

  • Develop and supervise effective workflow strategies and procedures for multiple news programs and outlets

  • Ensure that all content adheres to journalistic standards and ethical guidelines

  • Deliver a vision and create trust among reporters, photographers and newsroom staff

  • May provide on-air, multi-platform coverage for breaking news as needed

  • Perform other duties as assigned

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred, or equivalent years of experience

  • Generally, 7+ years of experience in related field preferred

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Demonstrated expertise in storytelling

  • Knowledge and demonstration of editorial judgment, journalistic ethics and libel laws

  • Curiosity for the community, city, state and world we report on daily

  • Deep understanding of the content strategy

  • Ability to work a variety of shifts including nights, weekends, early morning, and holidays

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK AND PLAY:

Norfolk, Virginia, sits at the heart of Hampton Roads, one of the most dynamic regions on the East Coast. As part of the largest naval installation in the world, Norfolk offers a unique blend of military heritage, maritime culture, and coastal living. The city boasts a revitalized downtown waterfront featuring world-class museums like the Chrysler Museum of Art, vibrant dining and entertainment districts, and the beautiful Elizabeth River.

Residents enjoy easy access to miles of beaches, the Chesapeake Bay, and outdoor recreation year-round. The region's moderate climate means you can explore the Virginia Beach Boardwalk, kayak through the Great Dismal Swamp, or catch a show at the historic Attucks Theatre any time of year. With affordable housing, no state tax on groceries, and a thriving arts scene that includes the Virginia Opera and Virginia Symphony Orchestra, Norfolk offers an exceptional quality of life. Plus, you're just a short drive from the Blue Ridge Mountains, Washington D.C., and the Outer Banks of North Carolina.
