job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. The New York Times Shows department is hiring a staff editor to fact check episodes of Hard Fork, both in video and audio formats.

You will work with producers and editors to check facts and assertions, with extra attention to the tone and context in which they're delivered.

You are comfortable working in print, audio and video mediums in a fast-paced news environment. We're looking for exceptional news judgment, an investigator's mind and the ability to dive into unfamiliar material on deadline. And while we value deliberate, careful checking, speed is also important. The fact checker will be part of a small group of producers and editors, so collegiality, diplomacy and a collaborative spirit are a must.

This is a part-time role for 20 hours a week to start. It could scale up over time. You will report to the Executive Producer of Hard Fork.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Check factual assertions in podcast and video episodes to determine veracity and correctness on deadline
  • Check prep documents and listen during live recordings to track facts and assertions to be verified
  • Listen to drafts, checking all facts, noting attribution, and providing guidance on editing or adjusting material as needed
  • Conduct quick and accurate research to gather and verify facts in collaboration with producers, editors and hosts
  • Work to ensure fairness and accuracy; correct contradictions and omissions in consultation with producers, editors and hosts; correct spelling and grammar
  • Check episode descriptions and other copy for video and audio assets. Adjust show print excerpts, transcripts and captions for factual accuracy
  • Check video episode's visuals for factual accuracy and context
  • Exercise news judgment
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 or more years of fact-checking experience
  • Available to work evenings as needed

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Exercise news judgment
  • Quickly identify facts to be checked in a podcast episode transcript
  • Communicate notes & feedback clearly
  • Superb research skills
  • Use data to inform decisions
  • Manage deadlines simultaneously

  • Experience in a deadline-driven environment

job.title: FOIA Editor
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for a FOIA editor to oversee and guide our strategy of using the Freedom of Information Act and other local, state and federal public records laws to obtain information from governmental and public entities.

You will serve as a hub for the newsroom’s public records requests, helping provide resources and guidance to journalists across The Times about how to maximize our ability to obtain information in the public’s interest. You will serve as a consultant to teams on effective tactics, working with reporters and editors at the inception of stories and projects to help integrate FOIA requests early in the process. You will also be responsible for developing story ideas and original coverage through the FOIA process, identifying opportunities to obtain public records that will generate news. You are excited to experiment with new technology and formats and collaborate with our data, visual and product teams to tell stories that resonate with our audience.

You will help track and expedite public records requests by maintaining a centralized database of FOIA requests and appeals, and will work closely with the Legal department to identify efforts that merit litigation support.

This position is based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office each week. The person will also work closely with our bureau in Washington and make periodic visits there. 

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and refine FOIA requests in partnership with internal stakeholders for submission

  • Serve as a consultant for teams as they design public records requests to bolster their reporting, with a priority on integrating such requests early into the process of developing stories.

  • Propose and drive story ideas based on FOIA requests and coordinate coverage across multiple desks 

  • Consult with desks to understand when and how to augment ongoing themes with FOIA requests

  • Advise journalists across the newsroom about the most effective approaches to obtain information through public records laws.

  • Develop and maintain training materials and deliver training about what information can be obtained through the federal Freedom of Information Act and similar state and local statutes.

  • Coordinate, track and help expedite public records requests by maintaining a centralized database of FOIA requests and appeals.

  • Partner with the Legal department in identifying efforts to seek public information that merit litigation support.

  • Represent the Newsroom in partnership with Legal on FOIA matters

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the enterprise OR news research team.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years’ experience at a journalism or media company or other relevant organization.

  • Demonstrated success navigating and resolving legal issues related to public records laws. 

  • A record of collaborating and partnering with colleagues to find innovative storytelling approaches through the use of public records and other legal strategies. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous experience in shaping the public records strategy of a news organization.

  • Conversant in local and state public records laws and practices in addition to the federal statute.

  • Deep familiarity with media law or a law degree 

  • A record of adjusting to the evolving and changing needs of a newsroom

job.title: Graphics Multimedia Editor, Open-source Reporting
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times Graphics team is looking for a reporter with extensive open-source and investigative reporting skills to turn raw evidence into impactful visual stories. You have a track record for uncovering exclusive information off the news.

The Graphics team is a leader in using spatial and visual techniques on investigative stories, and we're looking for someone who is passionate about accountability journalism using cutting-edge reporting techniques.

Below are a few examples of the kinds of stories that you will be a part of:
  • An exclusive look at the failed columns of the Midtown Manhattan near-collapse
  • A 3-D analysis of why firefighters' lines of sight were limited in the deadly LaGuardia Crash
  • An investigation into the mass graves in Syria
  • An investigation into the causes of a Miami building collapse
  • A spatial investigation into a deadly fire in the Bronx
  • A forensic analysis of an apartment building collapse in the Turkey earthquake
Working with journalists on the Graphics team and across the newsroom, you will play an important role in shaping visual reconstructions and investigations that rely on spatial analysis or use 3-D modeling. You will gather and analyze evidence for stories across a wide range of topics for both quick-turn stories as well as longer-term enterprise.

You will be expected to take the initiative in leading major storylines, with the goal of uncovering new or exclusive findings across multiple visual story formats. You should be curious and driven, and be comfortable with moving between solo deep dives and fast-paced, cross-desk collaborations.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days a week.

Responsibilities:
  • Bring core OSINT fluency to the desk's coverage: geolocation, chronolocation, satellite/aerial imagery analysis, audio-video research, and more.
  • Analyze a variety of data sources, including satellite and aerial imagery, flight/vessel tracking data, social media platforms and radio scanner data.
  • Vet and build relationships with a network of sources on stories.
  • Generate ideas that help the team develop custom tooling to automate open-source reporting for analyzing and visualizing evidence.
  • Find new ways to report beyond the standard OSINT toolkit, by using computational techniques, including through machine learning, computer vision and approved AI tools.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to an Assistant Editor on the Graphics desk.
Basic Qualifications:
  • 5+ years of relevant experience as an investigative reporter, open-source researcher or forensic expert.
  • Proven experience conducting open-source investigations by sourcing audio and visual evidence across a variety of platforms.
  • Experience producing accountability journalism, with a strong portfolio.
  • Experience producing clear copy about the visual evidence on tight deadlines.
  • Experience verifying user-generated content from social media for authenticity.
  • Skilled in building timelines using a variety of sources, including official statements and metadata from user-generated content.
  • Familiarity with open-source intelligence tools and techniques like Google Earth, satellite imagery platforms, scanner audio data, flight or vessel tracking, or similar.
Preferred Qualifications:
  • Experience working both independently and collaboratively while managing multiple research threads.
  • Experience with advanced tools for reporting, such as QGIS, Blender for 3-D scene reconstructions, data analysis methods, audio and image forensics tools.
  • Adept at creating clear, visual explainers piecing together complex findings.
  • Familiarity with programming and custom tool development.
  • Familiarity with Adobe Suite and Figma.
  • Experience with web scraping tools and working with APIs.
  • Experience using command line tools.
  • Willingness and flexibility to work evenings and weekends as needed.

job.title: Graphics/Multimedia Editor, Elections Data Developer (Election Analytics)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Election Analytics team produces flagship, standard-setting elections coverage, including the live, election night statistical model known as the Needle and The New York Times/Siena Poll. The department is looking to hire an experienced data developer to contribute to data creation, management and architecture across our products.

Underneath our poll and the Needle are massive amounts of data. This includes the voter file, as well as demographics for different localities, hundreds of scrapers collecting precinct data and countless pipelines for processing and cleaning data. Our understanding of the electorate is only as good as the data we have access to, including the data we create to test our systems and the election night model itself.

You will have a central role in creating and cleaning these data sources for use in our products. You will help knit together data from different sections of the team to build our understanding of what may happen on election night throughout the year. And you will ensure we have proper observability into how data is being used.

Election Analytics is a multidisciplinary team of reporters, developers, statisticians and modelers who work on written coverage, graphics, our polls and the election-night model. This is a highly collaborative role that will involve working with colleagues from Election Analytics, the Graphics department and Interactive News.

This is an in-office position in New York City or Washington, D.C., and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

To apply, you MUST include a cover letter of no more than 300 words that…

  • Explains how you approached a specific instance where you had to balance engineering principles with the need to meet a deadline; and

  • Explains specifically why you are interested in covering elections

Responsibilities:

  • Create test data for the election-night mathematical model and for live election-night Graphics

  • Build and improve pipelines for ingesting, processing, and displaying large data sets, precinct data or absentee files.

  • Build and maintain observability tools for the model that allow for fast debugging on election night and clear monitoring of precinct data entering the model

  • Work with stakeholders to understand the data needs and schema requirements

  • Develop and maintain libraries in R that form the basis of our apps

  • Balance engineering principles with the need to move at the speed of news

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • You will report to the Director of Election Analytics

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of relevant experience

  • Familiarity working with large datasets and with best practices in data management

  • Experience working with data-oriented programming languages, such as R or Python

  • Experience working with cloud computing providers such as Google Cloud Platform or Amazon Web Services

  • Experience working collaboratively with people of different skills and backgrounds

  • Willingness to work a flexible schedule as needed to support coverage of elections and polls

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working with election data

  • Experience developing ETL pipelines, working with orchestration tooling, and ensuring reliability and observability

  • Experience with Google BigQuery or other OLAP databases

  • Experience building productionized apps

job.title: Hollywood News and Awards Reporter, Culture
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Culture Desk is seeking a nimble journalist to report on the movie awards season, and report out news stories and investigations about the consumer-facing side of Hollywood throughout the year.

The position encompasses writing the Projectionist awards season column and reporting live from the red carpet during the Oscars and other awards shows, as well as appearing in videos. But awards season is only part of the job. You will be expected to cover the news and controversies of pop culture throughout the year, deliver investigations and enterprise stories, and write features about the latest releases and how they impact audiences and society. Your work should drive conversations about Hollywood and entertainment both before and after a premiere.

We are looking for someone who is well-sourced in Hollywood, has deep expertise about movie awards and understands both how Hollywood works and how its output can generate larger conversations and controversies. Ideally, the reporter has the ability to cover fast-breaking news of interest to culturally curious readers.

Night and weekend work will be a necessary part of this coverage. The reporter will work in coordination with the Times business reporters who cover Hollywood.

This reporter should be able to brainstorm unique angles and anticipate what moments are worthy of our attention and to find creative ways to engage readers with coverage that satisfies their hunger for news about their favorite actors, directors, series and franchises. The priority for this role is to cover and write news, and would also include deeper profiles. Your stories may take the form of traditional articles as well as explainers, visual- and audio-rich stories, lists, and other story formats. Sophisticated reporting, interviewing and writing skills are a must, along with the ability to contextualize a subject within a larger cultural framework. You will be writing regularly on deadline, so the ability to digest complex information quickly and turn around stories quickly will be essential. This role requires precision and attention to detail.

The ideal candidate has a demonstrated track record of reporting on Hollywood, including breaking news and exclusives, and is collegial, prolific and enthusiastic about covering news. This person should be a collaborator with an affinity for teamwork and a willingness to share expertise and resources.

You will report to our Movies & Pop Culture Editor.

This is an in-office position, based in either New York City or Los Angeles, and includes regular attendance in the office each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Cover the news and controversies of the movie awards season and pop culture, deliver investigations and enterprise stories, and write features about movies and how they impact audiences and society
  • Write the Projectionist awards season column and report live from the red carpet during the Oscars and other awards shows, as well as appearing in videos
  • Collaborate with visual editors on new story formats and multimedia, including reporter video and audio
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10 years of reporting experience in journalism, including breaking news and exclusives
  • Richly sourced in the entertainment industry in Hollywood across movies, television and pop culture
  • Superb communication skills and the ability to collaborate with a large team of editors and reporters
  • Creativity and a desire to experiment with innovative story formats
  • The ability to contextualize news in a broader context for our audiences, and follow with multiple next-day storylines
  • A self-starting go-getter, you must be able to independently source news and exclusives

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A lively, accessible writing style
  • An aptitude and enthusiasm for video storytelling, such as reporting on camera
  • A passion for the mission and values of The Times
  • A willingness to write in a variety of story formats

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, HR Business Partner you will be a primary contact for daily operational HR issues, processes, and coordinating projects for our client groups.

You will balance business-aligned strategic support with rigorous operational execution. You will manage critical operational transactions—including Workday data integrity, position management, auditing, and reporting—to ensure seamless HR operations across all assigned departments. Additionally, you will partner with leadership and HR Centers of Excellence (COEs) on core talent programs. You will operate on a hybrid model requiring 3 days per week in our New York City office.

  • Partner with HRBPs, business leadership, cross-functional partners, and COEs (Total Rewards, Talent Acquisition, Talent Management, ER, Legal, and Labor) to support various people initiatives, e.g. end-to-end performance management, goal setting, and annual compensation cycles.

  • Maintain strict data integrity within Workday by processing transactions (promotions, manager changes, cost center updates, work location changes) and conducting regular audits.
  • Pull reports and reconcile data sets as requested (rosters, anniversaries, attendance), shout outs.

The HRIS Analyst II reports directly to the HRIS Senior Manager and is important for optimizing and supporting Workday Performance, Core HCM, Compensation, HR reporting, and related areas. Primary responsibilities include system configuration, issue troubleshooting, data analysis, testing, production support, and creating mid-level reports. Working with senior HRIS analysts, the HR operations team, and partners, you will guide enhancements to provide HR technology solutions.

This is a hybrid role based in our Norfolk, VA office. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Be a primary technical contact for the Workday Performance module, while providing functional support for Core HCM, Compensation, Payroll, and Time/Absence domains.

  • Accomplish end-to-end system configuration to support global performance evaluation cycles.

  • Be a primary contact for performance workflow design and resolution of technical issues.

  • Deliver technical and user support for Workday, handling questions, troubleshooting, and resolving issues across supported modules.

  • Execute assigned production support tickets and project tasks with high accuracy and within target deadlines.

  • Maintain HCM production support processes, encompassing monitoring, detailed analysis, and issue resolution.

  • Define, refine, and maintain business process configurations.

  • Configure, schedule, and oversee automated mass actions and system alert notifications.

  • Participate in Workday's biannual feature update cycles.

  • Collaborate with the Workday Security team to configure and maintain domain and business process security policies.

  • Design and deploy Workday solutions tailored to meet functional requirements and improve operational efficiency.

  • Test, and implement new feature enhancements, analyzing impacts across Performance, Compensation, HCM, Benefits, Payroll, reporting, and integrations.

  • Audit and validate system data and reports to preserve data integrity and maintain internal control standards.

  • Review end-user data entry practices to identify process gaps and strengthen data governance controls.

  • Provide HRIS system maintenance, solution implementations, and module troubleshooting.

  • Partner with senior HRIS analysts to achieve shared goals, exchange technical knowledge, and foster skill growth.

  • Engage with HR partners to lead new module functionality, enhancements, and broader HCM programs.

  • Communicate technical insights, analytical findings to non-technical partners.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Sr. Manager of HRIS

  • Minimum 2 years of experience in an HRIS Analyst or functional HR systems role.

  • Minimum 2 years of hands-on experience configuring and maintaining Workday Performance Management.

  • Demonstrated experience writing and generating custom Workday reports.

  • Experience maintaining Workday business processes, security protocols, and system release updates.

  • Advanced proficiency in Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel (e.g., complex formulas, pivot tables).

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Hands-on experience managing Workday Time Tracking and Absence modules.

  • Familiarity with additional Workday modules and departments, such as Security, Integrations, and Prism Analytics.

We are looking for an International Payroll Specialist to join our team in London where you will be responsible for the end of end payroll process and work closely with HR, Global Mobility and Finance Department. This is a hybrid position based in London and includes regular attendance in the office each week per your departmental guidance. 

In this role you will be involved with developing controls and procedures to ensure that international payrolls are processed accurately and on time. You will ensure corresponding costs are properly accounted for, review and improve on controls and procedures to ensure voluntary and mandatory deductions are submitted compliantly by third party providers

  • Be the key contact person for external payroll providers, HR and Finance Department, responsible for the monthly end to end payroll process for the assigned countries.
  • Process  payroll information from Workday to Cloudpay (Integration validation and input information via template. 
  • Managing new joiners and terminations.
  • Review reports and liaise with internal partners to ensure the data/all changes are accurate and complete.
  • Ensure all employees are accurately recorded in Workday.
  • Post reconciliation, provide approval to third party payroll providers.
  • Total payroll (earnings, voluntary and mandatory deductions) will be provided to Finance and Newsroom Accountants for verification to General Ledger.

  • Respond to employee enquiries in a pro-active and courteous manner.
  • Managing the year end processes.
  • Managing risk within your role. Escalating when appropriate.
  • Provide support for audit enquiries.
  • Perform Adhoc reconciliation and research any discrepancies.

  • Extensive payroll experience, including previous experience on multi-country international payroll.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office software (Excel and Word).
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to present clear information, convey ideas, and prepare reports.
  • Ability to build and maintain strong relationships with internal departments, employees and external vendors through a collaborative and proactive approach.

And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

Since 1851, The New York Times' mission has been to seek the truth and help people understand the world. Whether it's bringing new truths to light through reporting, finding the perfect side dish to pair with dinner, or challenging yourself with the Sunday crossword, our mobile apps bring this mission right to our subscribers' hands. Our iOS apps are progressive and innovative. Our teams advocate for the best approach to building apps and look to the future by participating in Early Access Programs.

Our mobile teams sit at the intersection of our mission. We’re looking for iOS Engineers across several teams to help us take our apps to the next level. Some of the opportunities include:

  • Build engaging features to improve the reader experience in our flagship News app
  • Maximize subscriber value within our Growth Platform
  • Apply the latest trends in native development to create engaging experiences on our Games team
  • Help users discover and cook the world's best recipes on the Cooking team
  • Build the foundational technologies that empower all mobile teams by joining the App Platforms team

This is a hybrid role, based at our New York City headquarters, reporting to the Mobile Engineering Manager and collaborating with native iOS and Android engineers, QA, product, project, data, and design professionals.

  • Build and ship iOS features by enhancing existing code and creating new functionality from scratch
  • Write clean, maintainable code using Swift and SwiftUI
  • Mentor other iOS engineers and support their growth
  • Participate in code reviews and write unit tests; collaborate with QA to enable robust automated functional tests

  • Integrate with internal NY Times services and external third-party APIs
  • Stay current on iOS technologies, best practices, and AI tooling for mobile development
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of professional native iOS development experience using Swift
  • iOS design patterns, memory management, and multi-threading, such as SwiftUI, UIKit, Combine, MVVM/MVI, and CoreData/GRDB
  • Knowledge of Git/GitHub and best practices for peer code review
  • Experience with the mobile app release process, build tools, and continuous integration
  • Experience with Agile software development practices
  • Understanding of dependency injection

job.title: Journalist, Graphics Intensive
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The Graphics Intensive is a unique opportunity for mission-driven students and early career professionals with visual skills to work alongside journalists for a 12-week, full-time program. We seek individuals who bring their own inquisitive nature to develop creative approaches to storytelling, including those who may not have previously considered working in an independent newsroom. Prior journalism experience isn't required — many of our team members have embraced journalism's core fundamentals while at The Times — but you must have a desire to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

The Graphics desk at The New York Times is composed of visual journalists from diverse creative backgrounds, including architecture, cartography, and computer science. We cover all topics across the news cycle, motivated by a shared curiosity. This position is designed to cultivate skills and judgment in the creation of visual stories, including training and regular feedback from team members. Many of our projects are a collective effort, so you will work with a range of people and skill sets.

We are interested in applicants who want to learn how to apply creative and technical skills to a range of journalistic and storytelling assignments. Do you know how to write code to analyze data and produce visualizations? Are you a mapmaker or satellite imagery analyst? Do you use design and illustration to clearly convey complex information? These are the types of people that we seek to develop as potential graphics journalists.

The graphics intensive position is available throughout the year, including winter, spring, summer and fall openings. This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Under close guidance and supervision of a senior editor, produce visual and data-based multimedia journalism in response to breaking or as ongoing news coverage
  • Design and build graphics and other visual forms using web-based markup and coding languages with guidance from senior editors
  • Participate in training sessions
  • Collaborate with colleagues across the newsroom
  • Complete work assignments based on team needs and news demands
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a Deputy Editor, Graphics.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 1+ year of demonstrated strong performance toward an undergraduate degree, or relevant professional experience
  • 2+ years of experience working with graphics tools and software, like D3.js, R, JavaScript, Python, HTML/CSS, GIS, and 3-D modeling software
  • Interest in data visualization, cartography or other forms of visual journalism and the skills to start producing work in these areas
  • Skill in interface design and information graphic design
  • Experience with Adobe Creative Suite, especially Illustrator, or with design tools like Figma
  • A portfolio demonstrating experience with news graphics or interactive visualizations

Preferred Qualifications:

  • News or visual internships or equivalent experience
  • Curiosity and interest in the news, and in finding innovative approaches to telling stories
  • Experience working independently, meet deadlines, and being attentive to detail in an unpredictable news cycle and a high-pressure newsroom environment
  • Experience working collaboratively with members of a team with diverse creative skills
  • Available to work some nights, weekends and holidays as the news cycle demands
  • Experience multitasking, prioritizing, and balancing multiple projects in a dynamic work environment
  • Interest in professional growth and openness to professional feedback

Applications should include links to a portfolio or work samples to demonstrate your skills and experience. Please attach a cover letter describing your role in specific projects and which periods of time you will be available for the Graphics intensive. Your cover letter should include any periods when you will be able to work full time in New York, such as, “Available: Winter (2026-27), Spring, Summer or Fall” — or any combination of these.

job.title: Lead Product Designer, Search
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Mission Overview & Responsibilities: 

The New York Times is looking for a Lead Product Designer to help us design and prototype compelling A.I. experiences that help curious people understand and engage with the world.

We are looking for a Lead Product Designer to shape how readers search for information and understand the world through New York Times products — someone with a passion for design, journalism, and technology, as well as experience delivering A.I.-enabled consumer experiences at scale.

The New A.I. Products and Platforms mission is a critical, company-wide initiative tasked with building the next generation of A.I.-powered products to accelerate The New York Times's essential subscription strategy.

The Times operates in a hybrid model, with those based in NYC working in-office two days per week. We plan to speak with all candidates about where they're based and how they work in a hybrid environment.

As a Lead Product Designer, you'll identify opportunities to use A.I. to address news and information needs through our products' search feature. You'll use your interaction design and coded prototyping skills to build functional prototypes that gain alignment and drive work forward. You'll validate that these prototypes meet users' informational needs and align with our brand and journalistic standards. You'll collaborate with product managers, engineers, user researchers, and editorial partners to ship excellent and performant experiences to the world.

We value an environment of learning and collaboration. You'll play a leadership role to grow and support more junior design team members. You'll help promote a "make to think" design culture. You'll participate in regular design rituals to give and receive critique.

Responsibilities:

  • Create sketches, mockups, user journeys and other UX artifacts to rapidly explore a range of editorial and consumer scenarios and identify promising concepts.

  • Frame different approaches and describe tradeoffs.

  • Create functional coded prototypes of A.I.-powered experiences.

  • Give input to product strategy and concept development.

  • Lead conversations and help make decisions with the cross-functional team.

  • Contribute to the development of design standards and systems around A.I.

  • Represent your work to leadership within the company.

  • Improve the people and process around you by shaping and participating in team and Product Design rituals.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Deputy Head of Product Design.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of experience as a product designer, with recent experience creating coded prototypes using AI-enabled tools and workflows.

  • 7+ years of experience with interaction design and prototyping, including a portfolio showing a deep care for micro-interactions, motion, and accessibility best practices.

  • 7+ years of experience collaborating, building alignment and communicating clearly.

  • 7+ years of experience working with user research and data analysis teams to inform product and UX decisions.

  • 3+ years of creating functional prototypes.

  • Experience designing features that use generative A.I. to deliver end-user experiences.

  • Experience refining A.I.'s tone, format, and behavior to align with brand guidelines, product goals, and quality standards.

  • A portfolio of shipped work demonstrating experience working in 0-to-1 environments.

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Experience with media production workflows.

  • Experience designing or conceptualize large solutions while also aligning user and and business goals.

  • Experience balancing multiple goals to achieve an excellent outcome.

  • Strong ability to show design decisions and impact.

  • Experience working with senior stakeholders.

job.title: Local Investigations Fellow
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The Times is looking for reporters with a local story idea who want to investigate it under the editing guidance of Dean Baquet, The Times’s former executive editor, and a group of veteran investigative editors.

The goal of the Local Investigative Fellowship is to provide fellows the opportunity to learn the ways and means of investigative reporting from some of the best in the business. Our fellows will be based in the communities where they are reporting and make periodic trips to The Times’s offices for training and support.

This one year program is for reporters in local newsrooms or freelancers.

Responsibilities:

  • Spend a year producing signature investigative work focused on your state or region that will be published by The Times.
  • Under the guidance of Mr. Baquet and a handpicked group of veteran editors, you will receive the rare opportunity to learn the judgment, skills and techniques needed to excel at investigative journalism from the best in the business.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 to 5 years of professional experience as a reporter covering a beat for a local newspaper or local digital news outlet
  • You are an independent journalist or a journalist employed at a newsroom willing to provide a yearlong sabbatical

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant experience covering a beat and an idea for an investigative story that you have not had the time, resources or editing support to pursue
  • Ability to bring a new perspectives to investigative journalism

Learn more about the program here. 

To apply, upload a résumé, Cover Letter (as described below) and five clips in one attachment. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered. 

Your Cover Letter must include at least one story idea or pitch, but you may include multiple if you'd like. Please limit each story idea or pitch to 500 words. We are not looking for polished story ideas or pitches. Instead, your answers to these questions will help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  1. What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  2. Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  3. Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  4. What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  5. What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  6. Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Candidates should submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials application question below. Please ensure to include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

You may apply to the Local Investigations Fellowship once per calendar year. You may also apply for other newsroom opportunities, however separate applications must be submitted for each program.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor new work visas for the fellowship, but we may consider you if you have an existing work visa or a valid student visa that can be extended via Optional Practical Training

Applicants will be notified about their status on a rolling basis. 

Keep in mind that the fellowships are very competitive and generate a high level of interest. We won’t be able to accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. Nor will we acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

These positions are represented by the NewsGuild of NY

job.title: Manager, AI Strategy & Enablement
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Manager, AI Strategy & Enablement will help execute Marketing's AI strategy by turning approved priorities into tools and workflows that teams can use. You will identify opportunities where AI can improve work, recommend whether AI, process changes, or conventional software are the better approach, and build and configure solutions directly.

Quality, business impact, adoption, and time saved will determine how we measure success, not the number of tools used or launched.

You will sit on the Marketing team and report to the Managing Director, MarTech & AI. You will work across Marketing and regularly collaborate with Enterprise IT, Product, Data, Information Security, Legal, Privacy, and Procurement teams. This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can expect to come into the office three days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Identify opportunities to automate or improve Marketing work and translate ambiguous business problems into practical use cases.

  • Recommend whether AI, process changes, or conventional software are the best approach to each problem.

  • Lead assigned AI projects from discovery through rollout and ongoing improvement, managing requirements, timelines, owners, dependencies, risks, and success measures.

  • Build, configure, test, and improve AI tools and workflows using approved enterprise, low-code, and development tools.

  • Apply established standards for instructions, reference materials, data, permissions, testing, monitoring, human oversight, and failure handling.

  • Partner with technical teams when solutions require production engineering, data access, integrations, or complex system architecture.

  • Create role-specific documentation and enablement, track adoption and impact, and use the results to improve tools, workflows, and training.

  • Evaluate AI tools and vendors for business fit, quality, integration requirements, risk, and cost. Work with governance partners to ensure solutions meet established legal, privacy, security, data, and AI oversight requirements.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience in product or program management, digital transformation, marketing technology, automation, enablement, or a related field.

  • 2+ years of experience applying generative AI tools to business problems and workflows.

  • Working knowledge of AI agents and related concepts, with experience building or configuring agents, automations, retrieval systems, or AI-enabled workflows.

  • Experience leading cross-functional work from discovery and prototyping through implementation and adoption.

  • Experience translating ambiguous business problems into requirements, implementation plans, and measurable outcomes.

  • Experience evaluating AI quality, privacy, security, data governance, legal risk, and AI-human workflows, and explaining technical concepts to non-technical audiences.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience creating evaluation methods for AI outputs and using the results to improve instructions, context, tools, or workflow design.

  • Experience with AI-enabled productivity, knowledge, automation, and development tools such as Notion, Glean, Gemini Notebook, Make, Replit, or Cursor.

  • Experience in Marketing, Marketing Operations, or MarTech, with familiarity in vendor assessment, procurement, contracts, and enterprise technology governance.

job.title: Manager, Cloud Efficiency & Insights
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The Cloud Cost & Capacity Engineering (CCCE) team sits at the center of how we invest in and use the cloud at The New York Times. We help leaders understand where cloud spend is going, where to invest, and where to optimize without slowing teams down.

As Manager, CCCE, you will lead our FinOps function: how we forecast, govern, and communicate cloud costs and capacity across the company. You will work closely with engineering, product, finance, and data partners to turn complex usage and cost signals into clear guidance and decisions for senior leaders.

You will do this in a collaborative environment that values trade‑off discussions, clear storytelling, and recommendations over dashboards.

Responsibilities:

You will oversee the FinOps Function & Strategy

  • Define and evolve the FinOps/CCCE vision and how the team works, including scope, success metrics, and ways of working with engineering and finance.
  • Set and maintain the roadmap for how we forecast, track, and optimize cloud cost and capacity (e.g., forecasting maturity, Showback+, optimization programs, Cost to Serve) so we align it with company and platform strategy.
  • Act as the accountable owner for FinOps outcomes: forecast accuracy, predictability of spend, optimization impact, and the quality of leadership conversations.
  • Define how FinOps shows up in senior forums (e.g., quarterly business reviews, steering committees, CFO reviews) so cloud spend conversations focus on clear decisions and trade‑offs.

Tell the Story Behind the Numbers

  • Develop a clear point of view on cloud spend drivers, risks, and opportunities.
  • Translate complex usage, cost, and capacity signals (compute, data platforms, AI tooling, observability, CDN) into concise “so what?” narratives for executives, mission leads, and finance partners.
  • Lead the creation of clear executive materials (short slide narratives, single‑slide summaries, monthly/quarterly readouts) that explain where spend landed, what's driving it, and what leadership should do next.

Lead Forecasting & Investment Governance

  • Own the cloud forecasting approach: methodologies, assumptions, tolerance bands, and how we govern forecasts across missions and platforms.
  • Partner with Finance and mission leadership on annual and multi‑year cloud planning, tying forecasted spend directly to growth drivers, capacity assumptions, and planned investments (including AI and data platform initiatives).
  • Drive scenario modeling for new initiatives and evolving projects, offering a clear stance on likely cost impacts, trade‑offs, and budget needs.
  • Shape and participate in investment review processes (e.g., ROI gates, budget intake, contract renewals) with a clear, data‑backed point of view on what should be funded, re‑scoped, or delayed.
  • Design ways to track forecast variance and explain it in a way executives can trust and act on.

Drive Cross‑Functional Alignment & Accountability

  • Serve as the strategic liaison between Engineering, Product, Finance, and Procurement on cloud spend, savings, and growth.
  • Establish predictable cadences (e.g., monthly cost reviews, quarterly deep dives) that hold teams accountable.
  • Work closely with platform and capacity engineering partners so that FinOps insights translate into architectural decisions, guardrails, and optimization work.
  • Build shared mental models of “what's driving spend and why” so leadership conversations focus on trade‑offs and priorities.

Enablement, Tooling & Team Leadership

  • Directly manage and develop a cross‑functional CCCE team (analysts, capacity engineers, program partners), setting clear priorities, standards, and expectations.
  • Own and evolve the FinOps tool stack (e.g., FinOut and related data pipelines) to ensure you're delivering trusted, decision‑ready views.
  • Champion a culture of cost awareness and financial accountability across engineering through training, documentation, office hours, and embedded engagements.
  • Partner with data and platform teams on advanced modeling, while retaining end‑to‑end accountability for FinOps frameworks, insights, and communication.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Job Description

The New York Times' Marketing team is looking for a Manager, Event Campaign Production to be the operational engine of the event marketing campaign and production assets. You will oversee the daily creative workflow — from receiving direction from the Director to ensuring the Creative team delivers the right assets, on brief, on brand, and on time. They are the connective tissue between strategy and execution, translating campaign priorities into clear assignments and keeping every moving part accountable. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Director, Event Campaign Strategy and Production. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

About the Role

You will be hands-on, someone who excels at process and clarity. As the Manager, Event Campaign Production, you do not attend external or client-facing partner meetings independently, but operate with authority within the production workflow. You will direct creative output, managing vendor relationships daily, and overseeing the project management infrastructure that keeps the campaign on track.

Responsibilities:

  • Be the primary daily point of direction for the Creative team — assigning work, setting task-level priorities, and reviewing output against the brief and brand standards.
  • Translate campaign direction from the Director into clear, applicable briefs and assignments for the Creative team and external vendors.
  • Build the Marketing Notion Board — the central project management tool tracking all creative tasks, owners, statuses, and deadlines across every active campaign.
  • Manage the creative production timeline for each event, from initial brief through final asset delivery.
  • Coordinate daily workflow across internal creative teams, external vendors, and agency partners to keep production moving without bottlenecks.
  • Brief the NYT Communications Systems team on landing page and event page updates and manage the production timeline for those deliverables.
  • Be the primary daily contact for external creative vendors and production agencies, under the strategic direction of the Director and Production Lead.
  • Manage the review and approval workflow for all campaign assets — scheduling reviews, coordinating stakeholder feedback, and tracking revisions to completion.
  • Manage the timeline, asset coordination, and deliverable tracking for the post-event sizzle reel in collaboration with the Copywriter and Director.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • 3+ years of experience in creative production, project management, or campaign operations
  • 3+ years of experience coordinating review and approval workflows across multiple company partners
  • Track record managing complex multi-asset campaigns with many simultaneous moving parts
  • Experience briefing and managing external vendors and creative agencies daily
  • Process-minded with the instinct to create structure where it is missing
  • Working knowledge of the full marketing asset landscape: digital, print, video, social, email, and experiential

  • Exposure to live event or in-show production
  • Experience with events, media, or a marketing environment

Job Description

The New York Times advertising department is looking for a Manager of Measurement Analytics. As a strategic and data-driven individual, you will transform our vast data resources into compelling narratives. These narratives will explain the unique value of our platform and products, focused on campaign performance. You will be a central hub of knowledge, applying deep analysis of our audience and ad products to empower our Sales, Strategy and Product teams. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Senior Director, Measurements, Audience and Insights. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

You will evolve how we measure and increase media and creative across a portfolio of diverse clients. This collaborative and strategic role will work with top tier advertising clients. You will also work with Sales, Sales Planning, Ad Product, Audience Insights, and Strategy teams. The goal is to achieve results to promote relationships with marketers and increase ad revenue. Furthermore, You will work with our Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Product Marketing teams to create and validate measurement solutions supporting new lower funnel advertising solutions.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop expertise in the full suite of NYT research capabilities and measurement products that deliver important performance metrics across the full marketing funnel, to current and potential clients.
  • Lead meta-analyses that merge different first-party and third-party data sources to create unified, powerful narratives about The New York Times advertising platform and its audience.
  • Monitor key datasets to identify latest trends, package them into applicable insights, and communicate findings to support go-to-market strategies and client conversations.
  • Translate complex analytical findings into clear insights and present for both technical and non-technical partners, including senior leadership.
  • Perform ad hoc analysis using data tools and 3rd party datasets to answer critical business questions from Sales, Strategy, and Measurement teams.
  • Be an important consultative partner to Analytics teams, providing expert user feedback to guide the design of our first-party data dashboards and tools.
  • Contribute to the development of new measurement capabilities, metrics, and frameworks that measure the value of our evolving suite of advertising products.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in data analytics, media insights, ad tech, or a related quantitative field.
  • Experience fielding measurement analysis, and an understanding of solutions that help report on performance from Awareness to Conversions (e.g., Brand Lift studies, Content Evaluation, Sales Lift, Incrementality, MTA etc.) with vendors such as Kantar, Brand Metrics, ABCS Insights, Lucid, Nielsen etc.
  • Experience working with data clean room solutions (e.g., LiveRamp, Snowflake) for measurement and audience activation
  • Experience translating complex data into applicable insights for non-technical audiences.
  • Experience with SQL
  • Experience working directly with sales or client-facing teams.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in the digital advertising, publishing, or media industry

Job Description

The New York Times Advertising is hiring for a Programmatic Manager who will drive growth of NYT programmatic revenue. You will partner with our internal advertising teams and work with company leadership to support the ultimate goal of revenue growth.

 

About the Role

You will build programmatic data sources that increase revenue across the global NYT portfolio. Work with SSP partners and reporting platform vendors to ensure data is accurate and complete. You will be an internal expert on programmatic business trends, new technologies and best practices, and communicate them with sales and operations teams. Be a subject matter expert where you will manage projects and keep our team informed about how the industry is moving with regard to yield management and programmatic ad technology. This is a hybrid role, reporting to the VP Revenue Operations. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide weekly reporting to Advertising and Product leadership detailing Programmatic revenue tracking and insights.
  • Special focus on deploying and maintaining the best programmatic technology solutions by testing partner's header bidding, price rules, and deal capabilities.
  • Produce ongoing reporting to highlight revenue performance and areas of opportunity. Oversee end of month reporting for the global magazines programmatic operation, supporting end-of-month revenue reconciliation processes with our partners in Finance.
  • Be comfortable navigating matrixed business operations and combining data sets across time zones, devices, geos and inventory types.
  • Build internal partnerships as they relate to reporting on the programmatic line of business. Partner may include Finance, Billing, Revenue Operations, Programmatic Direct Support, and Sales.
  • Grow revenue by identifying opportunities, identifying issues using performance reporting data, and supporting the programmatic direct support team.
  • Partner with Business Analytics to provide accurate and frequent analysis of programmatic optimizations and opportunities.
  • Manage the daily programmatic platform management and operations, which include rule and deal optimizations, ad quality enforcement, and troubleshooting.
  • Manage our relationships with ad exchanges and supply side platforms (SSPs).
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • B.A. or B.S. in a quantitative or technical field (e.g., math's, engineering, statistics, finance, and economics)
  • 3+ years experience with ad tech based programmatic advertising platforms or publisher side
  • 3+ years of experience in programmatic yield management
  • Knowledge of reporting on programmatic advertising business activities including running reporting in SSP platforms such as Magnite, Index Exchange, Google ADX, Triplelift and others.
  • High proficiency in excel (can write advanced macros) and can summarize and manipulate large volumes of data.
  • Experience with reporting and data visualization tools such as; Google Ad Manager, Adswizz, Salesforce, Tableau, DoubleVerify or Google Data Studio

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience using Domo, Adomik, BigQuery, and SQL
  • Knowledgeable with ad tech landscape including survey, data collection, verification, viewability, real-time bidding, behavioral targeting, retargeting, cookie matching, and platforms beyond desktop (mobile, video, social)

job.title: Mid Atlantic Bureau Chief
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for an experienced journalist to helm the Mid-Atlantic Region as its bureau chief.

You understand the issues that are playing out across the coverage zone — which includes DC, Delaware, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, Ohio and Kentucky. You see news moments as opportunities to show off your expertise through clear and vivid writing.

As the authority on your region and a leader among peers, you will conceive and direct coverage plans and identify revelatory follows and deeper work on breaking news.

You will come brimming with ideas for engaging stories in many formats that help to explain and visualize the region for our readers, driving the conversation on topics of import to the region and the country.

You must be able to write quickly, clearly and accurately on deadline. Willingness to embrace a variety of formats and embracing new forms of storytelling is essential. You must be collaborative with colleagues.

This position may be based in-office in Washington D.C or remote in the region, pending business needs. In-office would include regular attendance in the office, four days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • You will drive a sense of what is coming next, both by watching themes in their region and a calendar of what news and events are coming.
  • You will oversee what is happening in your region on a constant basis, by scanning competition and guiding editors on the relevance of stories coming from their region.
  • You will be the Times' ambassador to your region or bureau; demonstrate and share your authority and expertise with colleagues looking for knowledge on your region. Be a leader to fellow regional reporters with questions.
  • You will cultivate a deep source network of authorities, politicians, sheriffs, union reps, cultural figures, law enforcement, agency representatives and beyond – positioning yourself to tap a source in a given news moment, from scoops to interviews and real-time updates. Discern which stories to write to further develop and engage your sources.
  • You will develop relationships with the stringers and freelancers in your region, adding new talent, assessing their performance in those assignments and identifying contributors for stories when they break.
  • You will brainstorm and develop ideas with colleagues in your region or on adjacent beats. Initiate collaborations when opportunities arise. Keep in regular contact with your colleagues.
  • Your daily life will range from breaking news stories to enterprise, accountability pieces and scoops, and embrace a variety of story formats and collaborations — that as a body of work help readers understand your region.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to an editor on the National Desk.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years' experience at a journalism or media company

  • You will monitor news and deliver a steady stream of story ideas that help explain the region.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Science desk of the New York Times is looking for a creative, energetic reporter to cover the world of space exploration. We’re looking for a heartbeat of stories that capture the wonder, the successes and failures, the big dreams and big personalities of the space world, whether at private space companies like SpaceX or in the orbit of NASA. The ideal candidate will be an accomplished multimedia journalist who can report and produce both text and video. You are adept at moving quickly on breaking news including launch coverage and other fixtures of the daily beat, but also able to identify stories with visual potential and eager to pursue a wide array of types of stories, including developing ambitious visual enterprise stories.

This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in a New York Times bureau four days each week. There may also be flexibility to work remotely per departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Pitch, report and produce news, enterprise and explanatory stories in both text and video, including on-camera reporting.

  • Contribute to live and developing-news coverage, including launches, mission milestones, anomalies and breaking developments.

  • Help to develop well-structured scripts for linear videos and combine text and visuals in multimedia formats.

  • Monitor wires, local and regional outlets, social media feeds and other sources for developing storylines and reporting opportunities that help explain the beat and advance ongoing storylines, keeping us ahead of national competitors.

  • Cultivate existing sources and develop new ones to land exclusive stories to cover this beat authoritatively.

  • Work collaboratively across the newsroom including with editors, video producers, video and photo editors and motion graphics colleagues to develop stories from pitch through publication.

  • Ensure visual accuracy, fair representation and rigorous fact-checking.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • This role reports to the Space Editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience covering space or science-related topics 

  • Experience covering complex subjects with elegance, sensitivity and fairness

  • A portfolio that demonstrates you are well-versed in a range of topics, and have a growing circle of sources across storylines

  • Demonstrated understanding of the video production process and creative instincts that go beyond traditional text formats

  • A willingness to be flexible as the news demands and the newsroom's needs evolve

  • An openness to trying new storytelling approaches, and a demonstrated ability to communicate clearly

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working as a reporter in high-pressure, deadline-driven newsrooms

  • Experience covering live events, launches, breaking news or rapidly developing stories

  • A strong understanding of Times style and standards

  • Proven experience leading field productions, writing scripts and crafting compelling narratives.

  • On-camera experience 

  • Proficient in Adobe Premiere Pro

  • Ability to shoot video

job.title: Newsroom Operations Manager
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Role

The New York Times is looking for an operational owner and highly organized self-starter to join our Newsroom Operations team as an Operations Manager. You will provide hands-on support and oversight of numerous logistics involved in the smooth daily operation of several assigned department(s) – News Platforms and Data, T Magazine and others.

We are looking for a quick learner and creative problem solver who is capable of handling the ever-changing demands of a fast-paced newsroom environment. You will guide tasks across the finish line for the desks in the newsroom. Key to this will be supporting members of our masthead and our journalists with a variety of daily responsibilities and short- and long-term projects. This includes being at the center of on-the-ground coordination of both in-office and offsite events, ensuring execution of on-site logistics and meals for key news coverage events, ensuring that administrative operational tasks are completed by internal deadlines so that operations on the desk run continually and uninterrupted. You will report directly to a Senior Manager of Newsroom Operations.

This role will be Hybrid, with a required in-office presence of 4 days a week. The schedule of these 4 days can fluctuate based on the needs of the desks, and during some peak news cycles, you may be required to be on site for 5 days during those weeks.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the primary, accountable operational contact for members of the masthead, department heads, and journalists, resolving operational roadblocks independently.
  • Responsible for on-site setup of various in-office events including mock elections, team all hands gatherings of staff from around the country, team lunches and various similar events, and also serving as a production coordinator for all such events. including live coverage setups, catering logistics, seating arrangements, and equipment deployment during breaking news cycles.
  • Oversee complex equipment setups for assigned desks, special coverage teams, and events, ensuring that all hardware, workstation, and specialized technical configurations in real-time to ensure journalists have fully functioning tools.
  • Work with the Newsroom Finance team to help create annual budgets and provide oversight of those budgets, including monthly closes, supplying additional financial reports.
  • Manage work and vacation schedules and maintain accurate time banks in Workday, and work with Payroll to verify time banks for transfers, departures, and annual payouts.
  • Manage a travel calendar and be sure anyone traveling on assignment is properly set up on the company's business travel accident insurance.
  • Approve expenses and travel costs in Workday.
  • Manage and process freelancers and vendors' payments, working with the Contracts Manager
  • Oversee accounts payable and accounts receivable for assigned departments
  • Work with HR and recruiting teams to assist with position management transactions
  • Facilitate Workday management, including onboarding new employees and helping them to get the training, equipment, and information they need
  • Keep staffing lists, org charts, and various email distribution lists up to date with any staffing changes in the department
  • Purchase supplies and equipment, keep track of all departmental expenses, including capital spending and outside vendor spending
  • Work in Zip for independent contractor onboarding, sourcing events and purchasing
  • Be available for a variety of tasks that come up, often urgently, including troubleshooting, assisting writers and editors,with on-site and off-site needs, etc.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in an operational or administrative role
  • Ability to drive projects forward
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Experience dealing with detailed and confidential and private concerns
  • You can work and keep an optimistic attitude while maintaining a keen sense of urgency
  • Be accessible after hours or on weekends when circumstances require
  • Impeccable organizational and time management skills; ability to multitask, prioritize and work under deadline pressure
  • Ability to work with all levels of management and staff and manage the needs of a team of 100+ employees and leaders

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of training and experience
  • Able to research resources, troubleshoot, and solve problems
  • Workday experience
